entry.summary: LiveSearch is a live benchmark for financial search agents in which each question is stored as executable verifier code over a professional financial data service, so the gold answer is computed at evaluation time rather than frozen at annotation time. This prevents answer staleness and data leakage, rewarding genuine search and analysis over memorized recall.

entry.title: Layerwise Repacking: Variable-Length Hybrid-Attention Training without an Extra Redistribution Pass

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Junwei Feng, Dongliang Huang, Xiaoling Zhou, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song

entry.summary: The paper addresses conflicting sequence-parallel group requirements across full-attention and sparse-attention layers in hybrid-attention training, where reusing wide SP16/32 groups for sparse layers incurs 7.0x slower cross-node communication. Layerwise Repacking keeps groups fixed while repacking per layer, avoiding a separate redistribution pass at full-sparse boundaries.

entry.title: When Connectivity Misleads: Guiding Agentic Search with Contrastive Evidence Paths

author.name: Junchen Li, Liang Xu, Rongzheng Wang, Qizhi Chen, Junhao Wen, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: This paper addresses a failure mode in search agents using cross-document graphs: highly connected distractor documents crowd out valuable evidence under graph-diffusion methods like Personalized PageRank. The proposed Contrastive Evidence Paths (CEP) scores candidates by their strongest individual evidence path rather than aggregate connectivity. This improves agentic search quality in multi-hop retrieval settings.

entry.title: REACH: An RL-based Hierarchical Humanoid Crawling Framework for Adaptable Confined Space Traversal

author.name: Shengzhang Xu, Yuning Guo, Weiyi Hu, Yifeng Xu, Zhongyu Li, He Kong

entry.summary: REACH is an RL-based hierarchical framework enabling a Unitree G1 humanoid to traverse height-constrained environments using both variable-height bipedal walking (1.27-0.50m) and crawling (0.50-0.20m). It uses a history-conditioned latent representation built from proprioception to handle contact-rich crawling dynamics. This extends humanoid locomotion beyond height-adjustable walking into genuinely confined spaces.

entry.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models

author.name: XinYu Piao, Myunghoon Ryu, Joongheon Kim, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: SKIM explores storing dialogue directly in a frozen language model's parameters without external memory: the model generates its own questions about each turn and writes question-keyed associations into its parameters via closed-form updates, enabling later retrieval by matching user questions. This tests whether conversation can be recalled purely in-parameter.

entry.title: AnalogScout: Simulation-Efficient PVT-Aware Analog Sizing with LLM Agents

author.name: Yichen Long, Keren Zhu

entry.summary: AnalogScout is an LLM-agent framework for analog circuit sizing that satisfies specifications across process, voltage, and temperature corners while minimizing expensive multi-corner SPICE simulations. It equips the agent with reusable verified designs and analytical sizing of sub-blocks to save simulation budget, combining circuit knowledge with search efficiency. This targets a real bottleneck in tape-out-ready analog design automation.

entry.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning

author.name: Daan van Hamersveld, Ewoud Smeur, Iurii Kriachko

entry.summary: The paper presents an RL-controlled fixed-wing interceptor drone aimed at autonomously engaging Shahed-type strike drones at higher altitudes and longer ranges than quadcopter interceptors can reach. The neural network controller maps filtered monocular vision inputs to control, addressing a capability gap where conventional air defense is too costly and manual operation remains standard.

entry.title: Counting the Bandages: On measuring the time that AI saves

author.name: Solomon Shalom Lijo

entry.summary: This position paper argues that measuring AI-assisted time savings with a stopwatch alone is misleading; time saved must be weighed against escaped defects the work lets through. It defines model-free quantities (time saved, excess escaped defects) and a break-even defect cost, and models checking behavior showing escaped-defect rates are largely independent of model quality until workers stop checking. It reframes AI productivity measurement as a counterfactual accounting problem rather than a raw speed metric.

entry.title: WAKMan: Workload Aware KVCache Manager

author.name: Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Vaibhavi Lokegaonkar, Sachin Mathew Varghese, Wesley Harris

entry.summary: WAKMan is a workload-aware KV cache eviction policy for LLM servers doing prefix caching, motivated by the finding that agentic steps return within seconds and favor recency while popular prompts and long conversations favor frequency. Across 20 request mixes the authors show no single policy is always best, with vLLM's default LRU suboptimal for mixed traffic. The system adapts eviction to observed workload composition to reduce latency and serving cost.

entry.title: AC-JEPA: Anchored Cross-Modal Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Visual-to-Symbolic Translation

author.name: Chaofei Hong, Ziyang Chen, Baochen Wang, Christina Yi Jin, Qing Zhang

entry.summary: AC-JEPA extends joint-embedding predictive architectures to cross-modal translation, using an SFT-compatible plug-in that predicts masked intermediate states in representation space to complement token-level supervision. This targets scientific domains where paired data are imperfect and clean pairs are costly, since token-level objectives are sensitive to target-sequence errors. The approach aims to capture shared semantics while preserving fine-grained target-modality structure.

entry.title: The View from Nowhere: Population-Centered Agent Evolution

author.name: Shuo Yan, Ningning Hou, Haoyu He, Haochen Pei, Shang Gao

entry.summary: This paper observes that self-improving agent evolution centered on selected parent agents leaves broader population capabilities underused, showing a substantial gap between population coverage and best-individual performance. It proposes a population-wide principle, the view from nowhere, where agents improve by interpreting their behavior through population-wide patterns of success, failure, and priors. This is relevant to open-ended agent self-improvement methods.

entry.title: Correctness Conditioning as Selection in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation

author.name: Yueer Pan, Yuexi Pan

entry.summary: The paper shows that restricting chain-of-thought faithfulness evaluation to correctly answered instances changes the measured population, formalizing this selection effect in a seven-variable structural causal model that separates difficulty confounding from shortcut-induced collider bias. A review of 18 papers plus experiments on arithmetic tasks reveals positive selection gaps across four sub-ceiling deployments.

entry.title: Aligning Institutional Power and Operational Ability

author.name: Andrea Marino, Giovanni Sileno, Thomas van Binsbergen, Tom van Engers

entry.summary: This paper proposes a formal framework for designing multi-agent AI systems in which norms and responsibilities are aligned with the actual operational ability to fulfil them. It uses process-oriented modelling and the concept of institutional power to detect incongruences such as unsatisfiable expectations or privilege escalation, and discusses repair strategies and the lifecycle of normative positions.

entry.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents

author.name: Ziyang Chen, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Task Advancement Memory (TAM) defines verified task progress as a state that reshapes remaining goals during long-horizon GUI workflows and, after each task, abstracts the interactions that produced verified results into reusable operations. This lets agents build on earlier achievements across applications while filtering out failed attempts. It targets the key problem of durable, reusable memory for GUI agents.

entry.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models

author.name: Chang Su, Bin Wu, Emine Yilmaz, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Using point-in-time language models trained on web snapshots from different years, the authors propose a temporal variability score based on the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models, probing how general versus domain-specific knowledge accumulates during pretraining. Evaluating six benchmarks across six open-source model families, they characterize how consistently knowledge is represented across years of web text. This offers a novel longitudinal lens on pretraining dynamics.

entry.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Ruijia Niu, Kaiwen Liu, Rose Yu, Kristina Klinkner

entry.summary: EMMA addresses adaptation of LLM agents to specialized domains via structured episodic memory at the context level, using multi-agent evolution with explicit update rules to reduce cross-task interference. It targets limitations of single-agent episodic memory and ill-scoped multi-agent evolution where backbone model preferences dictate system changes.

entry.title: DuplexTune: Coupled-State Replay for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Adaptation

author.name: Paul Raj, Simon Caldwell, Daniel Whitmore, Mutlu Mete

entry.summary: DuplexTune is a memory-efficient framework for adapting mixture-of-experts LLMs that replays coupled hidden states through pretrained attention and expert modules via trainable width bridges between two residual streams. On Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B with a single H800, it reports 38.8 GB peak memory versus 64.8 GB for SFT with checkpointing, higher throughput, and solid task scores (67.2% MMLU, 75.6% GSM8K).

entry.title: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates

author.name: Johannes K. Fichte, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: count-catcher is a tool that converts CPOG certificates produced by the exact model counter d4 into verified Lean theorems stating that a CNF formula has exactly N models over given variables, enabling verified counting of combinatorial objects. It performs forward and reverse checks in Lean, streaming a refutation through the standard LRAT checker and proving circuit validity within Lean. This contributes to the growing intersection of formal verification and combinatorial reasoning.

entry.title: HIDRA: Hierarchical Dual-Routing Attention for Replay-Free Lifelong Imitation Learning

author.name: Fanqi Yu, Matteo Tiezzi, Cigdem Beyan, Tommaso Apicella, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: HIDRA is a structured routing framework for replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning that decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement via hierarchical dual attention. It further stabilizes routing under representation drift using a key-based mechanism, addressing how expert selection degrades over sequential multimodal demonstration streams. This targets realistic robotic settings where storing past data is prohibited.

entry.title: Full Collapse Is Suboptimal: Controlled Partial Neural Collapse for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Hyeontaek Hwang, Cheonghwan Hur, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: The paper argues that forcing tail classes to fully undergo neural collapse toward an ETF target over-contracts their features and harms generalization in long-tailed recognition. It proposes a controlled partial collapse regime via a Class-Adaptive Sparse Activation classifier and an ETF-constrained adaptive margin loss, letting head classes collapse while tail classes keep within-class diversity. This offers a more nuanced theoretical account of neural collapse under imbalance.

entry.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search

author.name: Xiaohan Ye, Zihan Gong, Jingqian Zhao, Lianyu Du, Yunmeng Shu, Xu Chen, Zesheng Zhou, Renchun You, Bocheng Chen, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: This industrial technical report from Alibaba presents PailitaoMMSearch, a unified end-to-end multimodal search system that generates product semantic IDs directly from raw query images and free-form instructions, scaling across data, model, and serving dimensions. It removes scenario-specific couplings common in industrial generative retrieval deployments.

entry.title: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks

author.name: Victor Cook (LIRMM | ADAC), Gilles Sassatelli (LIRMM | ADAC), Thierry Gil (LIRMM), Mohamed Watfa (LIRMM | ADAC), Marina Reyboz (CEA-LETI)

entry.summary: The paper tackles catastrophic forgetting in equilibrium-propagation-trained Hopfield networks using an energy-based generative replay scheme where a single model serves as both classifier and sample generator. This eliminates external data buffers and architectural overhead required by standard experience replay, suiting edge hardware. It opens a largely unexplored continual-learning setting for biologically grounded learning rules.

entry.title: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: The paper proposes Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), an evaluation metric for articulated object manipulation that projects commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis, separating progress along the joint from off-constraint waste instead of relying on binary task success. On 74 simulated articulated objects, CRS exposes distinct signatures of transfer failures that binary success conflates, demonstrated with a door-trained policy opening drawers.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence

author.name: Yunuo Wang, Maoyuan Chen, Yuanjin Huang, Xing Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces matched same-class replacement controls to test whether audio-language models genuinely use local sound events: same-class edits preserve correct answers while different-class edits should change them if evidence is used. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, different-class replacements trigger 49.7 to 60.9 points more answer changes, providing a more rigorous causal attribution method for audio grounding.

entry.title: Smaller NLAs and probes read eval awareness as well as full size NLAs

author.name: Adam Bricknell

entry.summary: The author distills a Natural Language Autoencoder (NLA) reader trained on Qwen3.6-27B internals down to a 2B model, finding the distilled 2B NLA matches the 27B version at detecting agentic misalignment and eval-awareness signals (though not obscure facts), and that a cheap linear probe on 2B-generated labels matches a 27B NLA plus LLM judge on eval awareness at a tiny fraction of the cost. Results come from 76 technical tasks with injected cues, and generalization is not yet established.

entry.title: Generalized CliqueBots in Open-Source Game Theory

author.name: Arsen

entry.summary: This LessWrong post introduces an interface-relative notion of CliqueBots in open-source game theory, where programs cooperate only with similar programs as judged by a finite set of probing functions. The framework treats submitted programs as secondary to their interfaces, unifying existing bots in a coherent picture and providing a generative factory for new bot designs, with potential to characterize interface properties via bot properties.

entry.title: From Structural Feedback to Prompt Policies: Learning Faithful Text-to-Image Prompt Editors

author.name: Wentao Ye, Yali Ye, Zhiqing Xiao, Ru Peng, Xinpeng Ti, Liyao Li, Zhanming Shen, Peng Lu, Jie Zhang, Haobo Wang

entry.summary: StruPO is a structure-aware prompt editor for text-to-image systems that uses a calibrated scene graph as a shared representation for policy conditioning and image-grounded supervision, ensuring prompt edits preserve the user's requested scene. Deletion, reordering, and insertion operations provide token-aligned prompt modification, turning structural critique into a training signal for a reusable editing policy. The method must handle uncertain grounding and stochastic image generation during learning.

entry.title: LoRA on a Budget: Function-Aware Post-Hoc Compression for Adapter Fleets

author.name: Shenghui Li, Thiemo voigt

entry.summary: The paper formulates post-hoc LoRA compression as a two-level allocation problem: distributing rank across layers within each adapter and across adapters within a fleet under a shared budget. It introduces functional rank-distortion frontiers per adapter and fleet-level minimax allocation, arguing spectral redundancy alone does not determine tolerable compression. Given exact frontiers, the decomposition is shown to have desirable optimality properties.

entry.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yipeng Hao, Yuxuan Cai, Wenkai Ji, Jie Zhou, Liyang Yu, Qin Chen, Zhiguo Yan, Shulei Zheng, Liang He

entry.summary: DiscernMem is a training-free framework improving both memory quality and memory usage in LLM multi-agent systems. Defect-Aware Memory Refinement diagnoses flaws in stored advice by comparing executions with and without a memory and validates repairs against earlier tasks, while Boundary-Learning Meta-Memory records past uses and effects to learn when each memory should be applied or avoided. This addresses the real problem that stored memories can be wrong or misapplied.

entry.title: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds

author.name: Haoxi Li, Sikai Bai, Jianfei Ma, Qinglin Hou, Xiaocheng Lu, Tao Han, Jie Zhang, Song Guo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Dwell, a model-based RL framework that recasts a pretrained vision-language model as a recurrent latent transition operator able to predict the consequences of its actions in latent space. This enables learning from online interaction while avoiding expensive continual updates of large pretrained models, leveraging internalized world knowledge for policy improvement.

entry.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

author.name: Anouar Imel, Imad Charradi, Abderrahman Sghir, Khalil El Khammar

entry.summary: CrossProfile is a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates (480 tasks) crossing the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts while holding text fixed, designed to test what LLM group-discussion memory should retain. Across Qwen2.5, Llama-3.1, and DeepSeek models, both natural heuristics (keep rarest claims, keep relevant claims) fail predictably: rarity selection is confounded and relevance selection readmits on-topic decoys. The work isolates a subtle failure mode in compressed group memory.

entry.title: Generation and Verification: Human-Agent Collaboration for Safety-Critical Automotive Software Engineering

author.name: Elizaveta Zinovyeva, Aiham Taleb, Nikita Kozodoi, Daniel Schleicher, Amir Mahdi Namazi, Martin Kraus, Levent Kent, Brian Jensen

entry.summary: The paper presents a coding assistant for safety-critical automotive C/C++ that exposes generate, edit, and verify tools to developers via the Model Context Protocol, emphasizing verification against standards like MISRA and AUTOSAR. It addresses the narrow-domain challenge of layered architectures and embedded constraints underrepresented in general LLM training data.

entry.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning

author.name: Johnny Yu, Cyril Gorlla

entry.summary: The paper presents Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe in which the student itself identifies and critiques its first incorrect reasoning step and training resumes from a truncated trajectory, reducing the dependence of on-policy distillation on a strong external teacher or full reference solutions. It targets multi-step financial reasoning under data-residency constraints favoring small open-weight models.

entry.title: Balanced State Subspaces for Mamba-2 State Compression

author.name: Shang Tingyu, Cao Wenfei

entry.summary: The paper analyzes trained Mamba-2 states and finds that while energy is nearly rank-one, the output actually reads content from a low-dimensional subspace misaligned with the state's coordinates, meaning coordinate-wise compression scores miss the directions that matter. It proposes compression targeting the write-read subspace with balanced state subspaces. This improves memory and bandwidth efficiency for Mamba-2 decoding.

entry.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu, Zhe Jiang, Xin Si, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: CoS-VQ is a vector quantization method for low-bit LLM weight compression that preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and a shared scale across positions. It tackles scale-induced coupling, where optimal scales depend on the full codeword combination and alter candidate rankings, by collecting candidates at multiple levels before committing. This aims to keep VQ lookup simple while recovering accuracy.

entry.title: OA-RAG: Ontology-based Agentic RAG for Faithful LLM Reasoning

author.name: Hui Yang, Jiaoyan Chen, Yongsheng Gao

entry.summary: OA-RAG integrates formal reasoning over domain ontologies with LLM reasoning inside an agentic RAG loop, using both logical structure and informal annotations to ground answers in established knowledge. For each answer it reports the ontology observations used as evidence along with a model-assessed grounding level, targeting hallucination reduction in domains like biomedicine where faithfulness is critical. It addresses RAG's usual neglect of logical relationships between retrieved facts.

entry.title: MedConstBench: Benchmarking How Constitutions Steer LLMs in Medical Ethics

author.name: Yibo Yang, Zerui Huang, Haomiao Yang, Zixia Wang

entry.summary: MedConstBench is a medical-ethics benchmark that treats a model's deployment constitution as a controlled variable rather than a fixed property, organized around Beauchamp's four bioethical principles. It evaluates how different constitutions reshape trade-offs between competing ethical values in locally deployed medical LLMs. This addresses a gap where most work focuses on factual correctness rather than ethical value conflicts.

entry.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations

author.name: Qiming Shi, Yikun Li, Beidi Luan, Rui Sun, Yan Ma, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: AutoVend is a benchmark in which an LLM agent manages 20 vending machines across five site types through a web-based operating interface over 180 simulated days, with a data-grounded simulator including shared warehouse, procurement lead times, paid replenishment, inventory expiration, and recurring costs. It evaluates whether online decisions translate into sustained economic returns in online-to-offline commerce.

entry.title: Grounding LLM Agents in Business Processes: Process-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Reliable Multi-Step Service Invocation

author.name: Saiful Khan, Afrah Farea

entry.summary: The authors build typed property graphs that combine OData API metadata with BPMN reference business processes so that LLM agents can select endpoints respecting process order, schema keys, and coded values. A hybrid retriever uses dense embeddings plus process-edge traversal to fetch subsequent endpoints. Evaluation on 42 enterprise services with process-chain ground truth shows improvements, especially for low lexical overlap queries.

entry.title: Curriculum-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Far-Range Rocket Landing

author.name: Atin Chowdhury, Piyush Joshi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a curriculum-driven deep RL framework for vertical rocket landing covering both far-range navigation and precision landing, using a three-stage curriculum with critic warm-up to handle nonlinear dynamics and stringent precision requirements. It aims to improve on flat training paradigms with overly simplified initial conditions common in prior RL work on this task.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Still Need a Debugger? Frontier-Model-Based Fault Localization at the Accuracy Ceiling

author.name: Christoph Daxerer, Johann Glock, Christian Macho, Rudolf Ramler, Martin Pinzger, Josef Pichler

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates how accurately coding agents based on GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-6-Luna, and Qwen 3.8 localize seeded single-line faults with and without interactive debugger assistance, across 610 faults in 144 programs and five behavior-preserving transformation recipes. It asks whether debugger tooling still improves localization now that frontier models reason well from static code alone.

entry.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization

author.name: Ege Demirci, Ambuj Singh

entry.summary: Concorde is an energy-based framework for link prediction in sparse graphs that decomposes link likelihood into three decoupled branches: a parameter-free spectral anchor, a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable product of hyperbolic and spherical spaces regularized by a feature-aware Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy, and a continuous vector field for non-local structural alignment. This addresses spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators. It targets a long-standing weakness of geometric methods on sparse graphs.

entry.title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation

author.name: Yijing Lin, Zhendong Mao, Mengqi Huang, Yuxin Wang, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: FrameForge repurposes pretrained video foundation models for unified conditional image generation by modeling condition-target relationships as input-adaptive virtual temporal relations rather than fixed temporal positions. It combines a Mixture of Temporal relations module with complementary mechanisms to capture these relations. This cleverly exploits the temporal transformation priors video models already encode.

entry.title: TOPS: Reshaping Flow Source and Transport for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation

author.name: Tuo An, Chuhao Zhou, Jiahua Dong, Jingliang Li, Jiaqi Bai, Jindou Jia, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: TOPS adapts the flow source prior and interpolation schedule per task for language-conditioned multi-task robot manipulation, without changing network architecture. It builds multimodal task sources by reverse-mapping expert action sequences so language instructions select where generation begins, and adjusts transport speed based on source-target covariance mismatch. This addresses the limits of shared Gaussian priors and linear transport paths in flow-based policies.

entry.title: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Ziluowen Luo, Ruochen Liu, Jun Yin, Hao Yan, Zhengxuan Hu, Xinze Shi, Chaozhuo Li, Chengqi Zhang, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: The authors observe that sparse autoencoder features from pretrained language models have human-interpretable annotations, so their indices can serve as reusable semantic ID vocabularies for generative recommendation. They address challenges of preserving item distinctions under compact token budgets and extending interpretability to retrieval, avoiding costly per-domain vocabulary fitting.

entry.title: GCSR-OCC: Geometry Calibration and Semantic Routing for Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Bohua Wang, Congyang Zhao, Tianxiong Lv, Chenxu Zhao, He Zheng, Hangqi Fan, Leigang Luo, Zhihao Liao, Yihong Guo, Yang Cai

entry.summary: GCSR-OCC improves open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction from a single RGB image by calibrating Gaussian geometry before voxel conversion and routing semantics with multi-mode query conditioning. Its evidence-conserving Gaussian-to-occupancy operator addresses scale inflation, overlap distortion, and semantic mixing in 3D Gaussian pipelines. The target application is indoor scene understanding, relevant to robotics and AR.

entry.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: This paper studies failure diagnosis for bimanual robot manipulation, where failure types differ fundamentally from the single-arm perturbation cases common in VLM-based diagnoser benchmarks. Using a simulated bimanual tool-use task with ground-truth failure causes, it systematically measures which sensing channels, such as a tool hand, one arm, or both arms, permit distinguishing failures like tool slip, mistimed gestures, and compound failures.

entry.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops

author.name: Aakash Sarkar, Ananya Mukherjee, Motoshige Sato

entry.summary: The authors formalize relational reasoning in attention-style architectures using lattice gauge theory, showing that under per-entity rotational freedom (gauge symmetry), relations sharing no cycle cannot interact, the only gauge-invariant triangle score is a Wilson loop of the composed holonomy, and the only equivariant edge update takes a specific conjugation form. This yields a principled derivation of edge attention scored by Wilson loops for composed-relation verification.

entry.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert's Interconnects essay uses the launch of Artificial Analysis v5 to examine the fundamental paradox of AI benchmarking: aggregate scores must collapse to a single number to be useful, yet every aggregation method involves trade-offs that can misrepresent frontier models. He argues independent evaluation is under-appreciated in difficulty, especially when fast AI progress makes benchmarks outdated within months.

entry.title: Verifiable Efficiency Limits of Innate LLM Planning in Sliding Puzzles

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Charles Ling

entry.summary: The paper isolates innate LLM planning by requiring complete plans in a single response without tools or execution feedback, on 4x4 sliding puzzles with certified optima. It proposes a decomposable verifiable metric, SPE = R x Q x E, capturing execution reliability, planning coordination, and action economy, evaluated over 8,400 full-plan outputs from seven model conditions. Trajectory replay and certified optima allow objective measurement of where unaided planning breaks down.

entry.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training

author.name: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang, Yike Yang, Tao Ren, Wayne Xin Zhao, Feng Chang, Jujie He, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: WorkFactory is a scalable framework that converts professional intents into coherent, executable tasks for supervised agent training, using an information support graph to represent dependencies and locations of required information, plus probe executions to detect and repair support failures. The authors construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use them to generate expert demonstrations.

entry.title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties

author.name: John M. Aiken, William Gilpin, Thorsten W. Becker

entry.summary: This paper trains a self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged physical properties across roughly 237,000 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder featuring heteroscedastic Gaussian decoding and learnable mask tokens. The key finding is that expert-assigned lithological labels do not improve prediction of marine sediment properties, as embeddings already separate lithologies. This challenges assumptions about the value of expert labels in scientific ML pipelines.

entry.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding

author.name: Koji Hashimoto, Tadahiro Taniguchi

entry.summary: This theoretical paper applies collective predictive coding, a theory of language and symbol emergence, to physics, modeling each atom as an agent predicting others' behavior so that macroscopic order parameters emerge analogously to how language emerges from communication. It demonstrates the framework on 2D ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a competing-stripe model, and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, recovering proper order parameters. This is an interdisciplinary bridge between cognitive theories of emergence and statistical mechanics.

entry.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction

author.name: Neil Chen, Adrian Serapio, Hanxue Gu, Evan Lee, Kang Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: CohortFlow is an agent for clinical cohort curation that represents natural-language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification, reconciled against a persistent execution graph so only affected computations are invalidated. On 100 clinical-trial scenarios with 126 correction turns, localized steering with an 8B model achieves 77.0% requirement micro-F1 versus 76.4% for full regeneration. The contribution is a practical architecture for incremental, steerable agent workflows in a clinical setting.

entry.title: Plenty of Room in the Middle: Revealing Opportunities on a GPU Cluster via Fine-Grained Monitoring

author.name: Andrew Sheinberg, Samyak Gupta, Kai Li

entry.summary: The authors build a lightweight monitoring tool using Nvidia's DCGM library to capture GPU-level compute utilization at 100 ms intervals on an 89-node, 319-GPU university research cluster, an order of magnitude finer than typical monitoring. The measurement study reveals underutilization invisible to second- or minute-level monitoring, identifying concrete opportunities to improve GPU utilization and reduce queueing. It demonstrates that fine-grained telemetry exposes headroom that job-level scheduling data misses.

entry.title: ATEMPO: Amortized Transfer Entropy Model Per-lag Over-Time

author.name: Emma Andrews, Konstantinos Kontras, Keane Ong, Maarten De Vos, Gianmarco Mengaldo

entry.summary: ATEMPO is a diffusion-based estimator of transfer entropy amortized over lags and time, designed to recover the specific delays at which one time series informs another without the separate fits per source depth and local windows required by existing estimators. Because informative delays can be narrow, fixed input windows can obscure temporal structure. The method is relevant to scientific applications like physiological signal analysis.

entry.title: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind

author.name: Ziqi Liao, Jiaqi Shen, Yiming Na, Kedi Lyu, Shao-Yuan Lo, Hongxia Xie

entry.summary: The paper identifies evidence calibration as a key failure mode in multimodal theory-of-mind models: LLM-based and Bayesian approaches leak agent-inaccessible events into belief inference, causing perspective leakage and source confusion. It proposes perspective-bounded evidence calibration that explicitly distinguishes objective events from agent-admissible evidence when evaluating mental-state hypotheses.

entry.title: Guided-RLVR: Guided Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Bo Yang, Zishuai Zhang, Weihua Li, Qinnan Zhang, Sijia Wen, Hainan Zhang

entry.summary: Guided-RLVR augments reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by adding a lightweight controller that injects semantically meaningful steering tokens at critical reasoning steps, encouraging exploration of multiple reasoning perspectives. This counters the known collapse of RLVR rollouts onto narrow trajectory sets, broadening the explored reasoning space for math and code tasks.

entry.title: RPSD: Retrieval-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Optimal Transport

author.name: Dongyue Li, Zebang Cheng, Zhongyi Deng, Hongboxu, Yi Bin, Fei Ma

entry.summary: For LLM-based sequential recommendation post-trained with RL such as GRPO, the authors identify two failures: credit-blind optimization (sequence-level rewards shared across tokens) and collaborative-blind supervision (signals from single users). RPSD introduces on-policy self-distillation with a privileged teacher and optimal transport alignment to address both. This is a targeted improvement to RL post-training for generative recommenders.

entry.title: ReForest: Interpretability Meets Reasoning in Isolation Forest

author.name: Juyoung Seo, Geonwoo Bang, Dongho Kim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: ReForest bridges the semantic gap in Isolation Forest anomaly detection by converting decision paths into natural-language explanations that an LLM uses to refine detection via an uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble. This keeps the statistical efficiency of Isolation Forest while adding contextual, semantic reasoning only where needed. It avoids the prohibitive cost of running LLMs over every data point.

entry.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry

author.name: Wenqing Peng, Michael Boy, Zhi-Song Liu

entry.summary: KPPax is a preprocessor that translates atmospheric chemistry mechanisms written in the widely used KPP language into differentiable, JIT-compiled, vectorizable JAX code, evaluating rate laws with sparse log-space operations and integrating stiff systems with diffrax adjoint solvers. This enables end-to-end differentiable and ML-coupled atmospheric chemistry simulation without hand-derived adjoints. It lowers a real infrastructure barrier between atmospheric science and machine learning.

entry.title: ReCoPII: A Relation-Grounded Framework for Building Contextual PII Masking Datasets

author.name: Taehwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces ReCoPII, a framework for generating contextual PII masking training data without real personal data, deriving MASK/KEEP labels from planned entity relations rather than author-based heuristics. It uses ontology-constrained relation planning, LLM sentence generation with placeholders, and a separate LLM verifier, evaluated on Korean documents across six domains.

entry.title: Can AI Guide Testing Without Generating Tests? A Comparative Study of AI-Assisted Unit Testing

author.name: Zihan Fang, Ron Asoulin-Handelman, Helen Wu, Yu Huang, Gina R. Bai

entry.summary: This classroom study introduces TestCompass, a generative AI tutor that gives novices targeted feedback on weaknesses in their unit-test suites without writing executable tests for them. The work examines whether AI can support students in developing testing skills rather than doing the testing for them, addressing concerns that novices accept AI-generated tests uncritically. It contributes to the emerging area of pedagogy-preserving AI assistance.

entry.title: CrowdCC: Jointly Benchmarking Corruption Robustness and Deployment Quantization in Crowd Counting

author.name: S Mahmudul Hasan, Lu Peng

entry.summary: CrowdCC is a benchmark that jointly evaluates corruption robustness and deployment quantization for crowd counting, spanning 23 corruptions at three severities, four datasets, and 26 models quantized at FP32, FP16, and INT8 with TensorRT, plus throughput and energy measurements on Jetson Orin NX hardware. This reveals interaction effects between input degradation and model compression that are missed when the two are evaluated separately. It provides a realistic deployment-oriented evaluation protocol for edge vision models.

entry.title: FIDES-Live: Evaluating Behavioral Concordance in Sequential Trading Agents

author.name: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan

entry.summary: FIDES-Live extends an earlier FIDES protocol to audit whether sequential trading agents behave consistently across decisions, orders, executions, ledgers, and reports, not just whether final portfolio values are correct. It separates decision validity, commitment adherence, reconciliation, and receipt-grounded reporting, and demonstrates the audit on 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds plus an equity pilot with real market data. This addresses reliability of autonomous agents in consequential financial settings.

entry.title: A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models

author.name: Senthil Rajasekaran, Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou

entry.summary: The paper adds quantitative rigor to LLM conformity studies by repeatedly sampling a single question to obtain answer distributions before and after exposure to manufactured consensus, then comparing distributions rather than point answers. Experiments confirm frontier LLMs conform, extending prior binary findings with distribution-level measures of conformity strength. This is relevant to understanding social bias and robustness in deployed LLMs.

entry.title: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution

author.name: Zihan Zhang, Zeyu Wu, Xin Zhang, Mingyu Luo, Haohui Que, Tong Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a traceable framework for self-driving laboratories with four components: LAM, a measurement-conditioned policy extending vision-language-action models to emit both robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls; OpenSDL, an execution substrate; Safe-SDL for safe execution; and L3-Bench, a benchmark. It aims to unify flexible robot control with instrument APIs in closed-loop lab automation.

entry.title: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding

author.name: Bingchao Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Chengyu Wang, Jun Huang, Jie Yang, Wei Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: AdaGround is a training-free framework for GUI grounding on high-resolution screens that adapts zoom magnification and depth to the model's own target-size estimates and uses a Yes/No click verifier to accept, reject, or re-do zooms. It also introduces existence queries to decide when to abstain.

entry.title: MRI-to-CT Translation of Spinal Images via Anatomy-Guided Pseudo-Pairing and Adversarial Diffusion

author.name: Eduardo Nieto, Ibai Genua, Davide Scorza, Karen L\'opez-Linares

entry.summary: The paper proposes a three-stage pipeline for synthesizing spinal CT from MRI: anatomy-guided pseudo-pairing of unpaired MRI and CT slices via segmentation and registration, adversarial diffusion translation, and 3D volume assembly with refinement. The goal is to reduce radiation exposure and streamline preoperative spine surgery planning. It combines several established components into a clinically motivated system.

entry.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction

author.name: Yuzhi Yang, Brahim Mefgouda, Hang Zou, Lina Bariah, Anis Bara, Yuhuan Lu, Hao Zhang, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: The authors apply a joint-embedding predictive architecture to MIMO-OFDM channel state information reconstruction from sparse pilots, predicting in a latent propagation-field domain rather than directly on raw phase-sensitive CSI coefficients. This exploits spatial, temporal, and frequency correlations of wireless channels for more robust estimation under fading, mobility, and scattering. It transfers a representation-learning idea from vision into communications.

entry.title: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yuxi Huang, Silin Zhou, Chenhao Wang, Zihan Li, Gangming Guo, Pei Ke, Shen Gao, Shuo Shang

entry.summary: REGER is a generative recommendation framework that explicitly incorporates inter-item semantic and collaborative relations into semantic ID pretraining, history encoding, and SID generation, addressing the limitation that randomly initialized SID embeddings and from-scratch training inherit item semantics only implicitly. The framework pretrains representations so that relations among items are modeled directly rather than through token-level attention alone.

entry.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction

author.name: Prakhar Kaushik, Soumava Paul, Alan Yuille

entry.summary: The paper proposes Hexels, planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field, as compact primitives for novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction, exploiting locally planar regions with fewer, larger elements. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR by 4.53-7.38 dB over memory-matched 2D Gaussian splatting while using less training VRAM.

entry.title: Anthropic Files Its S-1

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed close reading of Anthropic's S-1 IPO filing, recapping the company's finances and extracting top takeaways, including how briefly and passively existential risk is treated, the claim that pacing the frontier requires industry-wide cooperation, and the framing of the core business plan. It applies the same RTFB treatment the author gives to model cards.

entry.title: Spiking Neural Networks Are Harder to Steal: A Benchmark Study of Model Stealing Attacks

author.name: Ayana Moshruba, Maryam Parsa

entry.summary: This benchmark study examines whether model stealing attacks, well characterized for conventional ANNs, transfer to spiking neural networks whose sparse, time-dependent spike outputs complicate surrogate-model construction. The authors systematically evaluate MSA approaches against SNN targets to characterize how temporal dynamics affect extraction attacks. The finding that SNNs are harder to steal has implications for deploying neuromorphic models behind query APIs.

entry.title: Follow the Herd: A Data-Driven Approach for Actionable Recourse

author.name: Nishtha Madaan, Srikanta Bedathur

entry.summary: DDAR provides actionable recourse for machine learning decisions without requiring costly human supervision to hand-design action cost functions. It exploits the idea that highly likely trajectories in historical user data imply lower costs, building a dynamics model from that data to search for low-cost actions achieving desired outcomes. This improves the practicality of recourse in high-stakes decision systems.

entry.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents

author.name: Delin Wang, Sinuo Wang, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Qiming Shi, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: RubricAtlas derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports within a research type and organizes binary checkpoints around recurring analytical questions, giving related tasks a shared evaluation standard for deep research agents. This goes beyond query-specific rubrics and task-level checklists that leave the overall analytical structure underexamined.

entry.title: Task-Utility IQA: Rethinking Image Quality Assessment in Embodied Tasks

author.name: Jirong Zha, Yanwei Liao, Yemin Wang, Xiangmin Yi, Siqi Peng, Yingfeng Chen, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues that image quality assessment for embodied agents should shift from task-agnostic score regression toward goal-conditioned judgment reflecting whether an image supports the task at hand. It proposes an MLLM-based IQA agent framework that reasons about task requirements, grounds quality evidence, and produces decision-facing assessments, illustrated with a compact VisDrone study. This reframing is relevant to embodied and interactive imaging pipelines.

entry.title: Pricing Cross-Bank Context in Federated Anti-Money Laundering

author.name: Lidia Losavio, Dario Fenoglio, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich

entry.summary: This work tackles graph-based anti-money laundering when transaction graphs are split across banks, using transactions recorded by both endpoint banks to approximate remote account states locally for multi-layer GNN computation. It then introduces a disclosure ladder that prices the privacy-utility tradeoff of sharing additional cross-bank context, from remote transaction counts to counterparty GNN states.

entry.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data

author.name: Md Zahangir Alom, Quynh T. Tran, Breuer Alexandar, Brent A. Orr

entry.summary: This paper proposes an end-to-end OOD detection framework for DNA methylation-based tumor classification, extracting bottleneck feature vectors from DNN classifiers trained on sarcoma and brain tumor cohorts and comparing five OOD methods including 1D-SSA, KNN, and Mahalanobis distance. The goal is to prevent faulty predictions for tumor types absent from the training distribution, a real clinical safety concern. It demonstrates OOD detection in a high-stakes genomic diagnostic setting.

entry.title: ProCerDCL: Query-Efficient Black-Box Probabilistic Verification of Deep Learning Compiler Optimization

author.name: Zexin Li, Weibo Zhang, Linyi Li, Arvind Easwaran, Simin Chen

entry.summary: ProCerDCL is a query-efficient framework for black-box probabilistic verification of deep learning compiler optimizations, assessing whether a property's violation probability falls below a threshold with bounded error probabilities and a three-valued verdict. It uses a single sequential test instead of a family of interval tests, improving efficiency under a user-specified separation margin. This targets reliability of optimized neural network compilation.

entry.title: LearnPrunerV2: Learnable Progressive Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rinyoichi Takezoe, Yaqian Li, Weiren Wang, Zihao Bo, Huihong Shi, Anzhou Hou, Mo Guang, Jiale Yan, Kaiwen Long

entry.summary: LearnPrunerV2 addresses inefficient visual token processing in VLMs by extending a prior two-stage heuristic pruning framework into a fully learnable architecture. It tackles unreliable pruning criteria (attention biases, query-agnostic designs) and rigid pruning schedules that ignore how token redundancy evolves across model depth.

entry.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices

author.name: Kailai Feng, Haoxiang Rao, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Junsong Li, Yang Pan, Chengkun Cai, Jagmohan Chauhan

entry.summary: MoI-Bench is a benchmark grounded in real mobile user needs for on-device image generation and editing, comprising 64 subtasks and 1150 samples defined by 16 operations crossed with eight visual target categories. It also proposes MoI-Eval with task-specific criteria covering instruction following and other axes to quantify capability gaps between on-device and server-side image models.

entry.title: Ontology-guided multi-agent reasoning for explainable differential diagnosis

author.name: Roxana Ramona Szomiu, George Ursu, Adrian Groza

entry.summary: The paper proposes an ontology-guided multi-agent LLM system for differential diagnosis that structures patient case descriptions and grounds reasoning in clinical evidence to improve explainability. It targets the problem that LLMs achieve competitive medical benchmark scores yet often rely on pattern recognition rather than evidence, producing opaque conclusions clinicians cannot audit. Ontology structure constrains and exposes the reasoning used per recommendation.

entry.title: Proactive Memory for Event-Driven LLM Agents

author.name: Jinyang Li, Zichuan Fu, Xian Wu, Wenlin Zhang, Yimin Deng, Kaifeng Guo, Guojing Li, Junjia QI, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: ProactMem organizes agent history into recent events, temporal trajectories, and behavioral regularities, validating trajectory facts against source events and assessing regularities via historical replay before matching them to current conditions. The paper also contributes ProactiveStream, a longitudinal benchmark spanning three application scopes for proactive event-driven agents.

entry.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution

author.name: Daniel Ber\'anek

entry.summary: The paper proposes an authorization boundary for agentic entity resolution separating evidence available for reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize persistent identity-changing graph mutations. A domain-governed constraint-binding function maps failure distinctions to identity-preserving constraints, and a two-phase supervisor permits commits only when claim-specific authorization-eligible evidence supports all requirements. This guards against self-confirming erroneous hypotheses in iterative agent workflows.

entry.title: Dream-COP: Guiding Algorithm Discovery for Combinatorial Optimization Problems in an Experience World

author.name: Kuan Xu, Jianming Wang, Ni Zhang, Yaoxin Wu, Yong Wang, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: Dream-COP organizes LLM-driven algorithm discovery for combinatorial optimization around replaying past search trajectories stored in an experience world. A policy agent learns executable policies by dreaming over this experience to guide a discovery agent that generates and refines COP programs. The approach aims to make better use of limited search budgets.

entry.title: Dense Representation Learning and Differentiable Shape Modeling for Spine Landmark Detection

author.name: Augustin Daridon, Sofiane Sifaoui, Ayman Assi, Mohamad Karam, Wafa Skalli, Elsa Angelini, Loic Le Folgoc

entry.summary: The paper reframes anatomical landmark detection in spinal X-rays as pixel-level contrastive representation learning matching dense pixel embeddings to landmark prototypes, yielding more discriminative heatmaps than standard heatmap regression even with a U-Net backbone. Learnable shape priors over global landmark configurations resolve location ambiguities.

entry.title: Learning Human Sports Motion Feasibility via Quantile Regression on Tracking Data

author.name: Marc Guti\'errez-P\'erez, Antonio Agudo

entry.summary: The paper casts time-to-arrival estimation in sports as conditional quantile regression, learning the lower envelope of a player's locomotion times from kinematic state rather than using physics-based or density models. Trained on optical tracking data from all 64 PFF FC FIFA World Cup 2022 matches, a lightweight MLP matches or beats six established player-motion models re-expressed as TTA predictors. This reframes pitch-control analysis around feasible arrival times.

entry.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations

author.name: Reza Yousefi Maragheh, Jayesh Uddhav Kudase, Aysenur Inan, Ramin Giahi, Kai Zhao, Parth Parikh, Jianpeng Xu, Jason Cho, Evren Korpeoglu, Sushant Kumar

entry.summary: MAREval is a multi-agent LLM framework for evaluating natural-language recommendation explanations, orchestrating a planner using a novel Chain of Debate prompting strategy, plus supporting agent roles, to reduce prompt sensitivity and output inconsistency seen in single-agent LLM evaluators. It aims to replace resource-intensive human evaluation at industrial scale. The framework targets trust and transparency in recommender systems.

entry.title: Learning to Formalize: Bridging Open-Ended Workloads and Fast Decision Models

author.name: Chengxuan Pei, Ziyao Wang, Teng Mei, Zhe Li

entry.summary: This paper bridges generative LLM backends and fast decision models by training a small candidate formalizer that constructs explicit, validated alternatives from open-ended task context, which a frozen decision model then selects among. A motivating comparison on CALVIN-D episodes shows 11% success with generic motions versus 46.5% with a formalizer-plus-DeepSeek V4 Flash pipeline. The work targets workloads where no well-defined candidate list exists.

entry.title: Conservative Policy Iteration For Zero-Sum POSGs

author.name: Erwan C. Escudie, Matthia Sabatelli, Jilles Steeve Dibangoye

entry.summary: The paper introduces an approximate policy-iteration algorithm for finite-horizon zero-sum partially observable stochastic games that maintains one policy per player and updates them jointly along occupancy trajectories with conservative policy updates. Instead of approximating a full central value function over high-dimensional occupancy spaces, each update uses a single supporting hyperplane induced by the current joint policy.

entry.title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents

author.name: Humza Nusrat, Kundan Thind

entry.summary: OpenGray is a benchmark of radiotherapy planning tasks with known correct decisions, built on the OpenKBP-Opt head-and-neck dataset, including provably incompatible dose-goal contradictions and a feasible control. Four systems, from a rule-based script to full LLM agents using a commercial model and the existing local open-weights Ministral 3 8B model, were evaluated on 30 patients across decisions, dose, problem recognition, and technical failures.

entry.title: TCM-DiagCommit: A TCM-SD-Derived Benchmark for Evidence-Conditioned Syndrome Selection and Commitment

author.name: Erwei Hou, Yue Hu

entry.summary: This benchmark reframes Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome differentiation from static final-label selection into evidence-conditioned tasks testing whether models distinguish semantic-neighbor syndromes, update predictions as evidence is revealed, and appropriately abstain under uncertainty. It converts 1,834 cases into 23,842 task rows over 148 syndrome labels with staged evidence and graded candidate ladders. It offers a template for evaluating sequential diagnostic behavior in any clinical domain.

entry.title: A Hyper-Logical View on Multi-Agent Path Planning

author.name: Hadar Frenkel, Dor Atzmon

entry.summary: The paper shows that many multi-agent path planning variants can be modeled uniformly in the temporal hyperlogics HyperLTL and HyperQPTL, offering a specification-centered complement to specialized algorithms. The authors explicitly note that hyperproperty model checkers do not replace dedicated MAPP solvers, but the logical view unifies constraint specification across variants.

entry.title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine

author.name: Simon A. Lee, Jiahang Sha, Moonseong Jeong, Yunbei Pan, Jeffrey N. Chiang

entry.summary: MedJev evaluates a local, laptop-runnable System One model (Jev) that answers structured medical questions in a single forward pass without text generation, across ten benchmarks including MedQA, USMLE, and MIMIC IV patient-level prediction. It approaches published GPT-4-level accuracy on knowledge tasks with well-calibrated confidence (ECE 0.028-0.063) while being far cheaper.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Short-Term Glycemic Risk Prediction Using an Anchor-Based Comparative Framework of Sequence, Multimodal, and State-Updating Digital-Twin Models

author.name: Pir Bakhsh Khokhar, Carmine Gravino, Fabio Palomba

entry.summary: This study benchmarks three neural architectures (Hybrid LSTM-Transformer, Multimodal Digital Twin, State-Updating Digital Twin) for predicting hypo- and hyperglycemia at 30, 60, and 120 minute horizons using over 5.5 million standardized prediction anchors from 736 individuals with type 1 diabetes. The anchor-based framework emphasizes reliability and evaluation consistency over raw predictive performance. It addresses protocol inconsistency, a real problem in clinical ML benchmarking.

entry.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Feng Xie, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Zepeng Wang, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou

entry.summary: LociArt is a unified framework for localized video stylization that lets users specify both where to stylize and what style to apply while preserving the rest of the scene. Its GRNStyle module uses a polar style-aware mask and representation-geometry conditioning to achieve region-style association and temporal consistency. The paper also describes a strategy for building paired supervision data.

entry.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization

author.name: Shuo Chen, Li Cui, Cunxin Huang, Ya-Feng Liu, Minghang Xie, Meng Xu, Zaikun Zhang

entry.summary: NextEval integrates an LLM agent with a numerical environment to guide sequential selection of evaluation points in derivative-free optimization, exploiting accumulated observations under a limited evaluation budget. The environment provides analysis tools for past evaluations, and the paper also contributes a benchmark. This explores LLMs as reasoning components inside classical numerical optimization.

entry.title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Pu Ren, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: The authors propose iFLEX, a model that learns to correct a simple weighted-average numerical interpolation for reconstructing intermediate scientific fields between sparse observations. The approach frames refinement learning on top of classical interpolation, targeting expensive simulations and real-world measurements with low temporal resolution.

entry.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance

author.name: S M Abdulla Al Mamun, Akif Islam, Mohd. Ruhul Ameen

entry.summary: Through five experiments (13,638 model requests using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct), the paper studies whether more specialist language-model contexts improve software assurance when deterministic tool evidence exists, finding that scaling contexts from 1 to 50 increased token use 49-fold without improving unsafe clearance. It also probes robustness against deliberately misleading evidence packages.

entry.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification

author.name: Arooba Farhan, Afsah Syed, Muhammad Fahd Ibrahim Bhatti, Muhammad Areeb Khalid Kidwai, Muhammad Ahsan Salar Khan, Vincenzo Romano, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi

entry.summary: This work presents two compact spiking neural networks designed for on-headstage, real-time classification of Purkinje cell simple versus complex spikes in freely moving animals. One network maps to a microcontroller matrix-vector processor and the other processes one waveform value per timestep for streaming inference, enabling spike classification as compression under tight power budgets. It is a niche but well-motivated neuroscience-hardware co-design effort.

entry.title: WCC: A Learning-Based Framework for Deciding When to Apply Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization

author.name: Wenjie Qiu, Hepei Li, Jianfeng Wang, Jun Zhang, Yue-Jiao Gong

entry.summary: WCC is a learning-based framework that dynamically decides when to deploy cooperative coevolution versus non-decomposition algorithms in large-scale global optimization. The authors formulate the decision as a Markov decision process with a targeted feature set, robust reward, and tailored network architecture. It resolves a long-standing practical question of algorithm selection in LSGO.

entry.title: Some thoughts on GRAFT and follow-up work

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: A first-person notes-style post by a GRAFT paper author situating the method as a form of scalable oversight that extends weak overseers' reach to behaviors they cannot directly see, discussing connections to selective modularity and gradient routing, and brain-dumping desired follow-up research directions. The author flags much of it as speculative.

entry.title: Executable Archaeology of Programs That Model Programming: Reanimating the Heuristic Compiler (1961) and KBEmacs (1984)

author.name: Jeff Shrager, Kent M. Pitman, Mia Golec

entry.summary: The authors reanimate two historically significant program-synthesis systems: Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), which modeled programming as means-ends problem solving, and MIT's KBEmacs (1984), an intelligent programming assistant from the Programmer's Apprentice project. By making these programs executable again, they compare two contrasting theories of how people program. The work connects early AI's program-writing systems to modern code-generation research.

entry.title: PsyJev: Psychological Analysis via System-1 Judgment

author.name: Fangyuan Liu, Sirui Zhao, Xiaohao Wang, Guo Cheng, Peng Zhang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: PsyJev is a System-1 model that directly produces answer distributions for heterogeneous web-based psychological content analysis tasks, organized around PsyJudgeBench with 13 annotated datasets and 82 questions across six psychological areas. Training combines joint supervised learning with Judgment-Anchored RLCD adapting logit-space reward optimization to heterogeneous labels. The work unifies diverse psychological analysis tasks under one question-conditioned decision interface.

entry.title: HeteGCD: Statistics-Aware Dual-Prototype Learning for Generalized Category Discovery on Heterophilous Graphs

author.name: Xuanzhi Xi, Tongze Zhang, Zhili Qin, Yulin Tao, Hongliang Wang, Zhong Zhang, Qinli Yang, Junming Shao

entry.summary: HeteGCD tackles generalized category discovery on heterophilous graphs, where connected nodes are dissimilar, using statistics-aware dual-prototype learning to recognize known classes and discover novel ones without homophily-based inductive biases. It addresses the gap between graph GCD methods and heterophilous graph learning, whose neighborhood fusion is typically supervision-guided. This extends GCD to an important but underexplored graph regime.

entry.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge

author.name: Jannatul Shefa, Alejandro Salado, Paul Wach, Taylan G. Topcu

entry.summary: MARQ is a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype for assessing the quality of engineering requirements that supplements off-the-shelf LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria. The study is motivated by evidence that vanilla LLMs miss a large share of expert-identified defects and perform unevenly across quality criteria. It tests whether infusing expert systems-engineering knowledge improves requirement defect detection.

entry.title: LM-DSB: A Lightweight Multi-agent System for Automated Daily Safety Bulletin Generation in Construction

author.name: Xianxiang Zhao, Advik Mehta, Falak Sethi, Brian Gue, Qipei Mei, Lingzi Wu

entry.summary: LM-DSB automates construction daily safety bulletins by coordinating planner, researcher, and writer agents with retrieval-augmented generation over a locally deployable LLM that runs on consumer-grade PCs. It targets a workflow that currently takes 2-3 hours daily and yields inconsistent quality, with a quarter of crews skipping pretask planning. The system aims to free safety personnel for field supervision while improving bulletin consistency.

entry.title: Natural Hard-Negative Mining from Positives for Instruction-Following Retrieval

author.name: Chaolang Li, Jingyu Li, Zhaocheng Du, Xuyang Xie, Gang Wang, Pengwen Dai

entry.summary: NHNM addresses the scarcity of instruction-conditioned contrastive supervision for instruction-following information retrieval by repurposing original positives as natural hard negatives under query-compatible instructions. An automated pipeline of candidate cleaning, reversal construction, and geometry filtering produces compact, high-contrast training data aligned with the pretrained retrieval space.

entry.title: Counterfactual Profile Perturbations for Recommendation Explanations: A Reproducibility Study

author.name: Meysam Varasteh, Elizabeth McKinnie, Robin Burke

entry.summary: This reproducibility study extends the LXR technique for counterfactual recommendation explanations, testing whether it works for explaining items other than the top-ranked one and comparing against alternative baselines like item popularity and latent factor similarity. The findings confirm effectiveness for the extended task while revealing nuances where some baselines are competitive. Reproducibility work of this kind strengthens the evidentiary base for explainable recommendation.

entry.title: Tap2Listen: Instant Target Switching for Streaming Audio-Visual Speaker Extraction

author.name: Hansol Park, Minkyung Song, Zinu Kim, Yujun Lee, Hoseong Ahn, Hyunjin Choi, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: Tap2Listen is a streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction model that supports instant target switching mid-conversation, decoupling a target-agnostic audio encoder from a decoder conditioned on visual cues of the selected face. A switch requires only a 0.12ms re-projection and takes effect immediately. Component-wise losses cover prediction and discrimination aspects.

entry.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque

author.name: Andoni Sudupe, Inma Hernaez, Ander Arriandiaga, Christoforos Souganidis, Ibon Saratxaga, Eva Navas

entry.summary: The authors build the first open speech language model for Basque, based on LLaMA-Omni with a Latxa text backbone, fine-tuned for low-latency spoken interaction. Data scarcity is addressed by translating VoiceAssistant-400K into Basque and synthesizing audio with a Basque TTS, achieving reasonable content quality and intelligibility scores.

entry.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap

author.name: Saurabh Rai, Sanmay Ganguly

entry.summary: Using model stitching, the authors diagnose whether performance gaps between Lund-plane and Particle Transformer jet taggers stem from weak representations or weak downstream computation. With an incomplete primary-branch Lund representation as a positive control, stitching shows the deficit is representational rather than computational. The methodology offers a clean attribution tool for physics ML architectures.

entry.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design

author.name: Ziwei Yang, Takeyuki Tamura

entry.summary: HGPRGDel is a protocol for metabolic engineering that learns and ranks gene-deletion priorities for designing growth-coupled microbial production strains, reusing knowledge from previously evaluated strain designs to prune the combinatorial search before constraint-based evaluation. This avoids a separate exhaustive search per target metabolite.

entry.title: Some different lenses of agency and their implications for alignment

author.name: SJ_Beard

entry.summary: A conceptual survey presenting nine lenses on agency (e.g., agents as goal-directed systems) drawn from 2026 PIBBSS fellowship discussions, describing what each lens highlights and obscures and the alignment methods and risks each implies. The author is explicit that the value is synthesis and providing a single reference point rather than new results.

entry.title: How researchers are adapting olmOCR 2 for historical and archaeological archives

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Ai2 blog post describing how researchers are adapting the existing olmOCR 2 model to make historical photo libraries locally searchable and to improve transcription of handwritten archaeological records. It demonstrates domain adaptation of open OCR tooling for humanities and heritage applications.

entry.title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration

author.name: Chenyu Guo, Wenjie Dai, Yiqian Chang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Yunfan Wei, Shuhan Qi

entry.summary: ReliMorph is a reliability-routed symmetric framework for 3D deformable image registration that couples local correspondence confidence with spatial context selection and deformation update strength. It targets ambiguity in homogeneous, weakly textured, and heavily deformed regions where unreliable matches cause erroneous deformations. The design uses local correlation distributions with modality-specific adaptation.

entry.title: Do bots feel bad? Assessing empirical evidence for functional valence in LLMs

author.name: Iwan Williams

entry.summary: This philosophical analysis critically assesses recent empirical claims that LLMs possess functional valenced states such as functional pleasure, pain, emotions, and welfare. The author argues that key aspects of valence, as understood in philosophy and cognitive science, remain untested in LLMs and that existing experimental paradigms are inadequate for the functional role.

entry.title: Beyond Greenwashing: Algorithmic Resilience and the Non-Linear Governance Premium in Sovereign Capital Flows

author.name: Sourav Bose, Taoufik Bouraoui

entry.summary: Using a forward-chained global panel of 147 sovereign entities over 2010-2024, the paper shows sovereign FDI tail-risk transmission is non-linear, with a gradient boosting architecture cutting forecast errors by over 39 percent versus L1-regularized baselines during extreme macro events. Dual interpretability frameworks map discrete threshold effects of institutional quality, identifying a non-linear governance premium. This is an applied econometrics-ML study of ESG and capital flows.

entry.title: Dirichlet Process Mixtures within Semiparametric Bayesian Networks: A Novel Conditional Density Estimation Approach

author.name: Victor Alejandre, Pedro Larra\~naga, Concha Bielza

entry.summary: This paper replaces kernel density estimators for non-parametric conditional distributions in semiparametric Bayesian networks with Dirichlet Process Mixtures, yielding a data-adaptive, more compact mixture representation. The DPM-based CPD modeling aims to reduce inference costs and density estimation errors relative to one-component-per-observation KDEs.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Discovery of CNOT Decompositions for Quantum Permutations on Constrained Topologies

author.name: Daniele Lizzio Bosco, Jacopo Cossio, Simone Faro, Francesco Pio Marino, Gabriele Messina, Carla Piazza, Giuseppe Serra

entry.summary: Using an AI-assisted synthesis tool called AlphaCNOT as an exploratory instrument, the authors identify a recurring decomposition for remote transpositions that improves on adjacent-SWAP routing for compiling quantum permutations under constrained qubit connectivity. The work demonstrates how AI search can uncover principles that inform deterministic compilation algorithms.

entry.title: A Smart Instant Book Filter Model based on Dual-Objective Optimization

author.name: Yi Hou, Li Fan, Huizhong Duan

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-objective optimization model for deciding which booking requests to auto-accept via instant book in hospitality marketplaces, addressing response delays and rejections on request-to-book listings. It extends a previously deployed instant-book feature with a smarter filter to improve booking outcomes for guests and hosts. The work is a concrete industrial application of ML to marketplace trust and conversion.

entry.title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: Yonglong Zhang, Zongwu Xie, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents a reliability-aware framework for spacecraft pose estimation from event cameras, combining polarity-time localization, geometric recovery, event-CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization across multiple levels. A three-branch representation with cross-branch attention handles positive events, negative events, and event timing, with an ordered semantic-point head estimating correspondence precision. Sequence-level optimization further stabilizes estimates.

entry.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mart\'in de Frutos, Baptiste Corban, Claire Bizon Monroc, Ana Bu\v{s}i\'c, Donatien Dubuc, Jiamin Zhud, Esteban Ferrer

entry.summary: The paper proposes Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximize wind farm power while satisfying local noise constraints, exploiting how yaw affects both wake interactions and noise emission direction. A low-fidelity acoustic model enables training at reduced computational cost.

entry.title: Multiple Leak Localization in Water Distribution Networks through Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Arvin Ajoodani, Sara Nazif, Pouria Ramazi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a GNN model that localizes a variable number of simultaneous leaks in water distribution networks without pre-specifying the leak count or exhaustively enumerating leak combinations during training. It is evaluated on the 31-node Hanoi and 92-node NET3 benchmark networks under sparse sensing and variable demand.

entry.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke

author.name: Md Wahiduzzaman Suva, Esm E Moula Chowdhury Abha, Md Imtiaj Alam Sajin, Md Iftekharul Mobin, Jia Uddin

entry.summary: MM-Net is a multimodal multi-task framework for joint sleep staging and sleep apnea assessment in post-stroke polysomnography, addressing representation inconsistency when pretrained EEG encoders are adapted across seen and unseen patients via cross-fitting and ridge-based embedding alignment. It fuses sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations with engineered neural descriptors. This targets an underexplored clinical joint-analysis problem.

entry.title: An Algebra of Transformers

author.name: Yong Wang, Zhiyan Wang, Hexiao Kang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper builds an algebra for reasoning about transformers, using functional decompositions as atomic actions with sequential and parallel composition, recursion, and abstraction. The authors claim it is the first attempt to model transformers logically and that it enables correctness verification of transformer-based applications.

entry.title: What do we mean by ‘long-horizon’ work?

author.name: Dhruv Trehan

entry.summary: A conceptual post arguing that frontier-lab long-horizon benchmarks mostly measure many-step, verifiable-end-state tasks with little external input, while genuinely long-horizon real-world work is defined by delayed external feedback, illustrated by contrasting building a Redis competitor with running personalized lead-conversion campaigns. The delay is presented as the constraint that makes human input high-leverage and that neither longer context nor agent swarms remove.

entry.title: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zafer Sahinoglu, Abdulazeez Mohammed, Buse Yaren Kazangirler, Cahit Berkay Kazangirler

entry.summary: SpectRAG combines hybrid candidate seeding, weighted chunk graph construction, graph-based expansion, spectral relevance propagation, and token-budgeted context selection to improve multi-hop RAG. By representing chunks with both dense embeddings and graph-spectral coordinates, it mitigates redundancy, missed cross-chunk dependencies, and incomplete evidence in independently ranked dense retrieval.
