entry.summary: AgentTrace identifies the foundation model behind a black-box LLM agent by injecting structurally ambiguous probes that trigger tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at tool interfaces, then fingerprinting model-specific multi-step repair behaviors with lightweight sequence models. It sidesteps obfuscated system prompts and schema-constrained tool generation that defeat semantic attribution and watermarking.

entry.title: MS-TTRL: Breaking the Frequency Conflict in Multiple-Solution Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhixia Zhang, Binqian Xu, Huaiyang Wang, Yikun Ban, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies the Frequency Conflict in test-time RL on multi-solution reasoning tasks: generation frequency must serve both correctness estimation and outcome diversity preservation. MS-TTRL resolves this via Outcome-Level Self-Verification producing frequency-independent correctness estimates while preserving group-level diversity for label-free RL on unlabeled test instances.

entry.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology

author.name: Cristian Tommasino, Antonio M. Rinaldi

entry.summary: PathJev-P builds a decision-native histopathology model on MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head that returns calibrated distributions over run-time candidate sets, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections. The design uses typed questions with organ-specific candidates and a none-of-these option, evaluated under a pre-registered analysis plan. It offers a principled alternative to free-form VLM outputs for clinical decisions.

entry.title: SEDATE: Do Large Language Models Share an Aggression Circuit Across Languages?

author.name: Sagnik Basu, Sayan Das, Somnath Banerjee, Animesh Mukherjee

entry.summary: Proposes SEDATE, a training-free detect-edit-verify approach that locates neurons responsible for aggressive outputs, edits them, and verifies responses, evaluated across 7 languages and 4 model families. Investigates whether aggression is mediated by a shared circuit across languages.

entry.title: Beyond the Opening: Tracing the First Token's Persistent Influence on Reasoning Length

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Hao Yan, Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: This mechanistic study traces how the first reasoning token persistently changes reasoning length in LLMs, showing that swapping only the first token of a reasoning prefix and resuming generation substantially alters remaining length even with all other prefix tokens fixed. It compares next-token distributions to locate how this influence propagates.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation for Principled Generalization Using a Kripkean Challenge to Meaning as Use

author.name: Niyar R Barman, Omar Naim, Nicholas Asher

entry.summary: Argues via Kripke's Wittgensteinian rule-following paradox that finite histories of use cannot determine a unique rule for future extension, challenging meaning-as-use assumptions underlying LLM evaluation and OOD generalization debates. The authors propose testing abstraction and recursion as capacities central to preserving rules under principled domain extension, and offer an experimental paradigm. A theoretically grounded contribution to evaluation philosophy in NLP.

entry.title: ImgMT: Wikipedia-based Dataset For Evaluating Text-in-Image Translation

author.name: \v{S}\'arka Uramov\'a, Petar Kirilov Petrov, Josef Jon, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar, Michal Nov\'ak

entry.summary: ImgMT is a massively multilingual benchmark mined from localized SVG illustrations on Wikimedia Commons, with 35,612 aligned image pairs spanning 129 languages and 4,886 language pairs for text-in-image translation. It proposes a multi-level evaluation protocol covering text-region detection, OCR, and translation quality, and benchmarks multimodal models on this underexplored task.

entry.title: UMAS: System-Level Uncertainty Quantification for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Hanwen Li, Jinhao Duan, Xiaoshuang Shi, Yue Zhang, Tianlong Chen, Kaidi Xu, Chenxi Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes UMAS, a parameter-free, cost-neutral framework for system-level uncertainty quantification in multi-agent LLM systems, estimating credibility of inter-agent influence from intrinsic confidence and aggregating node-level uncertainty across the system graph. Addresses the gap where UQ methods target single agents only.

entry.title: SkillShift-Bench: Benchmarking Skill Learning under Environment Evolution for Web Agents

author.name: Bo-Yu Chen, Zhi Zhou, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: SkillShift-Bench is the first benchmark evaluating web-agent skill learning under controlled open-environment shifts, simulating contextual, perceptual, and execution shifts across three self-hosted web systems. Experiments reveal systematic robustness degradations in learned skills as environments evolve.

entry.title: Improving VLMs on Scientific Chart Analysis via Autonomous Evolution

author.name: Abhinav Sudhakar Dubey, Vidushi Goel, Kiran Rana, Shikhar Mathur, Vaggos Chatziafratis

entry.summary: The authors improve open vision-language models on scientific chart QA without modifying model weights, by applying autonomous evolution (in the spirit of AlphaEvolve) to search over inference programs and surrounding code for a frozen model. Starting from a baseline inference program, iterative evolution recovers substantial accuracy from errors rooted in inexact answering.

entry.title: The Voice on the Line

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: This work trains causal voice isolators (masking transformers of 140M-374M parameters, 20 ms latency) that enroll a caller from the call itself for real-time telephony. It identifies failure modes hidden by short evaluation windows, such as forgetting the caller during long solo speech from another voice, and shows that making WavLM-Large weights causal and training them reduces error from 11.44% to 10.55% with a distilled student improving further.

entry.title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control

author.name: Lei Cao, Yu Liu, Wenhua Liao, Peng Zhang, Fei Wang, Hao Zhang, Jiajun Le, Daiguo Zhou, Jian Luan, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Proposes WorldCast, a framework for world-consistent character video generation under large-angle camera trajectories combining rotation, translation, and radius variation, addressing geometric distortion and identity drift when viewpoint changes reveal unseen character regions. Also releases CLACT, a large-scale character-centric dataset and benchmark with accurate camera geometry and multi-view observations.

entry.title: Distilling Dense Trajectory Teachers For Large-Motion Video World Models

author.name: Shuofeng Sun, Linqing Zhao, Haibin Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Dense Trajectory Teacher Distillation (DTTD), a post-training framework that transfers a video world model's generation capability from dense, small-motion trajectories to sparse, large-step camera trajectories, addressing frozen frames, inaccurate camera motion, and geometric drift at inference. The diagnosis of train-inference trajectory mismatch is crisp and relevant to world models for embodied agents. It targets a key failure mode of camera-controllable video generation.

entry.title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models

author.name: Xiaoang Zhang, Mert Kiray, Yordanka Velikova, Manoj Biswanath, Benjamin Busam

entry.summary: This paper probes whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information, finding that static-dynamic separation is decodable from frozen representations and concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace via rank and spectral analysis. It builds lightweight readout functions (ProMo3D) for dynamic 4D understanding rather than training high-capacity motion decoders. Informative about what 3D foundation representations contain.

entry.title: FlockWorld: Toward Population-Scale Multi-Agent Video World Models through Artificial Life Simulation

author.name: Meryem Koksal, Yunzhe Wang, Volkan Ustun

entry.summary: FlockWorld is an artificial-life environment based on the Boids algorithm for training population-scale multi-agent video world models, with synchronized egocentric crops and configurable camera-agent counts. FlockDiT, an action-conditioned latent diffusion transformer trained with flow matching, jointly generates synchronized multi-agent video.

entry.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation

author.name: Guowen Zhang, Liyi Chen, Xu Hu, Pengfei Wang, Jingfan Chen, Chenhang He, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes OSWAM, a world action model for autonomous driving and embodied control that achieves one-step action generation instead of tens of denoising steps, enabling real-time inference while preserving action quality that naive step reduction would destroy.

entry.title: RoboDuo: Attempt, Check and Atomic Recovery through Code for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jie Wang, Bo Zhang, Renzhi Lu, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RoboDuo, a closed-loop dual-system framework where a coding agent writes a program coordinating two VLAs: a full-task VLA attempts the task, completion is checked, and failures are recovered by composing reusable atomic skills. This targets the problem that open-loop VLA models cannot detect or recover from a single failed step in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Omni-InteractScope: Benchmarking Proactive and Agentic Interaction in Continuous Omnimodal Streams

author.name: Yinsong Yan, Ling Wang, Yuxuan Wang, Yifan Yang, Ruiyang Xu, Junming Lin, Qi Chen, Meng Gao, Minghao Han, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Xize Cheng, Jin Xu, Jibin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Omni-InteractScope, a benchmark of 1,479 human-annotated interactions with 1,790 temporal targets across eight task groups, evaluating how Omni-LLMs handle proactive, query-free assistance and event-timed tool invocation in continuous audiovisual streams. Results reveal critical limitations in how reliably current models connect stream evidence to timely, sustained interventions.

entry.title: A Differentiable Chassis Safety Layer for Intelligent Vehicle Motion Control

author.name: Lu Xiong, Xuge Hu, Yufei Song, Weidong Liu, Chen Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable safety layer integrating task-oriented vehicle control with explicit chassis constraints (actuator limits, tire forces, handling envelopes) via sequential quadratic programs. Implicit differentiation enables temporal gradient coupling through projected commands, so safety filtering co-adapts with policy learning in a two-stage scheme.

entry.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning

author.name: Haoyang Jiang, Dana Kulic, Michael Burke, Pamela Carreno-Medrano

entry.summary: This paper identifies an objective mismatch in using human behavior models as RL training partners: models that best resemble real human data may not provide useful training experiences for downstream robot policy learning. Across highway driving and object handover domains, it evaluates behavior models with generative metrics versus their utility as training partners. The finding challenges standard evaluation practice in HRI and RL-from-simulation.

entry.title: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena

author.name: Prajol Shrestha, Siddhant Mohapatra, Filip Novkoski, Julian Oelhaf, Nicolas Vandewalle, Ana-Sun\v{c}ana Smith, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: The paper presents a distributed predictive flocking controller where each miniature robot solves its own NMPC problem, exchanging only predicted trajectories with neighbors while optimizing cohesion, alignment, safety, and task objectives in a confined arena. It systematically compares six barrier and control-barrier-function safety constraint formulations as density increases. This quantifies how constraint choice limits how many robots can safely coexist.

entry.title: Replicate What Varies: Resource Sharing for Domain-Randomized Embodied Simulation

author.name: Zixu Hao, Weijun Wang, Xiangyu Li, Liang Mi, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Presents Patchwork, a resource-sharing system for domain-randomized embodied simulation that represents environments as a shared template plus patches of mutations (E = T + Delta). By separating randomization sampling from replay and reusing templates, it reduces the substantial CPU and GPU memory costs of running many concurrent diverse simulation instances.

entry.title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks

author.name: Taishi Watanabe, Ryo Karakida, Jun-nosuke Teramae

entry.summary: Through refined analysis of deep linear networks, the paper shows that the task spectrum determines when depth improves training-time scaling: for spectrally difficult tasks depth improves the asymptotic scaling exponent, while for easy tasks the exponent is depth-independent. This helps settle whether depth can improve training-time scaling laws.

entry.title: Recertifying decisions via e-closure: uniform improvements of conformal risk control and randomized e-BH

author.name: Tian Bai, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Building on e-value representations of risk-controlled decisions and the e-closure principle for multiple testing, the paper formulates recertification: a general paradigm for improving conservative statistical procedures by exploiting computable slack in their validity certificates. The authors show uniform improvements over conformal risk control and randomized e-BH while preserving risk guarantees. This is a notable unifying contribution to e-value-based inference.

entry.title: Import AI 478: Math for alignment; ProgramBench; and Mirendil shows what RSI means

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers Resolution's (formerly Sequent) autoformalization of the resolution of singularities in mathematics using orchestrated AI agents, framing it as groundwork for connecting loss-landscape geometry to generalization and as a case study in AI-driven research workflows. The issue also previews ProgramBench and commentary on what recursive self-improvement looks like in practice.

entry.title: PEAR: Adaptive Advantage Reshaping for Perception and Exploration in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junxin Wang, Yingfeng Luo, Xiangchen Song, Weiqiao Shan, Runsong Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Shunjie Xing, Yifu Huo, Dingyang Lin, Qiuyu Gu, Yongyu Mu, Chenglong Wang, Changliang Li, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: PEAR is an adaptive advantage reshaping method for multimodal RL that fixes underweighting of high-entropy, low-visual-dependency tokens important for exploration. It retains visual dependency as the base signal and adds an entropy-based exploration gain selectively at high-entropy positions with conditions on visual dependence. The work improves the balance between reliable visual perception and diverse reasoning in vision-language model training.

entry.title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System

author.name: Micha{\l} Remigiusz Janiszewski, Artur Stopa, {\L}ukasz Lenkiewicz, Wojciech Achtelik, Bartosz Gonczarek

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based medical triage system for telephone intake that grounds every disposition in the same commercial telehealth guidelines nurses use, having the LLM execute the guideline rather than triage directly. The disposition follows deterministically from the guideline evaluation, improving auditability and reducing over-escalation of routine cases.

entry.title: ReMedI: Inference-Time Refinement and Self-Distillation for Controllable Molecular Optimization

author.name: Jia Yi Zhang, Shivanshu Shekhar, Allison McLevige, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: ReMedI uses a Metropolis-Hastings search at inference time to exploit useful molecular edits already present in a pre-trained molecular language model, avoiding expensive RL post-training like C-MORAL and its task-specific datasets. It targets multi-objective lead optimization (e.g., permeability up, toxicity down) with limited scaffold changes, using self-distillation to internalize search gains.

entry.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates

author.name: Disen Liao, Yaoliang Yu

entry.summary: Studies why LoRA+ style asymmetric learning rates (larger LR for the up-projection B than down-projection A) can cause unstable training and ratio-dependent performance collapse under standard initialization. The paper identifies the initialization as the culprit and proposes initialization changes that make training robust to large LR ratios, reducing hyperparameter brittleness in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Pattern Matching in 3D MLLMs: Part-Level Functional Reasoning for Generalizable Recognition

author.name: Weihong Li, Hao Jiang, Yaohua Zha, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: Shows that 3D multimodal LLMs recognize objects via pattern matching that fails on geometrically similar objects requiring functional reasoning, exposing a 33.7% versus 84.0% accuracy gap between ambiguous and unambiguous samples via a per-sample Geometric Confusion Score. Proposes PFIR, built on PartNeXt with a 507K QA-pair pipeline, that reverses a function-as-annotation pattern so functional language supports inference rather than decorating known identities.

entry.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms

author.name: Xi Chen, Fengqi Hu, Zeyu Shen, Jiaying Xu, Shangding Gu, Pan Xu, Anqi Liu, Laixi Shi

entry.summary: RobustRLlib is a library and benchmark integrating 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface, paired with an enhanced evaluation platform covering real-world distribution shifts and humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. It aims to improve algorithm reusability and clarify the empirical capability boundaries of robust RL. Systematic evaluation across this breadth is a useful community resource.

entry.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making

author.name: Changxu Ni, Yiyang Ni, Jun Li, Feiran You, Hongyang Du, Haitao Zhao, Shi Jin

entry.summary: DT-JEPA replaces the Decision Transformer's reliance on expected future returns with JEPA-style latent prediction of future representations, addressing the incompleteness of return conditioning and its dependence on task-specific rewards. This enables offline RL policy learning that transfers better to tasks with similar but unseen rewards and requires no reward labels.

entry.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators

author.name: Aaditya Prasad, Steven W. Flavell, Brian DePasquale

entry.summary: ZENO is a neural operator trained against the Zakai equation, the SPDE governing unnormalized filtering distributions, enabling state inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters that are analytically and numerically intractable. It leverages operator learning and physics-informed advances with applications across engineering and neuroscience.

entry.title: Let's Do Turbulence Right: In Space and Time!

author.name: Maximilian Plattner, Fabian Paischer, Johannes Brandstetter

entry.summary: Using massive time-resolved direct numerical simulations exceeding 28 TB per run, the authors assess how numerical choices affect the resolved (3+1)-dimensional physics of 3D Navier-Stokes turbulence, then study how neural networks represent turbulent motion. The key finding is that spatial and temporal evaluations of learned emitters can diverge, arguing for rigorous space-time assessment. This is an important methodological caution for neural emulators of turbulent flows.

entry.title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap

author.name: Denglin Jiang (New York University), Annie Wang (New York University)

entry.summary: This audit of 113 works from 1999 to 2026 finds that evaluations of social world models rarely test whether systems can predict a real person's response to an action: only 9 primary evaluations measure this, and only 2 compare an explicit response forecast against the actual response under randomized intervention. A full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions.

entry.title: Adaptive Transfer of Representational Signatures for LLM Reliability Detection

author.name: Yongtong Li, Yixuan Florence Wu, Jiawei Zhang, Naichen Shi

entry.summary: Proposes transferring representational signatures across related domains to detect unreliable LLM outputs (hallucinations, reasoning errors), using a statistical framework that extracts low-dimensional domain signatures and learns composition weights via cross-fitting. Reduces dependence on domain-specific labeled data.

entry.title: One Model, Two Paths: Balancing Single-Pass and Looped Performance in Language Models

author.name: Jiarun Shen, Lei Zhao, Xiao Li

entry.summary: Studies adapting pretrained transformers to support both single-pass and looped (weight-reused) inference, showing joint weighted-loss training with guidance from the frozen original model substantially reduces single-pass degradation while preserving looped gains. Most benefit comes from tuning the single-pass loss weight.

entry.title: IntentDelta: A Human-Constructed Benchmark for Evolving User Intent

author.name: Jieyu Zhou, Zijian Wang, Yun Wang

entry.summary: IntentDelta is a human-constructed multi-turn benchmark of 638 trajectories and 3,766 turns over WebShop and TravelPlanner, pairing utterances with cumulative intention states and reference actions. Evaluation of eleven agents reveals low intention recovery (33-45%) and action scores (32-41%), showing agents struggle to preserve earlier requirements and distinguish soft preferences from hard constraints. It complements synthetic benchmarks with cross-verified human construction.

entry.title: Entity Matching using Decision Models

author.name: Aaron Steiner, Ralph Peeters, Christian Bizer

entry.summary: The paper evaluates six LLM-based decision models, which return probabilities for predefined answer options rather than generating text, for zero-shot entity matching across eight benchmarks, comparing them against generative LLMs and fine-tuned PLMs. Decision models offer a cheaper, faster alternative to generative LLMs for large-scale matching.

entry.title: NumTrace: Auditing the Number Provenance of Financial Analyst Agents

author.name: Tianlei Zhu, Matt White, Xue Liu, Xiao-Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces NumTrace, a benchmark auditing the provenance of numerical claims made by financial analyst agents, checking source and financial semantics such as entity, concept, period, unit, and scope, with 540 questions over 2,163 SEC EDGAR documents. It is reportedly the first benchmark covering Form 13F holdings and Item 402(i) executive compensation, with academically grounded reference answers. This targets explainable failure diagnosis beyond right/wrong answer checking in finance agents.

entry.title: StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers

author.name: Feichen Song, Boyi Zeng, He Li, Shixiang Song, Yiqin Hao, Zitong Wang, Yizhou Yang, Yifan Liu, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: StateLoop augments looped transformers, which repeatedly apply a shared backbone for parameter-efficient language modeling, with a per-token persistent state gated across loop iterations so information useful several iterations later is not lost. The gated state is projected back and added to backbone outputs for subsequent iterations and final prediction.

entry.title: Speculative Forking: Turning Idle Wait into Parallel Exploration for Repository Environment Setup

author.name: Yuling Shi, Mingchu Zhong, Zhensu Sun, Weihan Peng, Zhi Chen, Shilin He, Chengcheng Wan, Kai Cai, Hongyu Zhang, David Lo, Xiaodong Gu

entry.summary: Presents SpecBuild, an LLM-based environment-setup system that speculatively forks to explore multiple setup routes in parallel while slow commands run, replacing the standard sequential trial-and-error loop. Turns idle wait time into parallel exploration for installing runtimes, packages, and build tooling.

entry.title: How Do Small Coding Agents Use Code Graphs and Embeddings?

author.name: Saurav Bellam (The University of Texas at Austin)

entry.summary: This large-scale ablation study tests whether embedding search and code-graph tools actually help small open-weight coding agents on SWE-bench Verified, stratifying tasks by graph hop depth. Across 79k episodes covering Qwen3 (0.6B-32B) and Gemma 4 models, structured tools double grep-only accuracy for some configurations, with gains analyzed by task depth.

entry.title: Cross-Loop Query Handoff: How Later Loops Redirect Two-Hop Retrieval in the Ouro Looped Language Models

author.name: Ziyu Mu, Zehua Wang

entry.summary: This interpretability study transplants attention queries between loops of the Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B looped language models, showing that injecting loop-3 query collections into loop 1 rescues roughly 90-97 percent of two-hop questions answered incorrectly at loop 1 but correctly at loop 3. The results clarify how later loops redirect retrieval through bridge entities in multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: A Canary in the Neural Mine: Catching an Image Classifier's Silent, Confident Failures

author.name: Wonseok Shin, Songkuk Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes why high-confidence errors in deployed vision classifiers escape standard confidence-based failure detection, showing Maximum Softmax Probability is structurally blind to feature variation orthogonal to its confidence gradient. Through factorial analysis of feature-space detectors, the paper derives a conditional-redundancy principle and identifies class-conditional typicality on the off-manifold residual as the complementary signal that survives fusion with MSP.

entry.title: Detecting Temporal Concepts in Video Transformers via a No-False-Positives Test

author.name: Jianghuai Li, Andrew Ren, Greg Shakhnarovich

entry.summary: This paper introduces the No-False-Positives (NFP) test, a statistical test with formal specificity guarantees for determining whether video transformer features truly encode temporal concepts rather than correlated non-temporal cues like spatial presence. Applied to VideoMAE, V-JEPA2, and TimeSformer with designed stimuli, it exposes entanglement between motion and appearance encoding. It contributes a rigorous interpretability methodology for video representation analysis.

entry.title: RIDE-Splat: Reflection Removal for In-the-Wild Driving Environments

author.name: Kevin David Hayes, Alex Hanson, Allen Tu, Pranav Asthana, Matthias Zwicker, Tom Goldstein

entry.summary: RIDE-Splat produces reflection-free 3D reconstructions from posed driving video captured through windshields, without clean images, reflection masks, or pretrained networks. It separates world-consistent transmission into a 3DGS scene while modeling the dominant camera-attached reflection as a shared signed RGB image, built in two passes.

entry.title: RSKD: Grounding Semantic Consistency in Driving VLMs via Distillation

author.name: Chuchu Xie, Yang Zhong, Kangan Qian, Hao Ye, Kun Jiang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: RSKD is a distillation framework for compressing large multimodal models into compact models for autonomous driving, routing supervision based on task importance and semantic consistency with the teacher. It uses phrase-level consistency scores to balance Jensen-Shannon divergence distillation against ground-truth supervision, avoiding amplification of teacher errors.

entry.title: VidEdit3D: Flexible 3D Gaussian Editing with Video Diffusion

author.name: Yanming Yang, Chenxi Song, Tong Zhao, Juntao Xu, Wenhao Rao, Yiwen Chen, Yiwei Wang, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Reformulates text-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting scene editing as trajectory-based video editing, leveraging pretrained Video Diffusion Models to maintain multi-view consistency while enabling structural modifications. This exploits the parallel between camera movement in 3D scenes and temporal dynamics in video.

entry.title: Vision Token Pruning via Query-Vision Interaction Decomposition

author.name: Harshithanjani Athi, Sravan Kumar Ankireddy, Jianzhong Charlie Zhang, Hyeji Kim

entry.summary: Proposes pruning visual tokens in large vision-language models by exploiting the low-rank structure of the query-vision interaction matrix in transformer attention, identifying dominant latent interaction modes rather than relying on attention heuristics. This reduces inference cost in a principled way.

entry.title: Exploring perceptual straightness in learned visual representations

author.name: Anne Harrington, Vasha DuTell, Ayush Tewari, Mark Hamilton, Simon Stent, Ruth Rosenholtz, William T. Freeman

entry.summary: Investigates the relationship between network architecture, robustness, biologically-inspired filtering, and representational straightening of temporal video inputs, connecting to evidence that humans straighten natural visual sequences. The work identifies strengths and limitations of straightness as a measure of how well deep networks model human visual processing.

entry.title: HumanoidNDM: Closing the Training-Deployment Gap of Motion Tracking via Humanoid Neural Dynamics Model

author.name: Chao Chen, Zhenrong Wang, Jilong Wang, Yusen Feng, Jiangran Lyu, Li Yi, He Wang

entry.summary: Proposes HumanoidNDM, an online fine-tuning framework for humanoid motion tracking driven by a real-world-trained neural dynamics model, targeting the sim-to-real dynamics gap from disturbances and inaccurate simulation. It includes a low-frequency reference perturbation method with adaptive intensity to balance feasible data collection with model quality.

entry.title: VISTA: Active Exploration for Self-Improvement in Embodied Agents

author.name: Zhang Zhang, Shengjun Zhang, Simin Huang, Min Chen, Chong Xia, Xin Fei, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: VISTA is a meta-agent framework that converts post-hoc rollout reflection into active self-exploration for improving the embodied agent harness, maintaining a harness graph that records the lineage of harness variants so updates can be autonomously tested and refined through subsequent embodied interaction. This departs from treating rollouts as static logs and supports continual self-improvement in dynamic physical environments. It connects agentic self-improvement ideas with embodied settings.

entry.title: Revisiting Direct Control: A Field Evaluation of Sensor Fusion Efficacy in Teleoperating Full-Scale Autonomous Vehicles via Bird's Eye View

author.name: Stanis{\l}aw Kuczma, S{\l}awomir K. Tadeja, Micha{\l} R. Nowicki

entry.summary: A field study with 18 participants teleoperating a real car-sized vehicle, comparing three interfaces: standard camera feed, LiDAR-based bird's-eye view, and fused LiDAR-camera BEV, to measure operator performance in safety-fallback teleoperation. Unlike most prior simulation-based work, it captures the physical dynamics of driving a full-scale vehicle. It provides empirical evidence on interface design for AV teleoperation.

entry.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MemCryst, a framework for lifelong LLM agents that jointly learns memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes in memory support skill creation and revision, while skill-guided interactions generate new experience, forming a bidirectional loop within bounded context windows. It addresses the tension between expanding interaction history and limited context.

entry.title: From Visual Affinity to Learning Credit in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuhang Han, Dingning Liu, Yujie Chen, Yaojie Zhang, Jingwei Song, Zequn Yang, Xuanming Shang, Li Ding, Zhijiang Guo, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit (OVC), a plug-in framework for multimodal RLVR that separates visual-association measurement from token-level credit assignment, avoiding amplification of negative-advantage updates on valid visual observations when later reasoning fails. OVC is compatible with policy-optimization methods that use uniform response-level advantages. It improves credit assignment between perception and reasoning tokens.

entry.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints

author.name: Kyeongseon Kim, Jiyeon Son, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: Introduces IGG, a benchmark of 601 tasks across 16 controllable GUI environments requiring agents to first make a hidden target visible (via scrolling, hovering, dragging, or waiting) before clicking it, covering seven visibility-constraint types. A human study calibrates task difficulty, exposing an unevaluated capability in existing GUI agents.

entry.title: Distributional Alignment of LLMs and Its Generalization Properties

author.name: Nelson Jo

entry.summary: This work studies how to align LLM output distributions with human reference distributions for behavior-simulation tasks such as survey modeling, and how such alignment generalizes. Using two large-scale benchmarks, it finds alignment is achievable and generalizes to unseen in-domain questions, while cross-topic generalization depends on topic relationships.

entry.title: Rethinking Representation Geometry in Supervised Contrastive Learning under Long-Tailed Data

author.name: Joonhyeok Jeong, Jy-yong Sohn, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical framework showing that supervised contrastive objectives and their balanced variants fail to form a regular simplex at the optimum under long-tailed data because they remain sample-count dependent. Motivated by this, it introduces structural balancing that removes this dependence.

entry.title: Uni-Stream: A Unified Streaming Speech Language Model for Speech Synthesis and Recognition

author.name: Xuan Shi, Chang Zeng, Tiantian Feng, Ye Zhang, Jun Liu, Shih-Heng Wang, Lie Lu, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: Introduces Uni-Stream, a unified streaming speech language model built on compact pretrained speech models that handles both speech recognition and synthesis in an interleaved text-speech streaming format, achieving performance comparable to task-specific models via two-stage training. The authors also develop a data annotation pipeline for streaming training and plan to release transcriptions with word-level timestamps.

entry.title: Tokamak-SI: Interpreting Tokamak Discharges with Labeled Catalogs

author.name: Nathaniel Chen, Alvin Garcia, Ricardo Shousha, Jalal Butt, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Egemen Kolemen

entry.summary: Tokamak-SI is a unified, scalable, time-aligned labeled dataset consolidating earlier task-specific labeling efforts for DIII-D tokamak discharges, covering phenomena such as confinement, detachment, Alfven eigenmodes, ELMs, sawteeth, tearing modes, and resistive wall modes. Models trained on it match or beat earlier specialized detectors for AE, ELM, and TM detection. The dataset is intended to enable task-specific benchmarking and physics-searchable analysis of plasma discharges.

entry.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis

author.name: Dennis Heijmans, H. \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Bilgi, Rui Wang, Kubilay Atasu

entry.summary: This work presents the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks used in anti-money laundering, using node-edge incidence matrices and adapting projected gradient descent and randomized block coordinate descent to optimize structural perturbations. It exposes robustness gaps in recently proposed multigraph AML architectures. This matters given adversaries actively manipulate transaction patterns to evade detection.

entry.title: PRISM: Promoting Sampling Diversity of Large Language Models with Implicit Stochastic Modulation

author.name: Qixin Xu, Zihan Zhu, Xiaojiang Liu, Bohan Lyu

entry.summary: PRISM addresses mode collapse in LLMs by internalizing diversity as a model capability rather than an inference-time trick, combining submodular curation of diverse-yet-correct multi-teacher solutions with stochastic embedding modulation. This aims to sustain self-evolution and continual learning by making rare, stronger solutions reachable through sampling.

entry.title: Correct but Unselectable: The Hidden Interface Tax in Multi-Candidate Reasoning

author.name: Qianli Ma, Zhiqing Tang, Fanshuai Meng, Zhi Yao, Hanshuai Cui, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: The paper identifies the hidden interface tax: in generate-then-rerank reasoning, a correct candidate may exist in the pool yet be unselectable because it is incomplete, unparseable, or misaligned with the selector's expected answer mode. It formalizes a coverage-conversion decomposition separating raw oracle coverage from selectable coverage, quantifying this overlooked bottleneck in test-time scaling.

entry.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms

author.name: Geetika, Shivani Singh Chauhan, Gauranshi Gupta, Anant Jain, Kaushik Kalyanaraman, Bapi Chatterjee

entry.summary: This paper studies combining sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) with Muon, the orthogonalized-momentum optimizer increasingly used for LLM training, and provides the first theoretical and empirical treatment of SAM behavior under heavy-tailed gradient noise. It addresses SAM's prohibitive extra-gradient cost in this setting.

entry.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer

author.name: Danilo Vucetic, Mohamad H. Danesh, Florence Clerc, Hsiu-Chin Lin, Jonathan Tremblay

entry.summary: This work empirically characterizes how regularization in RL affects sim-to-real transfer for robotics, deriving Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a regularized algorithm with strong robustness guarantees. Experiments on continuous-control benchmarks challenge the de facto reliance on weakly regularized PPO in sim-to-real pipelines.

entry.title: Semantically Rich, Metrically Affect-Blind: A Geometric Blind Spot in Modern Text Embedders

author.name: Mahdi Naser Moghadasi

entry.summary: The paper reports a systematic dissociation in text embedders: sentiment is nearly perfectly decodable from embeddings via linear probes (up to 91.3% accuracy, including on Qwen3-Embedding-4B, an existing model), yet almost absent from the cosine-similarity metric itself. Since retrieval, clustering, deduplication, and RAG rely on the metric, these systems are effectively blind to sentiment structure they encode.

entry.title: Sparse Bayesian Neural Networks via Sticky Piecewise Deterministic Markov Processes

author.name: August Arnstad, Geir Olve Storvik, Filippo Pagani, Leiv R{\o}nneberg

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that piecewise deterministic Markov process Monte Carlo methods can sample spike-and-slab posteriors of Bayesian neural networks asymptotically exactly when numerically constructed rate bounds hold, embedding sparsity via the prior rather than train-then-prune. This tackles the notoriously hard MCMC problem for BNNs with a rigorous sampling guarantee. It bridges modern PDMP samplers and structured BNN sparsity.

entry.title: Conceptizer: Next-Token Prediction Is Not All You Need

author.name: Haoran Zheng, Chen Shani

entry.summary: Conceptizer extends next-token prediction with a meaning-level reward using a fixed, model-agnostic vocabulary of about 9,000 concepts built from contextual synonyms; each next-token distribution is mapped to a concept distribution and reward is shared across possible wordings of the same meaning. Applied to 3 model families at 1B-8B parameters, it achieves the lowest held-out NTP perplexity without adding parameters.

entry.title: Distill, Debate, Discover: Grounding Multi-Agent Research Ideation in Graph-Distilled Insights

author.name: Qianran Ma, Muxin Liu, Grace Kim, Xiao Liang, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: Introduces InsightAgents, a framework where multi-agent debate for research ideation is grounded in expertise distilled from graphs of related papers, capturing evolving approaches, assumptions, and open challenges. Aims to give debate agents distinct, literature-grounded perspectives.

entry.title: StateWise: Teaching Language Models to Track and Obey Evolving Constraints in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Samarth Varshney, Ritu Yadav

entry.summary: StateWise addresses two failure modes in multi-turn instruction following: persistence failures (active constraints stop being honored) and relapse (withdrawn constraints keep being enacted). The approach teaches a single LLM to maintain its own typed, revisable constraint state with tombstones for revoked constraints, verified by executable checkers that also provide free ground-truth states for fine-tuning. This removes the need for external specification ledgers.

entry.title: RefinedGAW: A Refined German Academic Web Dataset

author.name: Maximilian Idahl, Oleh Astappiev, Benedikt Droste, Robert Scholz, Bj\"orn Pl\"uster, Jan Philipp Harries, Robert J\"aschke, Wolfgang Nejdl

entry.summary: RefinedGAW is a processed, annotated German text resource from 26 semi-annual crawls of the German Academic Web totaling 122 million documents and 314 billion tokens, with full crawl history. Its 87.6 billion academic-research tokens exceed the German subsets of FineWeb2 and FinePDFs despite far smaller raw size, with substantial educational, math-heavy, and low-commercial content.

entry.title: BehaviorMem: Building and Evaluating User Memory from Real-World E-Commerce Behavior Streams

author.name: Sizhe Wang, Xinghao Fang, Rui Qiu, Zhenjia Ma, Dagui Chen, Kun Kuang, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: Introduces BehaviorMem, a benchmark and method for building user memory from real-world e-commerce interaction logs, jointly supporting and separately evaluating remembering concrete evidence versus inferring underlying needs and preferences. It addresses the limitation that existing memory work focuses on language-based interactions with little real behavioral data. Relevant to personalization systems that must reason over implicit signals.

entry.title: The Lay of the Land in Idiom-Translation Quality Estimation

author.name: Malik Marmonier, Beno\^it Sagot, Rachel Bawden

entry.summary: The authors build the first parallel dataset pairing idiom-bearing English sentences with literal and idiomatic translations across nine languages, extended into multi-sentence segments along a graded literality continuum. They benchmark eleven QE metrics and ten LLM judges, finding most systems fail to reliably rank idiomatic renderings above faulty literal translations.

entry.title: Can Language Models Learn While They Think? Testing Gradient Adaptation Across Architectures

author.name: Surya Saka

entry.summary: Measures dynamic evaluation (test-time gradient steps on the text being read) across architectures, finding softmax-attention models (Qwen3, Gemma-4-E4B) lose 5-8% next-token loss over a document and beat the same frozen model given full 32k context, while hybrid Gated-DeltaNet models gain under 1% because linear-attention blocks impede adaptation.

entry.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to System 1 Models: Fast Decision-Making Beyond LLMS

author.name: Haggai Roitman

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of System 1 decision models: architectures that map input directly to a typed, structured decision in a single forward pass for routing, gating, scoring, and classification at sub-second latency. It proposes a five-family taxonomy spanning encoder classifiers, reward models, non-autoregressive decision engines, contrastive decision models, and extraction models with practitioner-oriented guidance.

entry.title: One Mean Log-Mel Vector per Phoneme: Simple and Fast Text Injection for Speech Recognition

author.name: Albert Zeyer, Davyd Naveriani, Dorian Koch, Ralf Schl\"uter, Hermann Ney

entry.summary: The paper replaces a frozen neural TTS model in text-injection ASR training with a trivial lookup table of mean log-mel vectors per phoneme with randomized durations, making training 1.8x faster at comparable word error rates. The resulting system achieves 1.36/2.90/1.52/3.24 percent WER on LibriSpeech, reportedly state-of-the-art using only LibriSpeech paired audio.

entry.title: AGQ: Action-Guided Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xuhong Qiu, Zhuoyu Wu, Qiawei Zheng, Wenhui Ou, Wenqi Fang, Rapha\"{e}l C. -W. Phan

entry.summary: Proposes Action-Guided Quantization for vision-language-action robot models, allocating per-matrix bitwidths by combining action sensitivity with a measured proxy for weight recovery cost under storage budgets. Per-channel calibration, uniform within-matrix bitwidths, bit-dependent grouped lossless coding, and block-wise recovery preserve task performance on memory-constrained onboard platforms.

entry.title: Explicit Frictional Contact Modeling in Neural Garment Simulation

author.name: Thanh-Nguyen Truong, Vu-Hoang Tran, Ching-Chun Huang

entry.summary: This work identifies that graph-network garment simulators leave body-garment friction implicit and unresponsive to friction coefficients, and proposes a Modular Contact Operator applied after prediction to resolve per-contact Coulomb stick-slip conditions explicitly at inference. This brings optimization-solver-grade friction control to fast neural garment simulation. It matters for realistic cloth animation and embodied simulation.

entry.title: C-DFF: Concept-Level Diagnostics for Mechanism Parity in Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous Driving Perception

author.name: Danial Safaei, Siddartha Khastgir, Matthew Higgins, Jeroen Ploeg, Mohsen Alirezaei, Son Tong, Ludo Gielen

entry.summary: C-DFF is a concept-level diagnostic for checking whether an autonomous driving perception system relies on the same visual evidence in real versus synthetic images, projecting decisive evidence from the frozen system-under-test into a semantic concept space and comparing importance vectors. This addresses the validation gap where matching task outputs does not guarantee matching internal mechanisms. Directly relevant to safety-critical simulation-based certification.

entry.title: What Sketches Tell Us about LVLMs: Conventions, Grounding, and Localisation

author.name: Chaitat Utintu, Ahmed Bourouis, Arkaprabha Basu, Yi-Zhe Song

entry.summary: The paper introduces a training-free sketch probe that uses abstract line drawings to expose which visual conventions large vision-language models retain, using readouts for temporal part-construction order, attention-based grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head locus of grounding. Evaluations across nine LVLMs reveal findings about how structural rather than photometric signals are processed.

entry.title: GRASP: Group-Adaptive Hybrid RL-SFT Post-Training for Medical VQA without Reasoning Annotations

author.name: Wanqi Dong, Wanyue Dong, Jingze Ge, Mehul Motani

entry.summary: GRASP is a hybrid RL-SFT post-training method for medical visual question answering when only short answers without reasoning annotations are available. It adaptively blends supervised and GRPO-style group-relative signals to avoid SFT overfitting and the zero-gradient degeneracy of all-correct or all-wrong groups, improving OOD generalization.

entry.title: Good Rankings, Poor Choices? Rethinking Language-Only Vision-Language Model Selection

author.name: Hyuk Kwon, Jaebyeong Jeon, Hyeonseo Jang, Kibok Lee

entry.summary: This work critiques the standard evaluation protocol for language-only VLM selection, showing that ranking metrics do not directly measure the quality of the selected model. It proposes regret-based metrics (SR, ORNR) and a new method, Target-Conditioned Expected Source Regret, reframing how model selection should be assessed.

entry.title: LOCUS: Locate Once, Check Until Settled. Draft-and-Verify Visual Grounding with a Box Head and Coordinate-Token Verification

author.name: Muhammad Talha

entry.summary: LOCUS accelerates visual grounding in VLMs by using a fast regression head as a speculative drafter whose box is written as coordinate tokens and verified by the backbone via Jacobi iteration over a shared image prefix. This reaches the model's greedy coordinate-token answer in roughly one-fifth of the usual cost while preserving precision.

entry.title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying

author.name: Salma Abdel Magid, Sanghyuk Chun, Eric Slyman, Kushal Kafle, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: Proposes a proactive defense against harmful edits by DiT-based image editors such as Flux Kontext: instead of perturbations that make the editor ignore the protected reference image, the perturbation encourages the model to copy the reference, leaving it unable to follow the edit instruction. This counterintuitive strategy is shown to outperform attention-suppression defenses.

entry.title: MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting

author.name: Shuyun Wang, Shangchen Zhou, Peiqing Yang, Yuekun Dai, Xin Yu, Chen Change Loy

entry.summary: Extends MatAnyone 2 for high-resolution video matting by propagating at low resolution to find uncertain regions, then applying expensive high-resolution memory matching only where needed. This sparse, uncertainty-driven computation preserves fine details like hair while cutting cost.

entry.title: ReSight: Task-Driven Self-Improving Memory for Embodied Agents

author.name: Lirong Che, Yang Chen, Yimeng Su, Daqi Liu, Zhenyu Huang, Jiong Wang, Yuzhe Yang, Xu Cao, Chuang Wang, Jian Su, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a memory system for embodied agents that retains keyframes with spatiotemporal associations and separates raw observation evidence from extensible derived fields, allowing stored observations to be reprocessed as new task demands arise. An execution agent and coding agent interact with the memory through different interfaces under bounded budgets.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference Needs Both Reuse and Pruning

author.name: Sooyoung Kwon, Carlee Joe-Wong, Kyunghan Lee

entry.summary: Presents TRIAGE, a training-free accelerator for VLA inference on embedded robot hardware that combines KV-cache reuse and token pruning, showing through token-level analysis that the two mechanisms have complementary strengths versus the single-mechanism approach of prior methods. This addresses prefill latency from hundreds of visual tokens at every robot control step.

entry.title: ORBIT: A Modular Multi-finger Robotic Hand Platform with Rotational Finger Reconfiguration

author.name: Benito Ribadeneira, Siqi Shang, Lillian Chin

entry.summary: ORBIT is a modular robotic hand platform whose rotating knuckle mechanism lets fingers travel around a cylindrical palm, enabling finger-layout reconfiguration in under one second without disassembly. It aims to enable principled comparisons of hand morphologies for dexterous manipulation, with solid specs (1.57 rad/s finger velocity, 50 N root finger force resistance).

entry.title: JevVLA: Jev-Inspired Energy-Based Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Wei Wang, Wenqiao Zhang, Zheqi Lv, Zheng Dong, Yingjie Niu, Jiaqi Zhu, Jun Xiao, Chao Li, Yueting Zhuang

entry.summary: JevVLA is a lightweight energy-based adaptation framework for VLA policies that keeps the base policy frozen and learns a differentiable scalar energy over observations, task context, and actions to model the relative quality of action proposals, trained from execution feedback, expert corrections, or demonstrations. It unifies adaptation for both discrete candidate selection and continuous action chunking. The frozen-base design preserves pretrained capabilities while adding a reranking mechanism.

entry.title: Preemptive Instruction Following with Resumption

author.name: Zerun Liu, Lechao Cheng, Yimin Liu, Shengeng Tang, Yaxiong Wang, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: This work introduces the PIFR benchmark for embodied navigation under runtime task preemption: an agent must finish its current atomic task, execute an inserted higher-priority instruction, and resume the original sequence from the changed environment state. It covers single, repeated, and nested interruptions with stage-specific metrics. Evaluations show recovery performance varies substantially across interruption conditions.

entry.title: On the Error Analysis of Triangular Transport Maps for Conditional Generation via MMD-based Objectives

author.name: Michele Martino, Bamdad Hosseini, Amir Sagiv, Amirhossein Taghvaei

entry.summary: Provides theoretical guarantees for conditional generative models parameterized by triangular transport maps, analyzing minimum divergence estimators via MMD-based objectives and average conditional estimation error. Notably, it shows that the common practice of minimizing joint MMD can fail to recover the true conditionals, clarifying when joint fitting suffices and when it does not.

entry.title: Intrinsic Information Rates of Summaries in Simulation-Based Inference

author.name: Vansh Bansal, Pradip Sharma Poudel, James G. Scott

entry.summary: The paper models neural summaries in simulation-based inference as lossy channels and quantifies their information budget via mutual information I(Y;S). It proves that the required budget grows unboundedly as the posterior concentrates, even when fixed-dimensional sufficient statistics exist, clarifying fundamental limits of summary-based SBI.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Output Control Should be the Focus of Machine Unlearning

author.name: Yahya Alkhatib, Yuyang Xiao, Wee Peng Tay

entry.summary: This position paper argues that machine unlearning research is misaligned by targeting parameter-space indistinguishability from retrained models, and instead should prioritize statistically guaranteed control of model outputs, which maps directly to user-relevant harms like bias, toxicity, hallucination, and sensitive information leakage. The authors contend output-space control with guarantees scales better and is the operationally meaningful notion of unlearning. It could reshape how the unlearning field sets its objectives.

entry.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents

author.name: Hariharan Devarajan, Neeraj Rajesh, Aniruddha Marathe, Nikoli Dryden, Kin Ng, Michela Taufer

entry.summary: Phronix is a learning paradigm for LLM-based agent harnesses in scientific computing that acquires, validates, and refines reusable capabilities from the agent's own executions, rather than relying solely on manually written skills and curated memory. It uses a predictor-validator-corrector loop with MCP tools to build a library of validated solutions that can be retained and reused across tasks. This addresses a key limitation in agent design: repeatedly rediscovering solutions instead of accumulating operational knowledge over time.

entry.title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation

author.name: Amit Sarker, Moumita Choudhury, Saaduddin Mahmud, Shlomo Zilberstein

entry.summary: The paper studies whether LLM agents can build useful trust estimates from repeated multi-party, multi-issue negotiations and use them to improve outcomes, including against a covert saboteur. It identifies a trust-agreement gap: accurate trust estimates alone do not guarantee that agents will reach or enforce agreements.

entry.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods

author.name: Zimu Wang, Xiaobo Wang, Siyu Ye, Jiaqi Li, Silin Chen, Yuling Shi, Ruobing Wang, Jingjing Zhang, Chaofan Wang, Kai Wu, Mengnan Qi, Kai Cai, Xiaodong Gu, Zilong Zheng

entry.summary: RSIHub is an open-source framework providing shared infrastructure for agent self-improvement methods, supplying execution, evaluation, recovery, and lineage while researchers define evolution policies as composable recipes. The authors instantiate four existing methods (AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, GEPA) without modifying the core, enabling fair comparison. It reduces duplicated experimental machinery in the fast-moving agent-evolution space.

entry.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents

author.name: Shen Liu, Ze Zhou, Zhenguo Xu, Shaopu Wang, Yike Gao, Chunlei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that lets recursive LLM agents handle low-level action grounding with a lightweight 1.7B selector instead of repeatedly invoking the full large model. It retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to admissible actions, and defers unresolved subtasks back to the original agent.

entry.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency

author.name: Yuhua Jiang, Chang Xu, Feifei Gao, Li Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes HarnessMM, which improves agent harness token efficiency via guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement: Executable Decision Graphs store resolved actions with guards, and a controller at the model-tool boundary reuses them to replace redundant reasoning callbacks while actor weights stay fixed. Companion harness configurations are iteratively refined from training feedback.

entry.title: Astro2Method: Benchmarking LLMs on Machine Learning Method Selection in Astronomy

author.name: Xingzhong Fan, Hangfeng He, Fatemeh Nargesian

entry.summary: Astro2Method is a 500-question, expert-reviewed benchmark testing whether LLMs can select appropriate ML methods for astronomy problems, drawn from 346 papers from 2024-2026. LLMs score above 87% on easy questions but only around 59-65% on hard ones, and RAG and most agent approaches do not close the gap.

entry.title: OpenHome: From Perception to Insight in Smart-Home Camera Videos

author.name: Xianglong Wang, Neil Rodrigues, Pei Guo, Yiru Fang, Kevin Beussman, Shuyang Wang, Jingzhi Wang, Liangju Li, Shunyao Xu, Zhongwei Cheng, Wei Li, Lin Chen

entry.summary: OpenHome is a visual-only, four-option multiple-choice benchmark evaluating how well VLMs understand smart-home camera footage, which differs from curated web videos in lacking narration, and featuring varied angles, lighting, and sparse signals. It fills a gap in existing VLM benchmarks for this consumer domain.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Backdoor Attacks on Code Models via Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring

author.name: Yu-Yu Lee, Ming-Feng Tsai, Tomohiro Morikawa, Chun-I Fan

entry.summary: This paper proposes TNCS, a method for selecting a minimal set of poisoning samples to mount backdoor attacks on pre-trained code models. It scores candidate samples by comparing model outputs on triggered inputs against trigger-neutralized counterfactuals, isolating the trigger's contribution. The work highlights a security vulnerability in code-generating models that the community needs to defend against.

entry.title: Clean-label Poisoning Attack and Defense Game for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks

author.name: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Nathan Stephenson, Mengran Xue

entry.summary: This paper studies clean-label poisoning attacks against federated learning in vehicular networks, where benign feature vectors are perturbed toward malicious extremes while preserving labels, degrading anomaly detection in Basic Safety Message classification. It proposes a feature-consistency relabeling defense and models the attack-defense interaction as a game-theoretic problem with equilibrium analysis. This matters for securing safety-critical distributed learning in dynamic vehicle topologies.

entry.title: Agreement rather than normalisation keeps depth reusable in looped language models

author.name: Ivan Viakhirev, Kirill Borodin, Maxim Abramov, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: The paper investigates why looped language models remain usable beyond their trained loop budget, testing whether loop-boundary normalization or train/inference loop agreement is responsible. Experiments on released Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B weights show that removing state normalization collapses accuracy, identifying norm growth as the failure mechanism.

entry.title: Curvature-Aware Clipping: Mitigating Bias in DPSGD via Approximate Second-Order Information

author.name: Xincheng Xu, Thilina Ranbaduge, Thierry Rakotoarivelo, David Smith

entry.summary: CA-DPSGD mitigates the geometric misalignment caused by gradient clipping bias in differentially private training by constructing a curvature-aware clipping space using approximate second-order information. It couples a rectified curvature estimator with an anisotropic noise mechanism to preserve privacy guarantees while improving utility.

entry.title: When to Trust Memory: Retrieval-Guided Probabilistic Spatiotemporal Forecasting under Distribution Shift

author.name: Haochen Lv, Jianhao Zhang, Zhichen Lei, Yang Jiang, Xiaowei Mao, Shengnan Guo, Youfang Lin, Huaiyu Wan

entry.summary: REMIND is a retrieval-guided probabilistic framework for spatiotemporal forecasting that explicitly characterizes the degree of distribution shift and adapts prediction strategy accordingly, improving calibration and reliability. It targets the gap between distribution-shift-agnostic probabilistic forecasting and coarse shift handling in practice.

entry.title: From Parameter Rebasin to Functional Transfer Across Heterogeneous Transformers

author.name: Filippo Rinaldi, Aniello Panariello, Giacomo Salici, Simone Magistri, Angelo Porrello, Andrew D. Bagdanov, Simone Calderara

entry.summary: Ariadne is a training-free method that transfers task-specific behavior (fine-tuning updates) across heterogeneous Transformers of different depths and widths without resizing or parameter transport, by characterizing fine-tuning through activation changes at matched blocks rather than parameter-space task vectors. It aligns functional effects rather than parameter geometry.

entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning with Time-Varying Movement Costs

author.name: Andrew Jacobsen, Emmanuel Esposito, Hao Qiu, Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies strongly adaptive regret in online convex optimization when the cost of switching decisions varies over time, capturing environments where both losses and movement costs fluctuate. The authors propose a novel algorithm achieving data-dependent regret bounds over arbitrary time intervals, generalizing prior work with fixed movement costs.

entry.title: How Much Do You Trust A Dog? Quantifying Hint-Following in Reasoning Language Models

author.name: Anxin Guo, Chirag Pabbaraju, Sara Ahmadian, Kamesh Munagala, Aravindan Vijayaraghavan

entry.summary: This work quantifies sycophancy in LLMs via hint-induced answer shifts on MMLU, varying the attributed source of a hint (professor, friend, or dog) across Qwen, Gemma, and SmolLM families. It finds the influence follows a predictable exponential-tilt structure and examines whether models calibrate their hint-following to source reliability.

entry.title: State Estimation as In-context Tabular Prediction

author.name: Ayushi Jolotia, Parikshit Pareek

entry.summary: This letter reframes power system state estimation as an in-context tabular prediction task, using pretrained tabular foundation models with frozen weights where historical measurements and state estimates serve as context and a new measurement forms the query. The approach is evaluated on 14-, 30-, 33-, 70-, and 118-bus networks, outperforming weighted least squares in low-observability and bad-data scenarios, with reported errors 11 to 57 times lower per bus. It matters because it demonstrates a training-free application of tabular foundation models to a classical engineering problem.

entry.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

author.name: Panagiotis Koromilas, Eleanna Vali, Diogenis Antonopoulos, Eleni Saka, Dimitris Christofis, Nikolaos Ioannis Bountos, Konstantin Klemmer, Ioannis Papoutsis, Yannis Panagakis, Mihalis A. Nicolaou

entry.summary: This paper proves a structural limitation of geospatial location encoders trained via contrastive alignment with Earth observation imagery: any Lipschitz location encoder has intrinsic output dimension at most 2, forcing the contrastive loss above its asymptotic optimum, and joint training collapses embedding covariance to low rank. The authors reinterpret frozen image encoders as covariance regularizers and propose a method to enable multi-modality in location encoders.

entry.title: Whispering Wisely: Smart Subset Selection for ASR Fine-Tuning

author.name: Roi Yozevitch, Or Haim Anidjar

entry.summary: This paper proposes an embedding-based subset selection method to reduce the cost of fine-tuning ASR models like Whisper. Audio samples are mapped into a fixed-dimensional embedding space using Whisper's pretrained encoder, and a greedy k-center algorithm selects diverse, representative training subsets. Experiments on Hebrew and Danish show k-center selection often improves fine-tuning efficiency, making language/domain adaptation more accessible to practitioners with limited resources.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Causality Assessment (MARCA) of Individual Case Safety Reports in Pharmacovigilance

author.name: Daisy Rae Lopez, Angela Boccia, Maurizio Sessa

entry.summary: MARCA is a four-agent RAG framework using Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 to perform Naranjo-based causality assessment of drug safety reports, evaluated against a consensus expert reference of 215 FAERS cases. It measures expert agreement and differences between RAG and non-RAG scoring.

entry.title: Examining form-based linguistic productivity in people and large language models

author.name: Michael Wilson, Robert Frank

entry.summary: Compares human and LLM generalization of novel verbs from active to passive voice, finding people generalize based on abstract form even without plausible meaning, while LLMs succeed only when a meaning compatible with an existing verb is available. Suggests LLMs rely on meaning-based rather than form-based productivity.

entry.title: Beyond Prompts: A Systematic Study of LLM-Based Machine Translation Evaluators

author.name: Dmitry Popov, Roman Bokhyan, Ekaterina Enikeeva, Artem Mekhraliev, Stepan Vysotsky, Nikolay Karpachev

entry.summary: A systematic study of design choices behind LLM-based machine translation evaluators, covering instruction design, few-shot demonstrations, backbone choice, and multi-step workflows. The authors collect new expert RATE annotations on WMT24/WMT25 English-Russian data with cross-lingual transfer validation. Key findings include that instruction structure shapes evaluator behavior and that high-quality demonstrations matter more than quantity.

entry.title: Refined Assessment for Translation Evaluation: Rethinking Machine Translation Evaluation in the Era of Human-Level Systems

author.name: Dmitry Popov, Vladislav Negodin, Ekaterina Enikeeva, Iana Matrosova, Nikolay Karpachev, Max Ryabinin

entry.summary: This paper critiques gold-standard machine translation evaluation methodologies (MQM and ESA), arguing they struggle to detect subtle errors as MT systems approach human-level quality, due to issues like annotator variability, coarse severity granularity, and accuracy bias. The authors release a new high-quality dataset of professional linguist evaluations for English-Russian WMT24 translations, showing that expert assessments without time pressure differ substantially from standard evaluations. They propose a refined assessment framework to enable consistent, rich annotation.

entry.title: Write What Matters: Disentangling Token Selection from Slot Allocation in Recurrent Memory

author.name: Chen Chen, Rui Cheng

entry.summary: Factorized Write Routing (FWR) separates the decision of whether to store a token in a recurrent memory from how many memory slots to update, allowing selective writes with token-adaptive slot counts. Experiments across ten seeds on synthetic long-context fact-query tasks reveal density-dependent effects of selective writing.

entry.title: DecisionTraceBench: Tracking Decision-Critical Information in Multi-Party Spoken Conversations

author.name: Wenchao Du, Fangxin Shang, Long Wu, Runze Cui, Qing Yang, Yehui Yang

entry.summary: Introduces DecisionTraceBench, a speech state-tracking benchmark for Decision-Critical Information State Tracking (DCIST) in multi-party spoken conversations, evaluated on Chinese financial dialogues with two to four speakers. It jointly assesses decision event sequences, speaker attribution, scope, and temporal evidence using trajectory-level F1, addressing gaps left by transcription-focused speech benchmarks. This matters for reliable speech understanding in high-stakes domains like finance where information evolves across speakers.

entry.title: Useful Diversity or Hallucinated Variety? Persona-Conditioned Synthetic Query Generation for E-Commerce Search

author.name: Filippos Ventirozos, Tom Armitage, Mahmoud Oshagh, Peter A. Appleby, Matthew Shardlow

entry.summary: Studies persona-conditioned synthetic query generation for cold-start e-commerce search, producing 118,098 pairs from 6 LLMs and 9 persona prompt families on a UK automotive schema, validated against human-annotated and production queries. It shows the IPIP personality bundle improves parser F1 across matched contrasts and that syntax conditioning best aligns generations with real traffic, introducing an alignment sKL divergence measure. Provides rigorous guidance on when synthetic diversity is faithful versus hallucinated.

entry.title: MANTIS: Multi-Axis News Transformations for Instance-Wise Stress Testing and Worst-Case Training in Fake News Detection

author.name: Dexin Liu, Fan Yang, Zimu Wang, Xunfei Zhu, Bolin Ren, Bingyan Zhang, Wei Wang, Qi Chen

entry.summary: MANTIS-Bench pairs original news with rewrites varying writing style, emotional expression, and dissemination framing to stress-test fake news detectors, and MANTIS provides an instance-adaptive adversarial framework for worst-case training with zero inference-time overhead. The approach reframes defense around fact-invariant credibility assessment rather than superficial stylistic cues.

entry.title: LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers

author.name: Feichen Song, Boyi Zeng, Yiqin Hao, Shixiang Song, He Li, Yizhou Yang, Zitong Wang, Yifan Liu, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: LoopFold reduces the decoding latency of looped transformers by folding computation at multiple recurrent depths into parallel batches, using a lightweight predictor to estimate inputs to later loops so they can start early. This addresses diminishing returns of prior parallel-loop approaches at large depths.

entry.title: Not One Belief: Answer Payloads, Persistence, and Dissociated Confidence Signals in Conversational Question Answering

author.name: Duc-Vinh Tran

entry.summary: Disentangles speech acts from answer payloads in conversational QA follow-ups, showing answers change only when users supply an answer string, not from re-asking or agreement alone. Compares four confidence signals (verbalized confidence, likelihood, hidden-state probe, P(True)) and finds they dissociate, with a frozen probe tracking persistence rather than truth on Qwen2.5-7B.

entry.title: Jointly Modeling Preferences and Imperfect Decision-Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Axel Abels, Elias Fern\'andez Domingos, Tom Lenaerts

entry.summary: This work asks whether preferences LLMs express in elicitation tasks predict their strategic behavior, introducing the Preference-Behavior Model (PBM) grounded in utility theory. It combines a preference component with a boundedly-rational decision model to test consistency across behavioral-economic elicitation and strategic game settings.

entry.title: AdaTutor: Adaptive Tutoring through Pedagogical Strategy Selection

author.name: Rajeev Bhatt Ambati, Shashank Srivastava, Snigdha Chaturvedi

entry.summary: The authors introduce Comparative Pedagogical Supervision (CPS), a training framework that teaches tutoring systems to select among pedagogical strategies when responding to student errors. On math and science reasoning datasets, CPS-trained tutors outperform the strongest fixed-strategy baselines after five tutoring turns, transfer across datasets, and their strategy selections can guide separate API-based tutors.

entry.title: GPDPO: Learning from Reward Conflicts via Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization

author.name: Zixuan Xu, Haoxuan Chen, Jiangxin Sun, Jian-Fang Hu

entry.summary: GPDPO is a multi-reward policy optimization method for aligning LLMs with diverse objectives that recovers pairwise supervision from conflicting reward signals using Pareto-dominance relations among sampled responses. It exploits relational information across rollouts that existing conflict-handling approaches (reweighting, gradient coordination, rollout filtering) discard.

entry.title: ProtoEEG: Structured Prototype Alignment for EEG Visual Decoding

author.name: Kieren Yu, Chang Huang, Ziyang Liu, Kaishun Wu

entry.summary: Reformulates EEG-to-image alignment as soft composition over a shared learnable codebook of 64 prototypes, with a trainable EEG encoder and a frozen visual teacher producing assignment distributions over the same prototypes. This structured reconstruction avoids forcing EEG to match dense image embeddings that contain texture and pose details EEG cannot capture, while giving an interpretable account of the visual factors behind predictions.

entry.title: Compression of Vision Foundation Models for Retinal OCT via Growing-Neural-Gas Codebooks and Graph-Guided Masked Image Modeling

author.name: Ali Yavari, Tilman Schmoll, Rainer A. Leitgeb, Wolfgang Drexler, Thomas Schlegl

entry.summary: The authors propose a topology-aware compression framework that distills large vision foundation models for retinal OCT into smaller networks using Growing Neural Gas codebook learning and graph-distance soft cross-entropy supervision for masked image modeling. Pretraining on 383 public Duke iAMD volumes shows how much downstream clinical utility survives aggressive model compression. This matters for enabling point-of-care deployment of retinal AI in resource-constrained clinics.

entry.title: CADonatello: Towards Real-World Multi-Part 3D CAD Reconstruction

author.name: Ahmet Serdar Karadeniz, Dimitrios Mallis, Parsa Akbari Chianeh, Kseniya Cherenkova, Anis Kacem, Djamila Aouada

entry.summary: This paper introduces a part-aware framework for reconstructing parametric CAD models from real-world 3D scans, addressing the gap between clean single-part benchmark datasets and noisy multi-part real-world objects. It first decomposes geometry using a foundation-scale 3D part segmentation model, then reconstructs each component. This matters for industrial design and reverse-engineering workflows where scanned objects rarely match sanitized training data.

entry.title: RelateGS: Reliable Semantic and Relational Evidence for 3D Scene Understanding with Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Seongjun Choi, Sangyoun Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces RelateGS, a structured language-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting representation that improves language-driven 3D visual grounding by refining semantic and relational evidence. The key insight is that multi-view semantic aggregation can incorporate weak or unreliable observations, and object relations may be under-observed along the camera trajectory, so the method selectively suppresses unreliable evidence to enable more reliable target disambiguation.

entry.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models

author.name: Guile Wu, Shuangzhi Li, Xingxin Chen, Chengjie Huang, Sam Hosseini, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: TurboWAM targets the high inference latency of world action models in robot policy learning by selectively aggregating structured world representations conditioned on action predictions, rather than using all video world model layers uniformly. This reduces redundant computation while improving representation utilization for real-time deployment.

entry.title: LegoOcc++: Towards Consistent Open-Vocabulary 3D Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Changqing Zhou, Yueru Luo, Han Zhang, Zeyu Jiang, Changhao Chen

entry.summary: LegoOcc++ addresses open-vocabulary 3D occupancy prediction for embodied agents, focusing on challenging indoor scenes with occlusion and long-tailed semantics. It uses a geometry-only supervision setting (binary occupancy labels only) built on Language-Embedded Gaussians, with an opacity-aware Poisson-based Gaussian-to-Occupancy formulation to reduce reliance on expensive voxel-level semantic annotation. This lowers annotation cost while extending 3D scene understanding beyond fixed category taxonomies.

entry.title: Robust Single-Parameter Point Cloud Registration using Truncated Lp Functions

author.name: Seong Hun Lee, Patrick Vandewalle, Javier Civera

entry.summary: Introduces TLP, a point cloud registration method using truncated Lp functions with a single tunable parameter to prioritize correspondences, select hypotheses, and refine the final model. GPU parallelization enables registration from thousands of correspondences in under a second, handling high outlier rates common in real 3D feature matching.

entry.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Yihao Hu, Yitong Lin, Pan Wang, Zhihao Wen, Hang Wang, Yiwen Zhao, Deyuan Liu, Yutong Li, Mingda Wan, Yuchen Mao, Tao Lin

entry.summary: This paper identifies an interface lock-in problem in training spatial vision-language models: optimizing for one output readout (e.g., categorical object relations) does not transfer to other readouts like metric distance estimation, and can even degrade them. ChronoReplay addresses this by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes while preserving source-native targets and balancing supervision across task families. A single checkpoint reportedly improves performance on multiple spatial benchmarks including OVO-S-Bench and OST-Bench.

entry.title: Supervising the Visible State: Separating Representation from View Selection in Streaming Video

author.name: Yihao Hu, Pan Wang, Yitong Lin, Zhihao Wen, Deyuan Liu, Hang Wang, Mingda Wan, Yiwen Zhao, Yutong Li, Yuchen Mao, Tao Lin

entry.summary: The paper identifies state under-specification in streaming video understanding, where identical labels across different event histories leave order, accumulation, and relations unconstrained. It proposes Visible-State Supervision with source-grounded probes plus Test-Time Causal View Search, improving OVO-Bench especially on hallucination detection while staying comparable on StreamingBench.

entry.title: DriveUniTok: A Unified Multimodal Tokenizer for Driving World-Action Models

author.name: Jingbo Xu, Hanchao Leng, JiaHui Huang, Hanbing Li, Jingwei Zhao, Kuiyuan Yang, Chen Gao, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Yong Li
