Addresses whether direct probabilistic decision structure actually reduces order-based selection bias in multi-option tasks.

entry.title: Whispers from the Neighbors: Rethinking Caption Consensus as Inference-Time Evidence for Vision-Language Retrieval

author.name: Khang Nhat Hoang Vo, Belal Shoer, Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri

entry.summary: This paper shows that consulting an image's neighboring captions at inference time improves text-to-image retrieval, but the magnitude depends critically on annotation provenance: gains of 3.4 to 16.8 R@1 points when captions share annotators with queries, dropping to about a point from a different annotation source. It reframes caption consensus as inference-time evidence with careful attribution of where the gains come from.

entry.title: EKT-Router: Expert-Evidence Alignment for Embodied Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weilin Ruan, Yingjie Xu, Yangkai Wei, Bohan Zhou, Shuaibo Li, Harold Haodong Chen, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng

entry.summary: EKT-Router jointly selects a capability expert (General, Spatial Reasoning, or Spatiotemporal), optional knowledge, and perceptual tools for embodied vision-language models answering questions from partial observations. It scores complete expert-evidence routes under a call budget using outcome-derived signatures and verifies acquired evidence with a packet verifier.

entry.title: Evaluating Visual Language Models on Visual Grounding for Visually Impaired People

author.name: Fairooz Azim, Lydia Achour, Claudia Borg, Lina Rojas-Barahona

entry.summary: Evaluates open-source vision-language models on visual grounding in VQA using the VizWiz-VQA-Grounding dataset of real images taken by visually impaired users, framing grounding as a trust and safety requirement in assistive settings. Proposes VG-SHAP, extending SHAP-based explanations to quantify grounding behavior in VLMs.

entry.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch

author.name: Callen MacPhee, Yiming Zhou, Bahram Jalali

entry.summary: MoViD is a physics-inspired motion estimation algorithm that treats video as optical time-stretch signals, drawing on principles from ultrafast photonic time-stretch acquisition to improve real-time motion detection in complex scenes. It aims to avoid the spatial-resolution sacrifices of background subtraction, frame differencing, and optical flow. The cross-disciplinary framing could influence robotics, autonomous driving, and video compression applications.

entry.title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding

author.name: Quang-Trung Truong, Thanh-Nghia Nguyen, Phu-Phong Vo, Jaeyeon Kim, Cheng Chen, Jie Zhang, Binh-Son Hua, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Ivor Tsang, Sai-Kit Yeung

entry.summary: The authors introduce a marine video-text dataset with 2,000 richly annotated video-text pairs (13 attributes, up to four objects per scene) across diverse lighting, times of day, and 7 countries, from which 16,080 video-question-answer instances are generated. It targets fine-grained, motion-aware understanding of complex in-the-wild marine environments. The resource enables applications in ocean ecology monitoring and marine robotics.

entry.title: Tracking Is Not Sensing: Artifact-Aware Thermal Video Respiration Estimation in Head-Free Marmosets

author.name: Penghao Wang, Sen Yang, Fenghua Xie, He Wang, Xindong Song

entry.summary: This paper presents artifact-aware estimation of respiratory rate from thermal video in head-free marmosets, enabling noncontact physiological monitoring where weak breathing cues are corrupted by head motion and fur. It supports neuroscience research linking behavior, internal state, and neural activity without contact sensor burden. The title highlights the key insight that tracking the animal is not the same as sensing its physiology.

entry.title: Scalable Unrolled Chains for MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Emiljo M\"ehillaj, Ender Konukoglu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a memory-efficient training framework for unrolled variational networks in accelerated MRI reconstruction, updating randomly sampled cascades while propagating supervision via an activation-light backward pass. A time-conditioned shared network keeps parameter count independent of chain length. This decouples training memory from chain depth, enabling deeper unrolled architectures.

entry.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yiyuan Yao, Xinpeng Ding, Minglei Chen, Fei Gao, Lihuo He, Jie Yuan, Aijun Li, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: The authors identify instruction-stage insensitivity in existing explainability methods for vision-language navigation, where explanations fail to distinguish evidence across navigation stages. They propose a stage-aware attribution framework that constructs action-conditioned temporal instruction-visual attributions across historical and current observations.

entry.title: CropReward: A Human-Preference Benchmark and Reward Model for Aesthetic Image Cropping

author.name: Xiangfei Sheng, Xiaofeng Pan, Leida Li, Qian Zhang, Biao Wang, Johan Wagemans, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: This paper tackles the reliability of evaluation in aesthetic image cropping (AIC), showing that widely used geometry-based metrics like IoU and aesthetic-assessment models poorly reflect human preferences. The authors build a human-preference benchmark (CropBenchmark/CropReward) covering methods from specialized vision models to multimodal LLMs, and train a reward model aligned with human judgments. This provides a better signal both for benchmarking AIC systems and for reward-guided optimization.

entry.title: Learning Discriminative Prototypes via Boundary Repulsion MixUp for Object Re-Identification

author.name: Athena Psalta, Vasileios Tsironis, Konstantinos Karantzalos

entry.summary: PBR-ReID represents each identity with a learnable prototype optimized alongside a DINOv3 backbone, using the prototype similarity matrix to identify confusable identities. Boundary Repulsion MixUp then applies geometry-aware regularization at the hardest inter-class decision boundaries to improve re-identification embeddings.

entry.title: Recursive CLIP: Vision-Language Distillation with Looped Transformer Blocks

author.name: Szymon Mazurek, Alberto Presta, Micha{\l} Byra

entry.summary: This paper studies how far parameter sharing can be pushed in contrastive vision-language models by reusing a small set of N transformer blocks M times per forward pass, with N times M held fixed to match standard ViT-B depth. The authors introduce two families: rCLIP with a recursive vision encoder and r-squared CLIP with recurrence in both vision and text encoders, trained under direct and distillation settings. The work probes whether CLIP's transferable capabilities survive aggressive recurrence-based parameter reduction.

entry.title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts

author.name: Gabriel Adineera, Jinoh Kim

entry.summary: SynerNet learns novel visual concepts in pre-trained vision-language models by anchoring discriminative visual evidence to concept-specific name embeddings exposed to compatible linguistic contexts, with difficulty-aware processing and adaptive objective weighting. It reports 74.35% mean 16-shot accuracy across four VISTA-Beyond domains.

entry.title: CoDeRNet: Selective Cross-Task Routing under Heterogeneous Supervision for Change Detection and Captioning

author.name: Eunki Cho, Hyeon Bae Kim, Seong Tae Kim

entry.summary: CoDeRNet reformulates joint change detection and captioning in remote sensing as selective information routing between heterogeneous task branches, deciding when and what to communicate given differing supervision granularity. It targets uneven reliability across tasks and spatial locations that shared-representation unified models mishandle.

entry.title: DUET4D: Self-Corrective Coupled Guidance for Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Beizhen Zhao, Nanjie Yao, Boyi Fu, Qingsong Yan, Haofan Ren, Kaiyong Zhao, Hao Wang

entry.summary: DUET4D tackles sparse-view 4D Gaussian splatting by using a self-corrective coupled guidance framework where the 4D representation steers generative priors to produce spatio-temporally consistent supervision. It avoids redundant primitives and floating artifacts that arise from naively absorbing uncertain generative outputs into Gaussian optimization.

entry.title: Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition

author.name: Junze Wang, Lei Fan, Dezheng Zhang, Donglin Di, Yang Song, Sidong Liu, Cong Cong

entry.summary: The paper identifies two failure modes in test-time prompt tuning (magnitude expansion and directional drift) where noisy unlabeled objectives accumulate across steps and destabilize prompt updates. It proposes Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition (TPD), which characterizes and controls these failure modes to make test-time adaptation of large pretrained models more stable under distribution shift.

entry.title: Domain-Adapted Latent Diffusion Models for CT-to-PET Image Translation

author.name: Yann Bourd\'e, Lea Bogensperger, Arnela Hadzic, Michael Krauthammer

entry.summary: The paper proposes a domain-adapted latent diffusion framework for CT-to-PET translation that transfers natural-image priors using a modest paired dataset of 21,930 CT/PET slices, with a signed power transform to handle extreme PET intensity sparsity. It outperforms the state-of-the-art CPDM baseline, addressing PET's limited accessibility due to cost and tracer requirements.

entry.title: Reading Beyond OCR Noise: Robust Cross-Lingual RAG for Legislative Archives

author.name: Radha Krishna Deshpande, Ajoy Mondal, Akash Manna, C V Jawahar

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end framework for India's degraded, multi-script parliamentary archives that couples vision-based layout segmentation and multi-script OCR with an agentic retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. An iterative agentic loop navigates OCR noise and layout ambiguity before answering. Evaluated on a large 200,000-page corpus of historical records.

entry.title: Shared-Factor-Conditioned Diffusion for Low-Rank Tensor Recovery

author.name: Zhengyun Cheng, Guanwen Zhang, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes DiffTR, an unsupervised diffusion-based framework unifying tensor completion, denoising, and hyperspectral super-resolution via coordinate-conditioned score networks over shared tensor factors. Scalar and vector-valued outputs accommodate entries and tubes, enabling a common formulation for tabular tensors, images, and videos while separating representation learning from observation models.

entry.title: Learning Scene Coordinate Reconstruction from Unposed Images via Pose Graph Optimization

author.name: Tze Ho Elden Tse, Jizong Peng, Angela Yao

entry.summary: Integrates pose graph optimization into learning-based structure-from-motion (ACE-Zero) to refine camera poses and suppress incorrect refinements in complex scenes. Relative pose constraints are extracted from predicted scene coordinates to build pose graphs, with an uncertainty-aware optimization strategy to avoid degrading good estimates.

entry.title: SeeRF: Learning to See Beyond Fields of View via Generative Image Registration and Fusion

author.name: Xunpeng Yi, Yibing Zhang, Qinglong Yan, Yifan Lu, Han Xu, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a generative registration-then-fusion framework for multi-modal image fusion that overcomes field-of-view mismatches between sensors. It uses diffeomorphic stationary velocity field-based deformation generation with foundation-model-guided features in a coarse-to-fine pipeline to produce complete scene-level fusion results.

entry.title: Optimizing Physical Neural Networks through Device Variable Selection

author.name: Sjoerd van den Belt, Manuel Escudero, Mohamadreza Zolfagharinejad, Wilfred G. van der Wiel, Nikolaos Alachiotis

entry.summary: Treats the routing between input signals and device variables in broken-isomorphism physical neural networks as trainable parameters, optimized via a Gumbel-softmax categorical distribution. This expands device-level tunability and improves expressivity of energy-efficient physical networks with negligible inference overhead.

entry.title: Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory

author.name: Fengxin Li

entry.summary: Introduces Iris, a framework extending text-only typed decision-making (UI selection, recommendation, chart matching) to visual and hybrid candidates while preserving order invariance and exact cache reuse. The paper proves these properties hold for any per-candidate encoder and derives closed-form latency reductions.

entry.title: MMGNet: Multi-Modal 6-DoF Grasp Synthesis for Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yichuan Li, Yunfan Yu, Chi-Wing Fu, Jiangliu Wang, Yun-Hui Liu

entry.summary: Proposes MMGNet for scene-level 6-DoF grasp synthesis in cluttered scenes, combining hierarchical image-to-3D feature injection to enrich noisy point clouds with RGB cues and rotational graspness modeling that jointly predicts grasp approach direction and in-plane rotation. It addresses bottlenecks in using RGB information for scene representation and local grasp reasoning.

entry.title: An Interactive Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization Algorithm Based on Interpretable Active Preference Learning

author.name: Thomas Quadt, Boris \v{C}ule, Roy Lindelauf, Herman Monsuur, Mark Voskuijl

entry.summary: This work introduces an interpretable interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithm that uses active learning to build a tree-based preference model from pairwise comparisons, replacing typical black-box preference models. The learned model extends NSGA-II/NSGA-III survival operators, targeting high-stakes domains like healthcare and defense where transparency and accountability are required.

entry.title: Intellectual Property Protection of Hyperdimensional Computing Classifiers: Black-Box Ownership Verification via Model Watermarking

author.name: Hamed Poursiami, Farshad Soleiman, Ahmad Tahmasivand, Guojing Cong, Thomas Potok, Khaled N. Khasawneh, Kai Zeng, Maryam Parsa

entry.summary: This is the first systematic study of model watermarking for hyperdimensional computing classifiers, adapting backdoor-based watermark embedding to three prototype-learning mechanisms and evaluating across four benchmarks against neural network baselines. Error-driven classifiers like AdaptHD and OnlineHD support verification with about 1% trigger exposure and at most 0.58 percentage points of accuracy loss, with analysis of watermark robustness to model modification and replication.

entry.title: Energy-Based Fault Detection and Isolation Framework for Flat Port-Hamiltonian Mechanical Systems

author.name: Johnny Garcia, Nicolas Salguero, Naveed Iqbal, Brahim Brahmi, Ramy Rashad

entry.summary: Develops an energy-based fault detection and isolation framework using port-Hamiltonian variables and differential flatness to construct mechanical port-power residuals without a dedicated dynamic observer. The SHAPE method combines nominal power references with continuous wavelet transform scalograms for diagnosis during regulated motion.

entry.title: RoboLongR: Causally Consistent Rewards Teach Robots to Progressively Master Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Zixuan Chen, Lin Cao, Fenggang Zhang, Haotong Zhang, Yangtao Chen, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Presents an offline-to-online RL framework that learns history-dependent rewards for long-horizon manipulation, with causal consistency as the central objective: rewarded progress must be supported by execution history. Stage-shuffle supervision, recurrent memory, and two-round training connect behavior cloning to online reinforcement learning with sparse terminal feedback.

entry.title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Variable-View Robot Control

author.name: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Juntong Zhang, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Presents X-World, a framework transferring pretrained video diffusion priors into robot control via a shared action expert, using residual cross-view attention to support one to three camera views, layer-aligned Q-Former aggregation, and dataset-specific modules bridging heterogeneous state/action interfaces. Training decouples video adaptation from action-only pretraining by freezing components.

entry.title: ThinkLocoManip: A Whole-Body Control Agentic Harness for Legged Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Nuo Chen, Shizeng Zhang, Yujie Yang, Jinghong Wang, Zhenyang Qu, Xiao-Ming Wu, Yunfei Guo, Zhongwen Lu, Haojie Liu, Chunpeng Lu, Qiao Sun, Xueyi Zhang, Jiangwei Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes ThinkLocoManip, an agentic harness for legged loco-manipulation that interleaves reasoning and acting, continuously observing outcomes and adapting strategy for complex long-horizon tasks in large environments. It orchestrates specialized tools for perception, navigation, manipulation, and locomotion, departing from direct action generation or plan-then-act paradigms.

entry.title: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving

author.name: Leandro Parada, Kevin Yu, Panagiotis Angeloudis

entry.summary: IntNet is a MARL framework for cooperative autonomous driving that transmits vehicle intent and adaptively schedules communication in a unified end-to-end paradigm, addressing non-stationarity and partial observability in safety-critical scenarios. It includes an observation prediction module and jointly optimizes all components for safe coordination. It is relevant to the growing intersection of V2X communication and learned driving policies.

entry.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent

author.name: Kordel Kade France

entry.summary: This paper applies the WWII-era German tank problem estimator to chemical sensor readings from a small robot, producing estimates of peak odor-plume concentration to answer whether the robot has reached the odor source in conditions where gradients flatten and turbulence makes signals intermittent. It is a clever transfer of a classical order-statistics estimator to olfactory navigation termination. The approach is lightweight and suited to small robots with limited positioning accuracy.

entry.title: Enhancing Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Motion Planning via Task Decomposition

author.name: Yuanzhi He, Victor Romero-Cano, Jiayu Xu, Juan David Hern\'andez, Gualtiero Colombo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a DRL task-decomposition framework combining transfer learning, which transfers only first-layer critic parameters across structurally related tasks, with reward redesign that stages sub-objectives for obstacle-rich manipulation. This improves learning efficiency and robustness where DRL policies typically converge slowly. It is a pragmatic recipe for simulation-trained motion planning policies.

entry.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints

author.name: Aakash Khandelwal, Ranjan Mukherjee

entry.summary: Addresses nonprehensile robotic catching via virtual nonholonomic constraints, controlling the end-effector motion directly in terms of the object's states before contact. This avoids object trajectory prediction and time-varying trajectory generation, and a single VNHC depending only on desired catching height can catch objects with minimal relative normal velocity at contact.

entry.title: How Much Graph Is Too Much? Graph Construction and Exposure in Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Saj Maru, Qiyu Han, Krishna Mamidala

entry.summary: A diagnostic study asking whether graph neighbors actually add predictive value beyond a node's own history in spatio-temporal GNNs, tested on US unemployment, traffic speed, and electricity demand benchmarks. It disentangles graph construction from graph exposure (how messages enter the temporal model) using randomized graph controls and history-only GRU baselines.

entry.title: TGAge: A Phenotypic Aging Clock Based on Tabular Foundation Models and the Gompertz Law for Assisted Living Facility Residents

author.name: Chengzhuo Li, Rongjia Zhou, Shanshan Wang, Runze Yan, Carl Yang, Xiaobo Sun, Huiwen Xu, Jiaying Lu

entry.summary: TGAge is a phenotypic aging clock that predicts all-cause mortality risk from routine clinical tabular data using a tabular foundation model and converts risk ratios into biological age acceleration via the Gompertz law, targeting assisted-living populations where epigenetic clocks are impractical. It outperforms clinical indices on a large multi-state long-term care cohort.

entry.title: Can the Assistant Axis Predict Reward-Hacking?

author.name: Koby Lewis

entry.summary: This post reports exploratory interpretability research testing whether a drop in the so-called Assistant Axis feature direction in GPT-OSS 120B predicts the onset of reward hacking under RLVR training. Contrary to the hypothesis from the Persona Selection Model, the Assistant Axis projection at reward-hacking turns was typical, and the authors document methodological pitfalls of using AUROC on feature projections that initially misled them. It is a useful negative result for mechanistic approaches to monitoring misbehavior.

entry.title: A cat-belling problem for FDT

author.name: jessicata

entry.summary: The author examines the specific functional decision theory formulation of Yudkowsky and Soares (2017), highlighting that its subjunctive dependence operator rests on philosophically shaky foundations — Pearl formalized causal structure inference, but no analogous treatment exists for logical/subjunctive dependence — and constructs a cat-belling style problem exposing difficulties for the theory. The post includes an AI-assistance disclosure (light edits with Opus 5.5).

entry.title: FOCUS: A Lightweight Mamba-2 Model for EEG-Based Cognitive Workload Classification

author.name: Ioannis Kyprakis, Stefanos Gkikas, Chariklia Chatzaki, Zongyi Jiang, Randy Gomez, Raul Fernandez Rojas

entry.summary: FOCUS is an extremely compact Mamba-2 model (0.04M parameters, 0.11 GFLOPs) for EEG-based binary cognitive workload classification, using a fixed FFT decomposition over five canonical EEG bands rather than learned frequency sensitivity. It combines depthwise-separable convolutions with a weight-shared encoder-bottleneck Mamba-2 pair under constrained data conditions. The design targets unobtrusive continuous monitoring in high-risk environments.

entry.title: CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans

author.name: Kaiwen Wu, Chaochao Lu

entry.summary: Proposes CauProphet, an LLM agent architecture that builds and continuously updates a structured Causal Belief combining stored causal knowledge with current task evidence. The agent uses this belief for decisions and refines its long-term Causal Cognition as new observations arrive, aiming at better long-horizon task performance than record-retrieval memory.

entry.title: ChoreoStudio: Planning What, When, and Who in Music-Driven Group Choreography

author.name: Jing Xu, Cunjian Chen, Qiuhong Ke

entry.summary: Presents ChoreoStudio, a system for music-driven group dance generation that makes choreography planning explicit — deciding formations, transition timing, and role assignments — by first decomposing audio into frame-level rhythmic and segment-level structural features aligned with high-level musical structure. It addresses limits of prior methods in formation evolution and inter-dancer interaction.

entry.title: EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models

author.name: Zhile Guan, Xu Jiang, Yule Duan, Gongbo Zhang, Shuyu Wang, Xiao Chen, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: EditJev is a lightweight routing model that predicts sample-level preference scores over a pool of instruction-based image editing models in a single forward pass, selecting the best editor per request. This addresses pronounced sample-specific performance variation and latency differences among editing models, improving efficiency over fixed-model deployment. A preference head on a vision-language backbone enables fast routing.

entry.title: The Standard Deviation in VICReg Buys a Safety Margin

author.name: Hawar Dizayee

entry.summary: This paper experimentally tests VICReg authors' untested claim that a variance hinge would fail to prevent collapse, showing in controlled CIFAR experiments that standard-deviation and variance hinges perform identically at default weights, but the std hinge tolerates 35-130x lower threshold weights before collapse because its gradient does not fade as feature variance shrinks. It reframes the design choice as a robustness margin rather than a necessity.

entry.title: Operationalising Weaker Faithfulness: Recovery, Ambiguity and Computational Limits

author.name: Cillian Hourican, Rick Quax

entry.summary: The paper investigates how to weaken the faithfulness assumption in causal structure learning via selective edge protection and explicit retention of alternative graph explanations, showing both early candidate-removal and later pruning changes can be necessary. In noisy XOR experiments, combining reactivation and protection raised complete parent-pair recovery from 0/20 to 20/20 at the cost of false edges.

entry.title: Democratizing LLM Training with the Edge: Challenges, Systems, and the Road Ahead

author.name: Ziyue Luo, Jiaxuan Cai, Cedric LeDenmat, Srijith Nair, Fatemeh Nourzad, Rohith Krishnan, Qinhang Wu, Jifan Zhang, Sungjae Lee, Zhe Li, Peiwen Qiu, Siddharth Shah, Rishabh Sharma, Sundararajan Srinivasan, Yinglun Xia, Xue Zheng, Zidong Liu, Bicheng Ying, Kaushik Chowdhury, Gauri Joshi, Yingbin Liang, Robert Nowak, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Saurav Prakash, Balaraman Ravindran, Sanjay Shakkottai, Ness B. Shroff, Haibo Yang, Aylin Yener, Jia Liu

entry.summary: This position paper surveys distributed LLM training approaches (federated, split, and decentralized learning) for geo-distributed settings with heterogeneous hardware and unreliable connectivity, arguing they can democratize training for institutions without data-center-scale infrastructure. It presents a unified systems perspective and outlines open challenges across pretraining and fine-tuning paradigms.

entry.title: Random Jump Forests

author.name: Martin Bladt, Rasmus Frigaard Lemvig

entry.summary: Random jump forests are introduced as a nonparametric tool for estimating conditional cumulative transition rates and occupation probabilities in multi-state models, with Nelson-Aalen estimators at tree leaves and product-integral recovery of occupation probabilities without a Markov assumption. The authors establish uniform consistency and a functional central limit theorem, enabling confidence intervals. This extends random-forest methodology to multi-state survival analysis with theory.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Shreeram Suresh Chandra, Ashwyn Sharma, Liang Lu, Xiutian Zhao, Leda Sari, Bj\"orn Schuller, Berrak Sisman

entry.summary: The paper formulates speaking-style captioning (SSC) as an instruction-following audio-language task in which explicit instructions target specific paralinguistic dimensions such as speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style, and introduces a unified benchmark for controllable SSC. This supports downstream applications including conversational agents, controllable speech generation, and audio annotation.

entry.title: When Does GEPA Merge Help? A Mechanism-Level Diagnostic

author.name: Chong Zhao, Ruyi Yang, Changming Liu, Alice Zhao

entry.summary: This diagnostic study investigates why GEPA's system-aware prompt merge operator improves gpt-4.1-mini but degrades Qwen3-8B. Through a nine-configuration sweep across five datasets, the authors show merge helps both models when configured appropriately, attributing instability to configuration sensitivity rather than an inherent flaw, and find that static prompt-level features do not predict merge-accept decisions. This rules out a simple gating explanation for the asymmetry.

entry.title: DRA-SAM: Disagreement-Driven Referential Active SAM for Low-Altitude Drone Referring Segmentation

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Huaiyuan Peng, Wencan Zhang, Bimei Wang, Jingwen Zhao, Wenjun Ma, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: DRA-SAM allocates additional inference passes for drone referring segmentation when candidate masks disagree, using a lightweight EvidenceScorer over candidates and an unresolved state plus a training-free policy that selects crops for local re-inference. This active inference approach targets small, visually similar instances under complex linguistic and spatial constraints.

entry.title: The Paired Thermal Channel Is Two Orthogonal Axes: A Controlled Attribution Study of Calibration Cost and Detection Gain in Infrared Person Detection

author.name: Tian Zhang, Yang Chen, Bing Bai, Weikai He, Xiang Gao, Zhirong Su

entry.summary: Uses a controlled 2x2 factorial design to show the calibrated thermal channel in infrared person detection decomposes into orthogonal axes: calibrated delta-T improves mAP over scale-matched grayscale (+0.0221, statistically significant), while preserving paired correspondence and absolute calibrated scale jointly drives a large rise in expected calibration error. The interaction analysis localizes the ECE rise precisely, with significant p-values and large effect sizes.

entry.title: Cross-Scale Sparse Attention for Referring Segmentation in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yuxi Li, Lu Si, Xia Liao, Yidong Shen, Zheng Wei, Jun Zhang, Xin Yuan

entry.summary: The authors propose cross-scale sparse attention for referring remote sensing image segmentation, jointly modeling multi-scale visual hierarchies and linguistic dependencies while handling the spatial sparsity and dispersion of remote sensing targets. They also introduce structured evaluation of multi-target, multi-hop, and multi-granularity references. This advances language-grounded perception for satellite and aerial imagery.

entry.title: Reversion, Retention, and Semantic Intervention: Measuring Functional Content in CLIP Fine-Tuning Deltas

author.name: Chih-Ting Liao, Kezhen Bao, Xin Cao

entry.summary: This work improves weight-space interpretability of fine-tuning deltas by pairing reversion (restoring selected parameters to pretrained values) with retention (keeping only selected updates), measuring how much task performance actually depends on identified weight changes in CLIP models. Experiments span synthetic financial charts, Flowers102, EuroSAT, and FGVCAircraft.

entry.title: ParetoGS: High-Quality Continuous-Budget 3D Gaussian Splatting with Sparse Adapted Anchors

author.name: Xiaobin Deng, Changyu Diao, Min Li, Duanqing Xu

entry.summary: ParetoGS enables a single 3D Gaussian Splatting scene representation to serve continuous Gaussian-count budgets by encoding member changes and parameter evolution with a small set of adapted budget anchors, decoding intermediate budgets without separate optimization per count. It alternates pruning and fixed-member adaptation to build nested anchors with persistent identities.

entry.title: Recovering Black-Box Point Cloud Models from Pose Shifts via Derivative-Free Optimization

author.name: Seonghwan Park, Min-Gyu Park

entry.summary: CanDO is a test-time canonicalization method that recovers performance lost to out-of-distribution rotations in point cloud models accessed only through score-only black-box interfaces. It uses derivative-free optimization to search for confidence-maximizing input transformations and characterizes conditions for successful recovery.

entry.title: OrthoRF: Exploring Orthogonality in Object-Centric Representations

author.name: Despoina Touska, Bastiaan Onne Fagginger Auer, Alexandru Onose, Tejaswi Kasarla, Luis Armando P\'erez Rey, Maximilian Lipp, Lyubov Amitonova, Martin R. Oswald, Pascal Cerfontaine

entry.summary: OrthoRF enforces orthogonality in the orientation space of Rotating Features, a synchrony-inspired object-centric representation that encodes object presence in magnitudes and affiliation in orientations. An inner-product loss plus architectural modifications yield sharper phase alignment and more reliable unsupervised object discovery, including scenes with overlapping objects and noise.

entry.title: Toward Clinical Translation of Deep Learning-Based Intracranial Super-Resolution 4D Flow MRI Using Multi-Cohort Transfer Learning

author.name: Oliver Welin Odeback, Susanne Schnell, Patrick Winter, Johan Lundberg, Fredrik Piehl, Tobias Granberg, Alexander Fyrdahl, David Marlevi

entry.summary: A mixed prospective-retrospective study evaluating synthetic pretraining and multi-cohort transfer learning for super-resolution of intracranial 4D Flow MRI across heterogeneous neurological cohorts including healthy controls, moyamoya disease, and multiple sclerosis patients. Synthetic pretraining reduced velocity-normalized error, moving the technique toward clinical translation.

entry.title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration

author.name: Zhengxin Li, Chongzhen Tian, Hui Yuan, Hao Liu, Sam Kwong

entry.summary: Proposes TP-JSCC for deploying large vision-language models on resource-constrained embodied agents doing 3D visual question answering via cloud-edge collaboration. A hybrid local-global semantics token pruning module reduces visual token count, and joint source-channel coding mitigates latency and distortion over noisy, bandwidth-limited channels.

entry.title: Doppler-aided Position-Velocity Tracking of Hidden Objects using mmWave Radar

author.name: Yerin Cheon, Kush Garg, Akshat Dave

entry.summary: Develops a method for tracking hidden objects indoors through walls using millimeter-wave FMCW radar, exploiting Doppler information—which is underused in existing NLoS localization—to disambiguate low-resolution spatial observations. This enables fast, practical position-velocity tracking without dependence on ambient lighting.

entry.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing

author.name: Mohammad Rasoul Roshanshah, Mehdi Modarressi, Saeed Safari

entry.summary: ChroNoC is a tableless time-division-multiplexed circuit-switched network-on-chip providing deterministic latency for time-sensitive neuromorphic hardware, embedding precomputed broadcast trees into combinational logic to avoid linear configuration-memory scaling. The accompanying hardware-software co-design also accounts for algorithmic axonal delays during joint task placement, routing, and scheduling.

entry.title: ScheNav: Schematic-Guided Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Guichen Huang, Chenchen Jing, Che Sun, Yuwei Wu, Yunde Jia

entry.summary: Develops schematic-guided embodied navigation inspired by human use of rough sketches and directional annotations, contributing a data pipeline that converts 2D floorplans into navigation environments (Furnished-RPLAN, 33k+ furnished layouts with noise-controllable schematic maps) and ScheNav, a closed-loop framework turning schematic guidance into exploration and stopping decisions via a learned SchemaField spatial module.

entry.title: Beyond Wasserstein Proximity: Finding Better Transfer Sources

author.name: Gordei Verbii, Georgii Killinkarov, Vladimir Yafarov

entry.summary: The paper argues that marginal distributional proximity is a poor criterion for pretraining-source selection and demonstrates, via a cryptocurrency volatility forecasting experiment, that selecting the farthest (rather than nearest) Gaussian-Wasserstein sources can improve forecast skill by 12-21 percentage points. It motivates a conditional alternative grounded in domain-adaptation theory.

entry.title: How Geometry Shapes Generative Model Evaluation on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Misha Oberski, Valentijn Oldenburg, Xanthos Kekkos, Soham Chaudhuri, Emma Oosterhuis, Floris de Kam, Sagi Schwartz, Alison Pouplin, Federica Valeau

entry.summary: A systematic study of how curvature and dimension affect generative-model evaluation on Riemannian manifolds, comparing geodesic, ambient, and tangent-space versions of Wasserstein and MMD metrics using flow-matching samples and controlled noise perturbations. The finding is that no metric is uniformly reliable, leading to practical reporting and calibration recommendations.

entry.title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents

author.name: Navyansh Mahla, Sashank Vandrangi

entry.summary: Introduces ActionRAG, a graph-based long-term memory architecture for LLM agents that couples cautious indexing with tiered entity resolution and query-time graph retroevaluation. Dual-channel entity and triple retrieval refine initial similarity scores using surrounding graph evidence, targeting mutually consistent answers that depend on relations among facts.

entry.title: Efficient Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection via Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF)

author.name: Khaled Waleed Dawoud, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: SAAF enables efficient zero-shot video anomaly detection by adaptively sampling frames using dual signals: a delta signal for sudden events via frame-to-frame cosine distance and a drift signal for gradual anomalies relative to rolling temporal context. Combined with OR-gating and adaptive EMA thresholding, it achieves broad anomaly coverage without training data while keeping computational cost compatible with large-scale video streams.

entry.title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Structured Metadata and Climate Science Publications

author.name: Aayush Acharya, Qi Zhang, Eduard Dragut, Longin Jan Latecki

entry.summary: The paper presents an agentic, ontology-guided framework for knowledge graph construction from climate science literature, using specialized agents for document understanding, information extraction, ontology conformance, and entity linking. LLM-extracted triples carry explicit textual evidence and pass multistage verification grounded in the ontology. Enforcing schema constraints and evidence requirements improves trustworthiness of scientific knowledge extraction.

entry.title: MAGIC: Margin-gated Contrastive Debiasing with Evidence Restoration for VLM Test-time Robustness Scaling

author.name: Shunshun Gu, Enze Zhang, Ming Pei, Hang Zhou, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: MAGIC improves test-time robustness of large vision-language models by using decision margins to selectively activate textual and visual perturbation branches, reducing both the evidence destruction inherent in perturbation-based contrastive decoding and redundant inference cost. The margin gating yields more efficient debiased inference.

entry.title: Timing Matters Twice: When to Query and When to Skip in Flow-Matching On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Renye Yan, Junyi Zhan, Jikang Cheng, Wei Peng

entry.summary: The paper studies when supervision from specialized teachers is most effective in on-policy distillation of flow-matching image generation models, noting that different evaluation dimensions and tasks benefit from supervision at different denoising stages. It proposes adaptive mechanisms deciding when to query teachers and when to skip, reducing overhead while improving quality.

entry.title: P2P-Former: Bridging the Supervision Gap Between Point and Proposal in Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Yunchuan Ma, Laiyun Qing, Sai Xu, Guorong Li, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: P2P-Former is a point-to-proposal Transformer framework that connects point-level supervision to proposal-level learning for temporal action localization, narrowing the gap to fully supervised models. It identifies and addresses two key challenges in transitioning from cheap point annotations to full proposal supervision.

entry.title: SGDB: Semantic-Geometric Decoupling and Evidence Binding for Logical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Chenrui Ji, Jiafan Lu, Zilu Luo, Feng Wan, Qiuhui Chen, Weimin Zhong

entry.summary: SGDB decouples semantic identity learning from geometric measurement for logical anomaly detection, binding geometric evidence to object identities via partial one-to-one association while retaining unmatched objects in counts. A support-certified reader selects mask-derived axes using line quality and component ownership, with explicit task constraints and normal-data references.

entry.title: Unveil the Mask: Jointly-Optimized Diffusion Masked Pretraining for Appearance-Agnostic Operator Verification

author.name: Katsuya Ogata, Ryoya Yoshiyama, Kawachi Hodaka, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: Addresses the problem that photorealistic avatar videos break conventional face recognition, proposing a framework to verify the human operator based on facial motion rather than appearance. It learns motion representations from landmark sequences via diffusion masked pretraining with auxiliary behavioral-cue tasks, combining them with video frames, without any external pretrained model.

entry.title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft

author.name: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone

entry.summary: Presents NeSySpec, an interpretable neuro-symbolic framework built on Logic Tensor Networks that audits engineering specifications by encoding physical constraints as differentiable graded predicates with tolerances learned from real fleet records. It diagnoses violated constraints, identifies altered fields via abduction, proposes minimum-change corrections, and abstains where evidence is missing.

entry.title: PS-DLO: Property- and Spatially Aware Deformable Linear Object Manipulation Policy

author.name: Mengdi Li, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Yifan Yang, Yunfan Lou, Xuan Han, Tao Liu, Zhibo Pang

entry.summary: Introduces a manipulation policy for deformable linear objects that uses contrastive image-text learning to map observations to categorical descriptions of physical properties, and SAM3 to extract mask-guided features distilled into the action expert. Evaluated on nine real-world tasks across settings, it addresses the coupled perception-control challenge of slender, deformable objects.

entry.title: Hessian-Similar Optimization with Capped Participation: Lower Bounds and Virtual Masters

author.name: Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper establishes communication-round lower bounds for federated optimization when each round can contact at most s of m clients, via a hidden-client chain argument on strongly convex quadratics, and proposes virtual-master SVRS algorithms that remove dependence on a poor anchor Hessian. It gives the first tight characterization of strict participation caps.

entry.title: CASE: Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution for Frozen Multimodal Emotion Models

author.name: Siyu Wu, Zeyu Liang, Linghao Wang, Qiyun Zheng, Yi Yao, Ling Lo, Hongxia Xie

entry.summary: Targets systematic confusion between semantically adjacent emotions in multimodal emotion recognition by maintaining a sparse, self-evolving library of pair-specific skills applied to frozen multimodal models, rather than adapting global parameters. This keeps confusion correction cheap and modular.

entry.title: Before the Ticket: Grounding HPC User Support in Documentation and Resolved Tickets with an Agentic LLM Assistant

author.name: Elham J. Barezi, Primus C Kabuo, Niveditha Nerella

entry.summary: This paper describes an on-premises agentic assistant for HPC help desks that combines RAG over live documentation with a QLoRA fine-tuned Llama-3-8B over 11,244 mined historical tickets, orchestrated via the Model Context Protocol. Evaluated on 400 held-out Purdue tickets, it addresses privacy constraints requiring institutional deployment.

entry.title: RobustNCL: Robustifying Neuromorphic Continual Learning under Transient Faults with Lightweight Detect-and-Cure Strategy

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Shuochen Zhou, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: RobustNCL is the first study of neuromorphic continual learning reliability under transient hardware faults such as particle-strike-induced bit flips, proposing a lightweight detect-and-cure strategy to preserve CL performance. It opens a previously unexplored reliability direction for energy-efficient on-device learning.

entry.title: Dual-Adaptive Z-Score PPO: Dynamic Clipping Using Action Confidence and Normalized Advantage Magnitude

author.name: Taha M. Mahmoud, Naima Kaabouch

entry.summary: Proposes PPO-DAZ3, an adaptive-clipping variant of PPO that replaces the fixed clipping threshold with per-sample intervals computed from action confidence (selected-action probability) and update confidence (normalized advantage magnitude). The aim is to give more or less trust-region width depending on update reliability rather than treating all samples identically.

entry.title: TENET: Time-point Encoding Network for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Dongchan Cho, Juwon Hwang, Keumyeong Kang, Jiho Han, Namsoon Jung

entry.summary: TENET reframes unsupervised multivariate time series anomaly detection as estimating whether the current point is compatible with the overall system state, using a latent representation built from variable-level temporal context. This latent-space scoring approach avoids the unreliability of reconstruction-error-based detection when local variation inflates errors. It targets a practical industrial monitoring problem.

entry.title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents

author.name: Juan Felipe Duran, Arthur Tobler, Martin Valli\`eres

entry.summary: The paper presents an LLM-agent pipeline that builds a knowledge graph of healthcare software customer and integration relationships from scattered public web sources, enforcing that every graph edge is backed by a verbatim source quote for verifiability. This grounding rule addresses hallucination concerns that could mislead hospital buyers. It is a practical demonstration of trustworthy agentic information extraction.

entry.title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization

author.name: Qing Liu, Xinrui Chen, Yi Du, Ou Wu, Weiyao Zhu

entry.summary: DRIVE is a data-weighting framework for fine-tuning that assigns per-sample weights via a unified differentiable objective balancing knowledge retention against new-task adaptation, incorporating contribution, diversity, and prior regularization signals. It targets catastrophic forgetting in single-stage fine-tuning when pre-training data is unavailable.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control

author.name: Rahul Golder, Bimol Nath Roy, MM Faruque Hasan

entry.summary: This tutorial presents KKT-HardNet, a modular physics-constrained ML framework that enforces linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints via differential projection while retaining fast neural inference. It demonstrates the framework across hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization, and model predictive control in a single platform.

entry.title: Real-to-Sim Calibration of Bosch Etching Simulators with Few-Shot XSEM Data and Hybrid Search

author.name: Xinyu Jia, Jainil Shah, Rahul Tripathi, Vijay Gupta, Zhihong Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a few-shot real-to-sim calibration framework for the Bosch etching process used in MEMS and TSV fabrication, decoupling simulator parameters from direct process variables to infer a recipe-specific parameter vector from sparse XSEM measurements. The approach enables reliable prediction of etch depth and sidewall angle under held-out process conditions, addressing the high cost of real calibration data.

entry.title: RoboCode: Learning Reusable Action Primitives for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xianyue Peng, Devi Amarsaikhan, Iman Soltani

entry.summary: RoboCode learns reusable short-horizon motion primitives from manipulation demonstrations via a shared soft-gated primitive interface, representing each action chunk as a soft composition of multiple learned primitives rather than a single discrete code. Primitives are learned across tasks and frozen, then used as a structured intermediate representation for task policies.

entry.title: Cross-Scenario Controller Parameter Transformation from Real-World Driving Data through Flow Matching

author.name: Christian Zink, Maik Pfefferkorn, Eric Lenz, Felix Kallmeyer, Rolf Findeisen

entry.summary: The paper frames adapting adaptive cruise control parameters across driving scenarios as a driver-individual transport problem, training a flow-matching generative model on real-world driving data to predict target-scenario behavior of unseen drivers from limited data. This aims to make driver assistance feel natural and personalized rather than generic. It is a creative application of flow matching to automotive control personalization.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yixuan Xu, Hailin Liu, Linxiang Peng, Can Yang

entry.summary: This work proposes knowledge distillation objectives that transfer item-level predictive knowledge from sequential recommenders to semantic-ID generative recommenders, bridging the gap between item space teachers and code space students. The two complementary distillation objectives provide distributional supervision beyond hard next-item labels for parallel semantic-ID generation.

entry.title: Quantifying Meaning with SCAPE-T: Semantic Complexity from Encoder-Only Transformer Attention

author.name: Maxim Khovansky, Lev Mukhanov

entry.summary: Defines semantic complexity as the code length needed to specify a text's meaning and operationalizes it via SCAPE-T, an attention-derived metric from encoder-only transformers combining self-focus, CLS-focus, and inter-head reduction submetrics. Positions it against readability and surface-feature measures.

entry.title: Propasafe-Hybrid: A Text-Based Hybrid Propaganda Detection Tool

author.name: Thomas Kimmeth, Avijit Roy, Vivek Sharma

entry.summary: Presents a sentence-level propaganda detection pipeline combining a fine-tuned transformer classifier with LLM-based technique classification, producing highlighted sentences, technique labels, and rationales. A cost-aware pre-filter controls inference cost by forwarding only high-risk content.

entry.title: Reversible Pseudonymisation of Documents Sent to External LLMs: an Open Bilingual Benchmark and an Engine

author.name: Vladimir Beskorovainyi

entry.summary: This paper presents an open benchmark evaluating five open-source pseudonymisation tools and a regex baseline on Russian and UK English documents, plus an engine combining the two strongest tools. The benchmark features rigorous pre-registration: held-out synthetic sets, published decision rules, hashes, and stopping rules before any runs, and tests whether placeholder masking preserves downstream LLM task quality. It addresses the practical privacy problem of sending working documents to external LLMs.

entry.title: Does the Outfit Change the Price? Context Halo in Vision-Language Model Valuation of an Identical Low-Cost Necklace

author.name: Brianne Lee

entry.summary: A behavioral experiment priced one identical necklace across four photographed contexts in 1,164 sequential sessions with six frontier models, finding vision models priced it 1.9 to 3.3 times higher in formal-attire photographs than flat-lay, with per-model variation across Grok 4.5, Kimi K3, and Claude Fable 5. It demonstrates a context halo effect in vision-language valuation.

entry.title: From Questions to Queries to Insights: A Schema-Grounded Agentic Workflow for Natural-Language Crash Data Analysis

author.name: Jingwen Zhu, Keshu Wu, Steven T. Parker, Bin Ran, David A. Noyce

entry.summary: Presents CrashDB-QA, a fully local, schema-grounded agentic workflow enabling natural-language analysis of transportation crash databases, with components for question interpretation, read-only SQL generation and validation, execution, and result explanation, supported by a shared knowledge base. It lowers the barrier for transportation agencies to query coded crash data without SQL specialists. A well-scoped domain application of text-to-SQL agents.

entry.title: Improving JEV Entailment Reranking with Span Readouts and Selective Adaptation

author.name: Haocheng Mei, Yuchuan Tian, Ye Yuan, Enhua Wu, Chao Xu, Allen Chen, Kai Han, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: Studies readout and adaptation choices for entailment-based reranking in JEV-style decision models, proposing a mean-span pooling readout over NLI options plus selective low-rank adaptation of attention and gated DeltaNet layers. Shows which selection-time design choices transfer to cross-request reranking.

entry.title: PreView: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Preprocessed Views and Cues

author.name: Wenjun Hou, Kaishuai Xu

entry.summary: PreView is a training-free auxiliary preprocessor that improves existing GUI grounding models by producing task-relevant cropped views and candidate-specific visual cues. A lightweight model predicts a center, crops and enlarges the screenshot, and adds a visual cue to disambiguate the target control.

entry.title: A Domain-Aware Pipeline for Structured Extraction and Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering over arXiv Superconductivity Literature

author.name: Ivan Iorsh, Aleksandr Kapitonov, Ivan Filianin, Matvey Lesonen, Nikita Chizhov

entry.summary: The authors build an end-to-end pipeline that converts arXiv superconductivity papers into a searchable corpus with structured metadata, including extracted materials and superconducting transition temperatures. Hybrid retrieval combining dense chunk embeddings with structured fields improves evidence retrieval and answer groundedness in RAG question answering for materials physics.

entry.title: Beyond Vision-Language Models: Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs for Emotion Recognition in Artworks

author.name: Ngoc-Duy Mai, Ha-Thanh Nguyen, Hideaki Takeda

entry.summary: The paper proposes Visual-Semantic Affect Graphs (VSAG), an interpretable graph-based framework for emotion recognition in artworks that explicitly represents color, brushstroke, composition, lighting, and visual entities as feature nodes. It argues that direct image-to-emotion prediction with vision-language models misses relational structure between formal and semantic affective cues.

entry.title: Decentralized Multi-View, Multi-Zone Tracking for Scalable Camera Networks

author.name: David Voihanski, Mor Sinai, Ben Zion Bobrovsky

entry.summary: Presents a decentralized multi-view tracking system that projects single-view detections into bird's-eye-view coordinates and fuses them via independent trackers managing dynamic spatial zones. A locking protocol, periodic global collate track-merging, and delayed-output buffering handle asynchronous coordination and cross-zone identity consistency at network scale.

entry.title: Semantic-First MixGRPO: Reliable Emotional Image Generation via Temporal Decoupling

author.name: Zhenxuan Wang

entry.summary: The study examines stochastic-window position in mixed ODE/SDE sampling as an attribute-control variable for flow-based image generation, using FLUX.1-dev with valence-arousal conditioning to edit emotional content without altering prompt-specified objects and layout. It compares fixed early, middle, and late SDE windows against progressive MixGRPO and full-path Flow-GRPO under matched settings. This refines how GRPO-style post-training controls specific image attributes.

entry.title: FreqPKC: Frequency-Aware PeakConv for Radar Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yangyong Deng, Pengyu Zhang, Shaoqiu Song, Xiaotao Huang, Jian Wang

entry.summary: FreqPKC revisits the radar-specific PeakConv operator from a frequency-domain perspective, explicitly modeling its spectral characteristics rather than treating guard bandwidth as opaque learnable parameters, and exploits this for millimeter-wave radar semantic segmentation in autonomous driving. The frequency-aware design aims to better capture the peak-dominated statistics of radar images. It connects radar signal physics with neural operator design.

entry.title: E3tereo: Improving Stereo Matching at Depth Boundaries with Learned Geometric Edges

author.name: Qi Xiong, Qinghua Zhao, Yongqiang Xi

entry.summary: E3Stereo learns geometric edges from disparity supervision and uses them with backbone disparity predictions to output full-resolution disparity corrections, noting that on IGEV/Scene Flow only 6% of pixels are geometric edges yet they account for roughly half of total error. The edge map also re-weights boundary errors during training via joint optimization. Targets the classic depth-boundary weakness of stereo matching.

entry.title: Rank-1 Weight-Corrected Trainable Weight Averaging for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Akito Shinohara, Hiroaki Aizawa

entry.summary: Building on rank-based analyses linking OOD overconfidence to dominant low-rank components, this work extends Trainable Weight Averaging with rank-one weight components extracted via SVD as correction directions. The contributions of these corrections are learned through in-distribution classification, improving OOD detection in parameter space.

entry.title: StaX-Net: Stackelberg Interleaved Asymmetric Network for Cross-Modality Medical Image Translation

author.name: Amin Golnari, Saeid Sanei

entry.summary: StaX-Net targets anatomically consistent cross-modality medical image translation (e.g., synthesizing one imaging modality from another) using a partially coupled encoder-discriminator structure and a FAST layer that distills target-domain priors via learning-using-privileged-information. A Stackelberg-inspired asymmetric optimization scheme with shared-parameter freezing and asymmetric learning rates stabilizes leader-follower adversarial training. The goal is clinically reliable synthesis that preserves diagnostic anatomy.

entry.title: From Presence Labels to Bounding Boxes: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Scale Surgical Instrument Localization?

author.name: Mohamed Hamdy, Muraam Abdel-Ghani, Fatmaelzahraa Ahmed, Sifna Nasar, Mariam Ahmed, Khalid Al-Jalham, Abdulaziz Al-Ali, Shidin Balakrishnan

entry.summary: This study designs a scalable MLLM-based annotation framework that converts surgical frames with existing instrument-presence labels into accurate bounding boxes, systematically analyzing reliability and cost. It addresses the scarcity of complete bounding-box annotations for surgical instrument localization.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting

author.name: Fatma Ahmed Mansour, Rahatara Ferdousi, Manar Fathy Elshenawy

entry.summary: Presents an evidence-grounded agentic framework linking liver lesion segmentation via TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models with deterministic quantification and LLM-organized structured reporting. Numerical consistency checks against source measurements ensure reproducible, traceable reports, evaluated on LiTS data.

entry.title: FGD2HF: Frequency-guided Dual-domain Hypergraph Fusion for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Xiaofan Yang, Wei Pan, Yubin Liu, Junyu Wu, Junming Zhang, Jie Zhao

entry.summary: FGD2HF is a semantic segmentation network that uses frequency-domain features to guide spatial-domain fusion, combining a hybrid-attention encoder with neighborhood and hypergraph attention plus a wavelet-based enhancement module. It targets better frequency utilization and lower computational complexity than prior frequency-based segmentation methods.

entry.title: DimFlow: Bidirectional Grid-Expert Learning for Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Gabriel Adineera, Jinoh Kim

entry.summary: DimFlow is a framework for dynamic Gaussian scene reconstruction that learns compact features via bidirectional interaction between a multi-resolution grid and coordinate-based expert branches. It uses adversarial feature alignment, adaptive fusion, and activation-masked residual feedback, with separate experts for deformation, rotation, opacity, and temporal attributes.

entry.title: Evidence-Guided Selection of Retinal Vessel Segmentation Pipelines: A Cross-Dataset Benchmark of Performance, Structure, Failure Modes, and Reproducibility

author.name: Ruoyu Yan, Yuejia Liu, Shixin Xu, Xiaoyan Li, Xi Luo, Yuhui Deng, Huaxiong Huang

entry.summary: Benchmarks five executable retinal vessel segmentation pipelines on 244 images from six public datasets using pixel-level agreement, cross-dataset stability, thin-vessel retention, structural metrics, and error composition. No pipeline is optimal in every setting; FSG-Net achieves the best equal-dataset mean scores. The study emphasizes evidence-guided model selection over single aggregate scores.

entry.title: Cross-View and Cross-Time Tracking of Crack Evolution in Concrete

author.name: Pengru Deng, Jiapeng Yao, Su Wang, Xuhui He, Zhao Wang, Takanori Emaru, Takashi Matsumoto, Xinrun Li

entry.summary: Formulates vision-based crack tracking as a coupled cross-view and cross-time problem where a physical crack must retain identity across changing viewpoints while new growth is distinguished from existing segments. The work targets structural health monitoring of concrete infrastructure beyond static crack detection.

entry.title: Thermal-Headroom Routing for Efficient Robot Perception in Extreme Heat

author.name: Sparsh Roy, Kevin Zhou, Arhaan Shah, Shreyan Garg, Vihaan Joshi-Apte, Maxim Kudryashov, Nanda Cheruvanthala

entry.summary: Proposes Thermal-Headroom Routing (THR), a lightweight policy that forecasts processor temperature via a closed-form RC thermal model and excludes detector configurations likely to trigger thermal throttling, balancing accuracy, latency, and energy in extreme ambient heat. Evaluated with YOLO11 configurations across seven traces and eight temperatures, it outperforms latency-aware routing and fixed thermostats at 45-55 degrees C.

entry.title: Optimal Connectivity of Random Boolean Networks for Reservoir Computing

author.name: Christopher Michael Skeide Vibe, Aliaksandr Hubin, Stefano Nichele

entry.summary: The authors study random Boolean networks (cellular automata with random recurrent wiring) as reservoirs for reservoir computing, focusing on how connectivity controls the ordered-to-chaotic phase transition near a mean in-degree of 2. They also analyze how input fan-out, determined by how inputs share network edges, interacts with connectivity to shape computational performance.

entry.title: Sybil-Resilient Multi-Drone Exploration of Indoor and Confined Spaces

author.name: Shyaam Mahesh, Aditya B Prakash, Rubal Sagwal, Avinash Gautam

entry.summary: Studies Sybil attacks on multi-drone cooperative exploration, where a compromised drone creates fake identities that claim frontiers and fabricate map data, causing real drones to leave areas unexplored or build corrupted maps. The paper defines five attacker models and five defenses requiring no security infrastructure, relying only on the drones' own sensors and map consistency checks.

entry.title: Dual Gradient Consensus for Adaptive Learning to Transient Out-of-Distribution Disturbances in Quadrotor Control

author.name: Mingtian Tan, Vasileios Tzoumas

entry.summary: DGC improves online residual adaptation for quadrotor control by comparing each residual gradient against long- and short-term gradient memories to classify in-domain versus out-of-domain disturbance regimes, then suppressing unreliable updates via a confidence map. Built on the prior DAPL residual policy, it prevents short OOD events from corrupting learned disturbance models. This is a practical fix to a known failure mode of constant-step online adaptation.

entry.title: 3D-Force Estimation for Dual-arm Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects via Factor Graphs

author.name: Annika Delucchi, Vincenzo Di Paola, Bruno Marco Quadrelli, Matteo Zoppi

entry.summary: This work uses factor graphs to estimate the magnitude, direction, and location of 3D forces acting on deformable linear objects like cables and wires while simultaneously reconstructing their shape, relating DLO state and sensor data through conditional distributions. This avoids impractical strain gauges or actuation sensing for thin unactuated objects. Reliable contact force estimation enables safer dual-arm DLO manipulation.

entry.title: Securing Edge & Physical AI: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain for Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents

author.name: K\"ur\c{s}at \c{C}akal, Suat \"Ozdemir

entry.summary: Examines the vulnerability of public-key authentication in distributed cyber-physical and Edge AI networks to quantum attacks and proposes a post-quantum IoT blockchain architecture. It introduces rotational secrecy as an architectural objective to manage the computation, memory, and communication overheads that PQC introduces for dynamic multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Certifying Distributionally Robust Decisions from Projection Observations

author.name: Pouya Ahadi, Kamran Paynabar

entry.summary: Studies when a scalar measurement can certify a robust decision without identifying latent covariance or full decision risks, in finite Gaussian projection experiments. It provides a confidence-set certificate that returns a decision or an unresolved outcome, proves soundness and necessary abstention for indistinguishable models, and reduces nonlinear risk comparisons to convex inner problems.

entry.title: Approximate Universal Prediction under Interaction

author.name: Richard Cornelius Suwandi

entry.summary: The paper studies which approximation guarantees for Solomonoff-style universal predictors survive when an agent's planning directs where the predictor is evaluated, showing that task and action-branch rarity can compound and that within a single universal mixture infinitely many computable environments admit unbounded excess prediction loss. This formalizes self-referential failure modes of optimistic universal agents like AIXI.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction with Stable Measurement Mechanisms

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: The paper studies conformal prediction intervals when transferring from a source population with reference outcomes to a target population where only cheap sensor readings and context are available, as in air-quality monitoring. Under a stable measurement mechanism assumption (a form of causal mechanism shift), the authors adapt marginal matching, predictive adjustment, and weighted conformal methods. This extends distribution-shift robustness of conformal prediction to measurement-bias settings.

entry.title: On the asymptotic behaviour of $\alpha$-divergence generalized posteriors

author.name: Ioar Casado-Telletxea, Omar Rivasplata

entry.summary: The authors analyze asymptotics of generalized variational inference posteriors regularized by alpha-divergences, showing the minimizer, after rescaling, converges in L1 to non-Gaussian limits: a Student-t distribution for alpha in (0,1) and a compactly supported Pearson-family distribution for alpha greater than 1. The posterior concentration scale departs from the classical Bernstein-von Mises n^{-1/2} rate. This refines theoretical understanding of divergence-based variational inference.

entry.title: Agentic Hazard Mapper: Emulating Expert Map-Making with AI Agents for Risk Communication

author.name: Sidi Wu, Lifeng Lin, Yizi Chen, Anna Yokokubo, Lorenz Hurni

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent system that automates production of hazard maps by emulating professional cartographic workflows and design trade-offs, adapting to different data, locations, and hazards. A formative study with map experts informed the design, and user studies with experts and practitioners showed improved spatial understanding and evacuation planning support.

entry.title: DIGOM: Disentangled Interaction Graphs for Outcome prediction in Multimodal healthcare

author.name: Hakima Laribi, Olivier Lefebvre, Dan Poenaru, Martin Valli\`eres

entry.summary: DIGOM is a graph-based framework for clinical outcome prediction that jointly models three interaction types: intra-patient cross-modal, cross-patient same-modal, and cross-patient cross-modal relationships. It learns a sparse multiplex graph over multimodal healthcare data, going beyond standard fusion approaches. This richer relational modeling could improve prediction in complex clinical settings.

entry.title: Promise and Limits of Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Medical Vision Transformers (LiteMed-ViT)

author.name: Shuaibu Shehu (SR University), Elijah M. Flomo (SR University), Mohammad Safiya (GITAM University), Anurodh Kumar (SR University), Subodh Kumar (Dr. KNS Memorial Institute of Medical Sciences)

entry.summary: LiteMed-ViT is a 0.234M-parameter dual-token vision transformer with a convolutional stem and class-balanced distillation objective, distilled across architectures from a ResNet18 teacher, achieving a 47.8x parameter reduction and a 0.89 MB footprint for point-of-care medical imaging. The study probes how far data-efficient ViT distillation can be pushed across architectures. It speaks to the promise and limits of deploying transformers on clinical edge devices.

entry.title: S$^2$-RL: Sample-Set Dual Reinforcement Learning for Generative Semantic Segmentation Dataset Distillation

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Fei Zhou, Qingqing Qiu, Lei Zhang, Wei Wei, Chen Ding

entry.summary: Proposes a sample-set reinforcement learning framework for generative semantic segmentation dataset distillation, addressing both the computational cost of bi-level optimization and the semantic poverty of texture-only generative proxies. The approach condenses rich semantic knowledge into compact sets of novel scene generations rather than fixed masks with injected textures.

entry.title: Cut a Wall, See a Wall: Identity Substitution in Occluded Point-Cloud Perception for Construction Robots

author.name: Tsung-Lung Yang

entry.summary: Shows that under test-time occlusion of whole scene regions, point-cloud segmentation networks for construction scenes do not merely miss hidden elements but actively relabel them, with errors collapsing onto a single sink class (up to 70 percent of points; baseline mIoU dropping to 0.15-0.27). Adding hand-computed geometric features per point restores mIoU substantially, offering a practical fix for occlusion-induced identity substitution.

entry.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition

author.name: Ziya Hosseynzadeh, Farjad Fallah, Farnoosh Fallah, Soroush Gooran, Mohammad Amanloo, Hossein Sameti

entry.summary: This comparative study benchmarks FISER, which uses structured social and embodied reasoning, against CEMIR, a multimodal enrichment method, for pragmatic intent recognition in human-robot interaction. It asks whether multimodal enrichment helps when ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing scene information.

entry.title: Beyond Channel Data: Configuration-Enriched Radio Foundation Models

author.name: Shrihari Vasudevan, H. G. Ranjani, Raaghul Ranganathan, Satwik Sahu, Thirumaran Ekambaram

entry.summary: Demonstrates that incorporating channel configuration information into Radio Foundation Model pre-training yields embeddings that act as effective inductive priors for downstream wireless tasks like LoS/NLoS classification, timing advance estimation, and beam selection, especially under label scarcity and out-of-distribution configurations.

entry.title: Generalized green and red concepts for artificial intelligence, big data, and information and communication technologies: Multidimensional framework and countermeasures

author.name: Jinsong Wu, Yixin Xiao, Haowei Bi, Huamin Fang

entry.summary: This position-style paper proposes generalized green AI and generalized red AI frameworks that extend sustainability discussions beyond computational efficiency and carbon emissions to lifecycle trade-offs, service-versus-use impacts, and water and material externalities. It is motivated by projections such as data centers consuming 6.7-12% of U.S. electricity by 2028.

entry.title: Guided Zero-Shot Anomaly Explanation for Anonymized Crowd Video Monitoring: Context, Categorization, and Spatial Localization

author.name: Mulugeta Weldezgina Asres, Lei Jiao, Christian Walter Omlin

entry.summary: XAVAD unifies zero-shot anonymization, anomaly type categorization, visual localization, and scene context description into an explainable, privacy-preserving video anomaly detection framework for crowd monitoring. It targets the underexplored intersection of explainability and privacy protection in safety and security video systems.

entry.title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images

author.name: Somraj Gautam, Gaurav Harit

entry.summary: The paper introduces Self-RefineVQA, a training-free inference-time self-correction framework that improves visual question answering over tables in document images. It iteratively critiques and refines answers to mitigate spatial misalignment and logical hallucinations, avoiding costly supervised fine-tuning or architectural changes. The method lowers barriers for improving table VQA without labeled data.

entry.title: SemGeo-Gen: Unsupervised Generation of Approximate Cross-Instance Semantic-Geometric Correspondences

author.name: Roy Amoyal, Shira Ifergane, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: SemGeo-Gen generates approximate semantic-geometric supervision from weakly aligned 3D object collections without manual correspondence labels. It lifts multi-view DINOv2 features to 3D, aligns instances with continuous piecewise-affine registration, and prunes candidate matches, producing diverse correspondences suitable for training modern correspondence models. This reduces dependence on expensive point-level annotation.

entry.title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model

author.name: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Armon Rasooli

entry.summary: Yalda-Embedding is a 595.8M-parameter open Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using over one million query-document pairs, achieving the best macro-average (0.5488) among 0.6B models on eight FaMTEB Persian retrieval tasks and nearly matching the 4B model. The paper documents incremental ablations over training choices. It addresses the scarcity of language-specific resources for Persian.

entry.title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning

author.name: Thanh Linh Nguyen, Quoc-Viet Pham

entry.summary: PDF is a path-dependent client-selection framework for federated unlearning that recognizes client influence is path-dependent, maintaining lightweight tracking during training to identify which retained clients best support removing a target client's influence without full retraining. It accounts for knowledge overlap, intermittent availability, and critical learning periods. This improves the practicality of privacy-driven unlearning in federated settings.

entry.title: BAARC: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Partial Spectral Measurement to Full Reconstruction for Material Classification

author.name: Adithya Ashok Chalain Valapil, Aishwarya Venkataramanan, Joachim Denzler

entry.summary: BAARC is a Bayesian adaptive acquisition framework for Raman spectroscopy that uses masked training to learn which narrow wavenumber patches to measure next, progressively reconstructing spectra and classifying materials without requiring prior knowledge of where distinguishing peaks lie. It is a jointly trained two-level measurement-plus-classification system.

entry.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

author.name: Ilya Brekin, Ariela Moldavskaya, Elina Sidorova, Ural Valeev

entry.summary: This analysis shows that supervised pairwise graph representations can outperform attention-as-adjacency baselines in an error-detection task, but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is nearly perfectly recoverable from hidden states. It provides provable post-hoc corrections and cautions that graph-level accuracy may not reflect genuine higher-order topological signal.

entry.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces

author.name: Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Andrea Angino, Rolf Krause, Matthias Voigt

entry.summary: This paper generalizes necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models from Hardy-Hilbert spaces to reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, and constructs an alternative to IRKA for RKHSs with differentiable kernels. It introduces generalized Malmquist-Takenaka functions enabling orthonormal bases and unitary transformations between separable RKHSs.

entry.title: Multi modal perceived conversation success prediction for spontaneous autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions

author.name: Thanushi Withanage, Desi Jones, Noah Sasson, Elizabeth Redcay, Carol Espy-Wilson

entry.summary: This study predicts participants' perceived conversation success in autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions from multimodal articulatory, facial, acoustic-prosodic, and turn-taking measures across three spontaneous datasets. It shifts focus from diagnostic classification toward predicting subjective conversational outcomes.

entry.title: WADE: An LSTM-Based Anomaly Detection Engine for WebAssembly Applications

author.name: Ilaria Campestrini, Stefano Zanero, Engin Kirda

entry.summary: WADE detects anomalous runtime behavior in browser-executed WebAssembly applications by training an LSTM on benign function-level execution traces and flagging deviations at runtime. It targets Wasm's weak runtime protections, such as the lack of stack canaries and ASLR, which leave applications open to traditional attacks.

entry.title: SyncPro: Synchronous Reasoning and Responding for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Xueyun Tian, Bingbing Xu, Jiaming Liu, Jinpeng Yu, Yang Shi, Yu Zhao, Ruihua Huang, Yuanzhuo Wang, Huawei Shen

entry.summary: SyncPro coordinates ongoing intermediate reasoning with timely responses in proactive streaming video assistants, combining the strengths of proactive response timing and scheduled streaming video reasoning. It addresses the underexplored problem of when to reason versus when to respond as new evidence accumulates.

entry.title: Empirical concentration for chains with infinite memory

author.name: Pierre Alquier, Paul Doukhan

entry.summary: The paper extends empirical concentration inequalities beyond stationary Markov chains to stationary chains with infinite memory, proving a bounded-differences inequality on bounded Polish metric spaces under a summable Wasserstein contraction condition.
