entry.summary: This study disentangles how much wearable blood pressure tracking accuracy comes from acquisition context versus the photoplethysmography signal itself, using participant-level cross-validation across 653 AuroraBP participants. The wearable-state model achieves mean absolute errors of roughly 7.7/6.1 mmHg for systolic/diastolic pressure, with follow-up analyses adding accelerometer signals, pulse-rate fusion, and an intraoperative VitalDB model. It matters because cuffless BP monitoring accuracy claims often confound signal quality with contextual calibration cues.

entry.title: From Association to Decision Value: Testing Paired Instruction Dependence for VLA Corpus Selection

author.name: Nurmukhambet Serikbayev, Abdul Basit, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: This paper studies how to rank robot demonstration corpora for training vision-language-action models, proposing paired instruction dependence (how often a demonstrator changes its first decision when only the goal changes) as a diagnostic. Experiments across 136 quadruped-navigation corpora show the audit predicts downstream paired correctness and reduces prediction error, though the proper-log-score improvement is modest with a confidence interval crossing zero.

entry.title: VHDLBench: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for VHDL-Based Chip Design

author.name: Patrik Drazic, Benaoumeur Senouci, Boualem Benatallah

entry.summary: VHDLBench targets the underexplored application of LLMs to VHDL hardware description generation, introducing an 18,500-example syntax-verified dataset and fine-tuning five 7B-parameter models with QLoRA for resource-constrained deployment. It includes evaluation of generated circuit designs to fill gaps in EDA workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey

author.name: Hamza Kheddar

entry.summary: A survey covering more than 100 studies on reinforcement learning implementations across FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms, organized by RL family and covering architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. It highlights the co-design challenges between hardware constraints and RL algorithms for edge and embedded deployment. Useful as a reference map for researchers deploying RL on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: StyleStream 2.0: Fast and Controllable Streaming Voice Style Conversion

author.name: Yisi Liu, Nicholas Lee, Gopala K. Anumanchipalli

entry.summary: StyleStream 2.0 is a streaming zero-shot voice style conversion framework that reduces end-to-end latency below its predecessor's ~1 second using a few-step pixel MeanFlow model fine-tuned with autoregressive feedback inspired by Self Forcing, and adds a text-based interface for designing and editing target voices. It preserves linguistic content while transferring timbre, accent, and emotion. This advances real-time, controllable speech generation.

entry.title: SSMCGM-Stream: A Streaming State-Space Model for Personalized Diabetes Management

author.name: Shakson Isaac, Chirag Patel

entry.summary: SSMCGM-Stream is a streaming state-space model that maintains a personalized hidden state for constant-time glucose forecasting with interpretable hidden-state attribution and counterfactual reasoning. Paired with SSMCGM-Agent, it provides guarded natural-language decision support, evaluated on the T1DEXI cohort.

entry.title: Where Does Timbre Hide? Localizing Speaker Information in Speech Signals

author.name: Yiquan Zhou, Yixuan Wang, Xiaozhe Qi, Xin Gao, Shihao Li

entry.summary: This paper systematically localizes speaker/timbre information across frequency bands, phase/magnitude structure, source-filter decomposition, voiced/unvoiced regions, SSL layers, and codec tokens, using speaker identity as a proxy plus a 45-listener test across Mandarin, English, and Japanese speech and singing. The findings inform voice conversion and zero-shot TTS quality.

entry.title: Latent space configuration for neural network finetuning, fast ranking, and embedding dimensionality reduction

author.name: Nikita Gabdullin, Anton Raskovalov

entry.summary: The paper proposes search algorithms over structured latent spaces of neural embeddings achieving O(1)-complexity candidate subset search for top-K retrieval, using Latent Space Configuration finetuning of ArcFace-pretrained models to impose desired geometric properties. It reports several-fold speedups over exhaustive search, including up to 3x on specific setups.

entry.title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?

author.name: Ashvin Gupta, Brendan Delaney, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: The authors adapt three JEPA formulations to longitudinal electronic health records and compare against masked language modeling on MIMIC-IV. Although the JEPA variants train stably without representational collapse, they consistently underperform MLM, providing an informative negative result for clinical representation learning.

entry.title: FogTTA: Online Test-Time Adaptation for Robust Transformer-based Object Detection in Foggy Weather

author.name: Ali Abedi, Q. M. Jonathan Wu, Ning Zhang, Shiqi Tian

entry.summary: FogTTA is an online test-time adaptation framework that improves transformer-based object detectors (using RF-DETR) in fog via a teacher-student design, adapting in real time to streaming target-domain data without source data or retraining. It targets the performance drop autonomous driving detectors suffer under adverse weather domain shift.

entry.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory

author.name: Zedong Peng

entry.summary: This short empirical study tests whether purpose-built agent memory systems like Mem0 and Zep still help when the underlying model is strong enough to search raw context itself. Across four memory methods and three coding agents with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna, and Claude Opus 5.5 on one LoCoMo conversation, it finds Mem0 only beats full context with the weakest model, and its build cost can exceed a full-context run.

entry.title: Code Comprehensor: Hierarchical Documentation and Cross-Modal Retrieval for Large Repositories

author.name: Sujoy Roychowdhury, Joseph H. R. Isaac, Jiangning Gao, Martin Klitte, Diarmuid Corcoran

entry.summary: Code Comprehensor combines a code dependency callgraph, CodeScribe (LLM-generated hierarchical documentation over repository call graphs), and CodeContrast (a CLIP-style dual-encoder trained on that documentation) to help LLMs understand large codebases. The aim is to support onboarding, maintenance, refactoring, and impact analysis at scale.

entry.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Zhanshuo Cao, Jiakai Tang, Yuqi Zhou, Sunhao Dai, Jun Xu

entry.summary: The paper shows that sequential recommenders waste compute by assigning a fixed depth to every item in a user history, demonstrating both that items vary drastically in required computation and that oracle non-uniform depth allocation outperforms fixed allocation. It proposes adaptive per-item recursion depth to allocate computation where it matters for the final prediction.

entry.title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering

author.name: Sergey Salishev, Zeev Volkovich, Oleg Granichin

entry.summary: The paper shows that every Transformer block with attention, LayerNorm, and GELU MLP can be compiled exactly into a generic deep neural network using only fixed affine maps, routing, and basic scalar nonlinearities (square, sigmoid, inverse square root, GELU). It quantifies the cost of eliminating activation-activation products, showing at least N-squared extra nonlinear evaluations per head are needed unless that operation type is retained, with implications for NPU design.

entry.title: Dissimilarity-Based Markov Decision Processes for Stabilizing State Distributions

author.name: Xun Shen, Yuepeng Wang, Daniyal Sajedi-Hosseini, Akifumi Wachi, Ken Kawano, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Mehrshad Sadria, S\'ebastien Gros, Katsuki Fujisawa

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for RL policies that stabilize state distributions rather than only maximizing expected return, formulating the problem as a Dissimilarity-based MDP in which the policy acts on the current state distribution and the objective measures its dissimilarity to a target. The authors establish sufficient conditions under which the optimal policy makes the target distribution asymptotically stable.

entry.title: MA-UITD: Offline Multi-Agent Reward Inference for Characterizing Continuous Social Behavior

author.name: Zeyuan Zhang, Yiyun Yang, Yuan Cheng, Herbert Zheng Wu, Yusi Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces MA-UITD, an offline multi-agent inverse reinforcement learning method that infers explicit agent-specific rewards from fixed behavioral datasets without extra environment interaction or inner-loop policy optimization. The approach targets continuous social behavior, connecting imitation learning with the study of neural computations underlying social decision-making.

entry.title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows

author.name: Ewsey Obzherin, Valentin Khrulkov

entry.summary: This paper develops a density-level backward-error framework for low-NFE generative ODE sampling that isolates the solver defect component affecting the evolving marginal distribution, ignoring trajectory-level distortion invisible in Wasserstein geometry. The resulting residual yields a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity fields.

entry.title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data

author.name: Ethan Levien, Trevor GrandPre

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies multiple-instance learning with max pooling, which suffers vanishing gradients, and analyzes learnable-softmax approximations whose sharpness parameter drives learning dynamics. The authors characterize conditions under which training succeeds via phase transitions driven by extremal data, explaining when increasing sharpness during gradient descent works.

entry.title: Fragment-Level Graph Encoding for Interpretable Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Rafael Lopes Almeida (School of Pharmacy, University of Eastern Finland, Kuopio, Finland), Ina P\"ohner (School of Pharmacy, University of Eastern Finland, Kuopio, Finland)

entry.summary: Rather than proposing a new model, the authors change the input representation: molecules become fragment-level graphs via BRICS decomposition so that any GNN and any post-hoc explainer yields explanations at functional-group resolution instead of atoms. Experiments across four architectures, four tasks, and two explainers under scaffold splits show fragment-level encoding preserves or improves accuracy while producing more actionable explanations for medicinal chemists.

entry.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma

author.name: Shihao Shao, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The authors prove a sharp global dynamic analogue of Haussler's covering lemma for bounded real-valued classes in normalized l_p, with cover size (C/eps^p)^d where d is a sequential fat-shattering dimension, plus a matching worst-case lower bound. The result extends classical metric-entropy theory to sequential/online settings with a single family of causal experts.

entry.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks

author.name: Francesco Mori, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Uses a teacher-student framework with a convolutional teacher acting on correlated input positions to derive exact ODEs for the learning dynamics of convolutional versus locally connected students in the large-dimension limit. The analysis separates the contributions of locality and weight sharing and shows their effects depend on spatial correlations of the input.

entry.title: S^3martCirc: Self-supervised Smart Circuit Discovery

author.name: Wendy Zheng, Yinhan He, Liang Wu, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Addresses mechanistic interpretability of LLMs by unifying the typically sequential circuit-discovery and functional-interpretation stages into a self-supervised approach. S^3martCirc argues that identifying important components and determining their roles should inform each other rather than proceed in two disconnected stages.

entry.title: KIRA: A Full-Stack Reading Screening System with Dual-Pathway Analysis for Children

author.name: Maggie Dong, Rohit Mekkoth, Zixuan Wang, Cheol Jun Cho, Jiachen Lian, Gopala Anumanchipalli

entry.summary: Presents KIRA, a dual-pathway reading-difficulty screening system combining word-level fluency scoring with phoneme-level error detection, adapting pretrained word and phoneme recognizers to children's speech (reducing word error rate from 13.88% to 8.84% and phoneme error rate from 41.66% to 23.00%). It implements Word Reading and Oral Reading Fluency tasks used in K-2 screening with transparent evaluation, contrasting with proprietary screeners.

entry.title: One Policy, Many Styles: Where to Aggregate Preferences for Steerable Humanoid Control?

author.name: Ziqian Huang, Yuzhuo Chen, Shimin Zhang, Junyang He, Xinyue Annie Yang, Animesh Garg

entry.summary: The paper studies preference-conditioned reinforcement learning for humanoid robots, where a single policy must adjust behavioral style at runtime without leaking into unrelated behaviors or hurting task performance. It introduces Preference Reward Responsiveness plus coverage and utility metrics, and compares reward-level, advantage-level, loss-level, and PCGrad-based preference aggregation across two humanoid-control frameworks. The key finding is that no aggregation level dominates across environments and criteria, providing practical guidance for steerable robot control.

entry.title: A Decade of Learning-Based Control: From Theoretic Foundations to Practical Deployment

author.name: Angela P. Schoellig, Matthias A. M\"uller, Sebastian Trimpe, Melanie N. Zeilinger, Mahathi Anand, Andrea Carron, Oliver Hausd\"orfer, Victor G. Lopez, Friedrich Solowjow, Haocheng Zhao, Siqi Zhou

entry.summary: This tutorial paper reviews ten years of advances at the intersection of machine learning and control, motivated by the Learning-Based Control Invited Sessions at IEEE CDC. It covers stability and safety guarantees, learned dynamics models for control under uncertainty, and data-driven policy synthesis via reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and Bayesian optimization, through to practical deployment. Authored by leading groups in the field, it serves as an authoritative reference for safe, capable autonomous systems.

entry.title: Supervision-Adaptive Curriculum and Guarded Anti-Curriculum Learning for Dense Prediction

author.name: Chunming He, Dingming Zhang, Fengyang Xiao, Zhiwen Cao, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: Extending the conference method CurriSeg, this paper introduces PaceShift, a stabilize-then-challenge paradigm for dense prediction that separates supervision reliability from temporal update value. It estimates sample reliability from supervision, augmentation consistency, model disagreement, and prediction certainty, then applies guarded spectral challenges after stabilization. The approach addresses the fact that sample difficulty alone does not capture label reliability in dense prediction tasks.

entry.title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications

author.name: Yan Gong, Zheng Chu, Wei Koong Chai, Hari Mohan Pandey, Jingrui Hou, Miao Zhang, Yuanjian Li, Pei Xiao

entry.summary: The paper introduces ComRSI, a framework where a fixed LLM-based agent recursively edits the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy of a semantic communication system, with a protected evaluator screening candidates under resource budgets. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals while weights are trained from scratch. Across a ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions yield an improved architecture.

entry.title: Mastering Model Fit: Applications of the InterModel Vigorish for Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Jiani Yan, Pengyun Wang, Klint Kanopka, Ben Domingue, Charles Rahal

entry.summary: The authors adapt the InterModel Vigorish (IMV), a betting-advantage measure of probabilistic fit, into machine learning evaluation, proposing SHAP-IMV for feature attribution, Multi-IMV for class discrimination, and Ablate-IMV for architectural component analysis. They validate the toolkit across tabular, image, sensor, and graph data over multiple seeds.

entry.title: Scan or Index? large Evidence Coverage, Answer Quality, and Cost in Long-Document RAG

author.name: Juan Terven, Diana-Margarita C\'ordova-Esparza, Julio-Alejandro Romero-Gonz\'alez, Edgar Chavez-Urbiola, Juan Irving Vasquez, Julian Andres Ramirez-Bautista, Silvia L. Chaparro-C\'ardenas, Gendry Alfonso-Francia

entry.summary: The authors compare 11 retrieval configurations for long-document RAG, including lexical, dense, hybrid reranking, and full-document scanning, on 396 QASPER questions and 80 textbook questions with a fixed answer generator. They find higher evidence coverage does not directly translate to better answers, and that full scans can still lose relevant evidence in later reduction steps.

entry.title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression

author.name: Oliver Giudice, Anna Russo Russo

entry.summary: Proposes compressing LLM embedding layers via a factorization scheme augmented with learnable non-linear projections inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, addressing the representational bottleneck of standard low-rank linear factorization. The method targets vocabulary-heavy embedding matrices, a major memory cost in modern LLMs. The paper notes KANs remain under-explored in NLP despite promise elsewhere.

entry.title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering

author.name: Kuniko Paxton, Ifeoluwa Wuraola, Dhavalkumar Thakker

entry.summary: Studies whether reduced bias in compressed small language models reflects fairer behavior or greater abstention, using the BBQ benchmark across model sizes and quantization settings of Qwen3, Gemma-3, and SmolLM2. Results show larger models achieve higher QA accuracy but bias shows no simple scaling trend, and quantization effects vary across configurations. Notably, many apparent bias reductions disappear under forced-choice settings that remove the Unknown option.

entry.title: Investigating the Impact of Learner Errors on Social Bias in Large Language Models

author.name: Federico Marcuzzi, Martin Christoph, Iryna Gurevych, Alla Rozovskays

entry.summary: This study shows that social bias benchmarks systematically underrepresent non-native English speakers by testing only fluent, well-formed prompts. The authors build a controlled framework that injects common learner grammatical errors into three bias benchmarks covering stereotype alignment and demographic preference, finding that errors increase measured bias and that the effect scales with error rate, with preposition errors producing the largest increase in stereotype alignment.

entry.title: Task-Preserving Multilingual Instruction Tuning for Open-Ended QA in WMT 2026 MIST

author.name: Aleix Sant, Jordi Luque, Carlos Escolano

entry.summary: A WMT 2026 shared-task submission that adapts Qwen3-8B with LoRA using the EuroAlpaca multilingual instruction dataset and a cross-lingual augmentation (CrossEuroAlpaca) that mixes source and target languages across instructions, contexts, and responses. The system targets open-ended QA in ten languages and reports a 7.8% relative improvement in Gemma-4 judge scores over the base model under matched decoding.

entry.title: RoPT: Robust 6DoF Object Pose Tracking in Video

author.name: Yongqing Liang, Yuzhong Chen, Sihang Li, Junsuk Kim, Chase Kidder, Hui-ping Wang, Yunzhi Xu, Raihan Haque, Yubiao Zhang, Chen Feng

entry.summary: RoPT unifies visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization in a closed-loop framework for 6-DoF object pose tracking in video. Mask-based perception handles occlusion while a kinematic factor graph regularizes updates, forecasts poses, and runs parallel multi-hypothesis tracking to prevent catastrophic divergence under rapid motion.

entry.title: LocalAgent: Collaborative Agentic Verification for Fine-Grained Instance-Level Consistency

author.name: Jiachen Guo, Xinshan Zhu, Boyun Wang, Yanyan Liang, Jun Wan, Feng Lin, Ajian Liu

entry.summary: LocalAgent tackles fine-grained instance-level verification—deciding whether two images show the exact same physical object—by combining a generalist MLLM that reasons globally to flag suspicious regions with lightweight specialist verifiers that examine local evidence. The agentic collaboration bridges global semantic perception and precise local scrutiny.

entry.title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI

author.name: Han Hu, He Chen

entry.summary: The authors evaluate seven locally deployable VLMs, including models built for physical AI and robotics, on thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction. Thermal sensing extends robot perception to darkness and privacy-sensitive settings, but VLM failure modes in this modality were underexplored. The study provides an empirical taxonomy of where RGB-trained VLMs break down on thermal imagery.

entry.title: OpenEarth-OVS44: A Multimodal Remote Sensing Dataset for Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Yimin Wei, Hongruixuan Chen, Hao Zheng, Hao Liu, Jian Song, Yuting Zhu, Junshi Xia, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: OpenEarth-OVS44 is a multimodal remote sensing benchmark for open-vocabulary segmentation with 290,587 expert-verified segments from 2,832 RGB images and 1,341 additional modality images, using a fine-grained 44-class-style taxonomy beyond coarse land-cover labels. It targets applications like urban zoning, carbon accounting, and post-disaster assessment that need generalization to novel categories. The dataset addresses limited category coverage in prior remote sensing segmentation resources.

entry.title: Efficient Generative Image Compression with Quantized Latents Refinement

author.name: Hao Cao, Yinhuan Huang, Wenqi Guo, Zhijin Qin, Jungong Han

entry.summary: Proposes GR-GIC, an efficient generative image compression method that identifies how coarse quantization collapses nearby latents holding distinct fine details, and introduces Guided Refinement combining latent refinement with guidance to recover them. It achieves competitive perceptual quality at low bitrates with fast inference, avoiding reliance on heavy pretrained diffusion models.

entry.title: Compositionality with Primitives: A Unified View from Euclidean to Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models

author.name: Puru Vaish, Meelad Dashti, Christoph Brune, Pascal Mettes, Tatiana Tommasi, Nicola Strisciuglio

entry.summary: Revisits compositional zero-shot learning by questioning whether explicit attribute-object recomposition is necessary, introducing new compositional scoring functions and a unified view spanning Euclidean and hyperbolic vision-language embeddings. Builds on the Geodesically Decomposable Embeddings framework that identifies primitive concept directions.

entry.title: ClunoGS: Compact Language 3D Gaussian Splatting via Unified Optimization

author.name: Jian Xu, Yi Li, Ying Huang, Siyi Wu, Bingzhe Li, Yuede Ji, Miao Yin

entry.summary: ClunoGS addresses storage blow-up in Language 3D Gaussian Splatting by jointly performing semantics-aware sparsification and vector quantization in a unified optimization rather than sequential pruning then quantization. This preserves Gaussians that matter for open-vocabulary semantic prediction even when their RGB contribution is small.

entry.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation

author.name: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song, Mingyang Sun, Xingjun Ma, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: DepState-JEPA is a dual-stream RGB-depth joint-embedding predictive architecture, built on V-JEPA 2.1, that grounds a shared latent state DepState in metric 3D space so scene geometry connects with action-conditioned state changes for manipulation. Depth serves both as a complementary observation and as a grounding signal for both modalities.

entry.title: State-Dependent Objective Coordination for End-to-End Balance and Navigation

author.name: Xuhao Huang, Xitao Xu, Yuxin Zheng, Yunfan Ren, Zheng Gong

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for end-to-end RL navigation on unstable two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots. A pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient dynamically adjusts the trade-off between balance stabilization and navigation progress, replacing cascaded mapping-planning-control pipelines.

entry.title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning

author.name: Yijun Shen, Diqi He, Jinbang Guo, Wanyue Zhang, Jiaming Mi, Huan Yang, Zhongyuan Wang, Zhiwei Yu, Kai Zhang

entry.summary: CausGround is a non-parametric framework that distills embodied interaction experience into reusable, action-centered causal knowledge capturing action preconditions and effects, enabling multimodal LLM-based planners to adapt to new environments without environment-specific training. It organizes this knowledge in a factorized structure to support adaptive embodied planning.

entry.title: Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery

author.name: Osher Azulay, Cheng-Lin Hsieh, Stella X. Yu

entry.summary: Presents RISE, an approach to humanoid fall recovery that lets task objectives steer which recovery motion is executed at inference time, by composing diverse recoveries from shared movements and anticipating how movements unfold physically. It addresses control over which of several valid stand-up strategies the robot chooses.

entry.title: What's in CODI's latent recurrent thoughts?

author.name: Jan Bauer

entry.summary: This post investigates whether the latent recurrent thoughts of CODI, a latent-reasoning model, can be decoded using activation verbalizers, building on prior work showing the thoughts causally carry intermediate computation values. Using a Qwen3-8B-based CODI, the author finds activation verbalizers weakly but significantly recover intermediate values, while LogitLens and J-lens only read values from late layers; however, editing the decoded values rarely steers outputs to counterfactual answers. This matters because it probes the interpretability of latent reasoning, an emerging alternative to verbal chain-of-thought.

entry.title: A general approach for alignment generalization and a Stupid New Technique that beat everything

author.name: AlexG

entry.summary: The author proposes Ironman Runs as a general method for alignment generalization: achieving competitive scores on a new capability benchmark without any samples from that domain, forcing technique design from first principles. Using a disposition-based approach inspired by Shard Theory, they report top-5 refusal scores on old agentic and code benchmarks with a Hermes-3 8B model (a 2024-era model with no refusal training) using only prefills and SFT samples and modest compute.

entry.title: Minimum required pacing: finish aligning it before you train the next one

author.name: orthonormal

entry.summary: A proposal on the AI Alignment Forum for coordinated frontier pacing: a lab should not train the next capability generation until all significant alignment issues in the current generation are adequately resolved. The author argues this creates better incentives — labs must advance alignment and interpretability research to advance capabilities — and can appeal to both prosaic-alignment optimists and pessimists for different reasons.

entry.title: Which Differences Matter? Controlled Tests of Rule Transfer, Joint Reliability, and Information Use in Decision Models

author.name: Tianyou Lai, Wentao Yue, Zhiwei Zuo, Qilei Li

entry.summary: Using executable arithmetic rules, this work designs controlled input changes to separately measure rule transfer, joint reliability, and directed information use in decision models, including marginal-preserving reassociation to calibrate joint correctness. Findings show adaptation gains depend on answer agreement between sources, and equivalent rewordings can produce divergent behavior.

entry.title: Block Diffusion for Longitudinal EHR: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Representation Trade-offs

author.name: Ashvin Gupta, Joshua Placidi, Brendan Delaney, Alessandra Russo

entry.summary: This paper evaluates block-based masked diffusion as an alternative to autoregressive models for zero-shot prediction on longitudinal EHRs under matched conditions on MIMIC-IV. Small-block diffusion retains most predictive performance while enabling faster inference, with a representative configuration achieving roughly 1.43x faster evaluation, though generative rollout remains below AR quality.

entry.title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition

author.name: Pavlos Poulos, Katelyn Sadorf, Themos Stafylakis, Costas A. Anastassiou

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU), which decouples temporal filtering in a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit from spike generation in downstream Resonate-and-Fire neurons, addressing LIF neuron limitations on continuous tasks like speech recognition. The bio-inspired design targets energy-efficient, event-driven computation while retaining long-range context.

entry.title: Privacy in Context Is Being Overlooked in the Age of General-Purpose LLMs

author.name: Prakhar Ganesh, Yash More, Marco Romanelli, Ferdinando Fioretto, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: This position paper argues that prompt-privacy research is drifting toward one-size-fits-all unified frameworks, contradicting decades of contextual privacy scholarship. The authors contend this trend is misleading, fosters false security, and that any future unified approach must confront fundamental tensions among desirable privacy properties.

entry.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning

author.name: Xiangyu Sun, Shirin Hosseinmardi, Ramin Bostanabad

entry.summary: The SNTO framework represents state, adjoint, and design variables with custom neural networks jointly optimized in a single loop using continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation, targeting large-scale stress-constrained topology optimization. A multi-component loss combines design objective, aggregated local stress constraints, and potential energy, with an architecture designed for sharp gradients and faster convergence.

entry.title: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization

author.name: Dominik Jehle, Tom Zehle

entry.summary: This work proposes a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework that automatically discovers task-specific multi-agent system topologies by combining evolutionary generation of workflow graphs with a graph-aware Gaussian Process and Expected Improvement criterion for candidate selection. It reports strong results on BigCodeBench code generation and a TabPFN-based tabular preprocessing benchmark.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Probabilistic Fusion for Multimodal Learning with Incomplete Evidence

author.name: Patitapaban Palo, Abhisek Tiwari, Mattia Carletti, Anshul Thakur, Xiao Gu, David A. Clifton

entry.summary: The authors introduce a reliability-aware Gaussian Product-of-Experts in which an input-dependent weight tempers each modality's latent precision and missing experts are omitted, with a theoretical characterization of how reliability and availability shape posterior influence. On two clinical multimodal tasks the method stays competitive with complete inputs and shows its clearest AUROC advantage under modality absence, notably on HAIM-MIMIC-MM.

entry.title: Tropical Cyclone Attributes in Sparse Autoencoder Features of an AI Weather Model

author.name: Jiapei Liu, Ruidong Li, Ting Sun, Guangheng Ni

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders to probe how GraphCast, an established AI weather model, internally represents tropical cyclones, relating SAE activations to cyclone position, intensity, and pressure structure across 2,115 timesteps from 205 cyclones. It finds attributes map to multiple overlapping features with organization that recurs across independent SAEs and layers.

entry.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials

author.name: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

entry.summary: The authors prove that every gradient trajectory of a definable C1 potential, including unbounded ones, has finite spherical projection length, i.e., finite total angular motion and directional convergence. This extends the celebrated gradient conjecture results (previously limited to bounded trajectories within o-minimal structures) to trajectories diverging to infinity, with no uniqueness assumptions. The result is a significant advance in the nonsmooth analysis underpinning convergence guarantees for gradient-based optimization.

entry.title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?

author.name: Li Zhang, Kevin Ashley

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLMs form internal representations corresponding to the 26 CATO legal factors used in symbolic case-based reasoning, testing linear decodability of these structured legal concepts. It connects classic AI-and-Law symbolic frameworks with modern mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: C$^2$U in RAG: Compositional Concept Unlearning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yiyang Duan, Fan Wu, Tiantong Wu, Che Wang, Zhiren Gong, Wei Guo, Yang Cao, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: C2U addresses query-side concept suppression in RAG, routing profile-derived directions through an augmented atom bank to add bounded edits to raw queries with a fixed encoder and index. Across five datasets and four encoders it reduces exposure to target concepts in retrieved evidence without degrading control queries, addressing a gap where moderation of the generator alone cannot prevent leaked concepts.

entry.title: B-CARE: Blind Classwise Assessment of Relative Evidence for Stance Error Ranking

author.name: Meysam Sabbaghan, Doina Caragea

entry.summary: Introduces B-CARE, a prediction-blind framework for ranking high-risk stance classifier predictions under limited human-review budgets. A fixed LLM verifier assigns ordinal evidence scores to all candidate labels without seeing the base model's prediction, and a comparative risk score contrasts alternative-class evidence against predicted-class evidence. This enables cross-model error prioritization for heterogeneous base classifiers.

entry.title: NeuralSRender: G-Buffer Guided Video Diffusion for Sim-to-Real Rendering

author.name: Yipeng Lu, Youqi Liao, Zhenyu Wang, Yuning Peng, Zhen Dong

entry.summary: NeuralSRender is a sim-to-real video translation framework for autonomous driving that uses a pretrained video diffusion transformer with a lightweight projector injecting G-buffer geometric and material priors, plus LoRA for parameter-efficient adaptation. Two-stage training preserves geometric consistency with source scenes while boosting photorealism of synthetic videos.

entry.title: Seeing through Denoising: Frequency-guided One-step Denoising for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Xuelin Qian, Zixuan Wang, Chang Xu, Dingwen Zhang, Junwei Han

entry.summary: DiffIRSTD reformulates infrared small target detection as background reconstruction, using a diffusion-based generative model to recover a clean target-free background so targets emerge by difference. It employs frequency-guided one-step denoising for efficiency. This generative reframe contrasts with the dominant discriminative paradigm in IRSTD.

entry.title: Learning to Measure and Diagnose: A Clinical-Dictionary Radiomic Bottleneck Model for Thyroid Nodule Classification

author.name: Guibin Zhang, Weier Luo, Lei Cao

entry.summary: Introduces a clinical-dictionary radiomic bottleneck model for thyroid nodule classification, with Family-Aware Radiomic Learning for balanced measurement estimation and Fidelity-Guided Bottleneck Modeling to preserve measurement fidelity during classification optimization. The goal is predictions whose evidence maps to familiar clinical descriptions.

entry.title: Training-free Acceleration for Blind Compressed Image Restoration via Activation-Calibrated Singular Value Decomposition

author.name: Suhang Yao, Xin Li, Xijun Wang, Yufei Wang, Yeying Jin, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Studies training-free acceleration of transformer-based blind compressed image restoration by profiling computation, characterizing channel-wise activations under compressed inputs, and identifying recurring projection operators as low-rank replacement targets via activation-calibrated SVD, all while preserving the original inference graph.

entry.title: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance

author.name: Taiga Ikeshima, Sheila Sutjipto, Lan Wu, Francisco J. Naranjo-Campos, Taiki Ishigaki, Taisuke Kobayashi, Teresa A. Vidal-Calleja, Eiichi Yoshida

entry.summary: This RL framework integrates Euclidean Distance Fields directly into the observation space for manipulator collision avoidance, giving the agent continuous geometric cues for stable, responsive behavior. It is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator with a streamlined reward formulation, with or without Artificial Potential Field guidance.

entry.title: Distilling Multi-Teacher Scoring Principles for Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Dongchan Cho, Jiho Han, Juwon Hwang, Changhee Min, Minsang Kim, Namsoon Jung

entry.summary: AnoMix distills heterogeneous unsupervised time-series anomaly detectors into a single lightweight student, extracting weak pairwise supervision from frozen teachers' training-set anomaly scores without labels. It normalizes teacher scores independently and uses a ranking-based loss, avoiding the inference and maintenance cost of running an ensemble.

entry.title: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining

author.name: Xintong Liu, Chenkai Zhang, Yanzhao Ma, Peng Yang

entry.summary: LineageEvo improves LLM-based evolutionary mining of formulaic alpha factors by introducing lineage-level search control, connecting successive factor variants through evolutionary descent rather than operating only at individual and population levels. This addresses weak directionality and concentration around structurally similar factors in the conventional LLM-EA paradigm.

entry.title: Every Alarm Has a Cause: An Open Generator of Telecom Alarm Storms with Exact Root Causes, Bound to NORIA-O, RFC 8632 and TMF642

author.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

entry.summary: This paper presents a generator, rather than a fixed dataset, for telecom alarm storms with exact per-incident root causes and propagation paths recorded as a by-product of generation. It runs on real Internet Topology Zoo backbone topologies and binds every field to standards terms (NORIA-O, RFC 8632/8345, TMF642), with fixed configurations, splits, and licensing.

entry.title: GaP-MoE : Explicit Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts via Orthogonal Gradient Accumulation and Projection

author.name: Donghyun Jeong, Yoon-Yeong Kim

entry.summary: GaP-MoE combats representation collapse in sparse Mixture-of-Experts models by directly manipulating expert gradients through orthogonal gradient accumulation and projection, rather than modifying routers or adding auxiliary similarity penalties. This induces expert specialization without conflicting with the primary task objective.

entry.title: Implicit Feature Reweighting for Label-Free Graph Generalization

author.name: Tianjun Yao, Chen Xi, Xinyang Li, Lixian Zhong

entry.summary: SCARCE is a label-free framework for graph-level out-of-distribution generalization that learns shift-robust representations using only an environment partition of training graphs, obtained from metadata or self-supervised clustering when unavailable. It uses a two-stage pipeline with a warm-started variational graph autoencoder and implicit feature reweighting to identify predictive substructures without class labels.

entry.title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization

author.name: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Tianyi Lin, Wenxuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper examines predict-then-optimize systems that return decisions without revealing cost vectors, showing that for linear prediction models an attacker can often recover the model up to positive scaling from decisions across contexts. It develops an adaptive attack alternating inverse optimization with boundary sampling and motivates defenses against such model extraction.

entry.title: Is Refusal Direction Universal across Low-Resourced Languages?

author.name: Anastasiia Ivanova

entry.summary: Tests whether the widely studied linear refusal direction transfers universally by extending the PolyRefuse pipeline to Belarusian, Bashkir, and Tajik on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, beyond the single previously evaluated low-resourced language. Findings show universality is graded: directions from safety-aligned languages transfer broadly, while those from strongly misaligned languages transfer poorly.

entry.title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness

author.name: Dimitris Oikonomou, Nicolas Loizou

entry.summary: The paper analyzes SAM-type optimizers under generalized (L0, L1)-smoothness rather than standard smoothness, introducing relative gradient distortion to quantify how the sharpness-aware direction departs from the gradient. It shows this distortion can become unbounded for SAM near stationarity and for USAM at large gradients, with constructed counterexamples, and proposes curvature-scaled variants with convergence guarantees beyond smoothness. This strengthens the theoretical foundations of a widely used training method.

entry.title: How Far Can the Gemma 4 Speech Encoder Go Without Changing Its Weights? Saudi and Gulf Arabic Speech Recognition with a Frozen and an Adapter-Augmented Encoder

author.name: Amr Abdelkhalik

entry.summary: A single-author study applying the frozen 305M-parameter audio encoder shared by Gemma 4 and EmbeddingGemma-2 (an existing released model family) to Saudi and Gulf Arabic speech recognition using only a CTC reader plus small adapters. The frozen system statistically matches a much larger commercial transcription model on character error rate in most conditions while running 3.4x faster on CPU.

entry.title: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation

author.name: Simran Khanuja, Rohit Gandikota, Gaurav Parmar, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: T-DIG is a text-conditioned framework that lets users control which axis of diversity (background, style, clothing, etc.) varies across a set of images generated for a prompt. It uses an iterative multi-module design for both generation and editing, addressing the fact that T2I models optimized for single-image quality yield low multi-image diversity.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary Models and Label Propagation for Uncertainty-aware Pseudo-Labeling of Object Detection Datasets

author.name: Jonathan Klees, Timo Heller, Matthias Rottmann

entry.summary: Introduces a semi-supervised framework for uncertainty-aware annotation of detection datasets: open-vocabulary detectors generate proposals and object representations, an object-level similarity graph is built, and probabilistic label information is propagated to assign soft labels with quantified uncertainty to unlabeled objects.

entry.title: Reading the Room: Scale-ambiguous Semantic Registration of Sparse VSLAM Maps to Floor Plans in Partially Built Environments

author.name: Bjorn Stragier, Emilia Szyma\'nska, J. Micah Prendergast, Lukas Rosenberger Schmid

entry.summary: This paper introduces Reading the Room, a global-local method for registering scale-ambiguous, sparse VSLAM maps to symbolic 2D floor plans in partially built construction sites, tackling cross-modal alignment, unknown scale, and visually repetitive scenes simultaneously. It targets robotic applications like construction progress tracking.

entry.title: Object- and Task-Aware Active Perception for Safe Navigation of Mobile Manipulators in Semi-Static Environments

author.name: Jingxing Qian, Xintong Du, Jun Yang, Siqi Zhou, Steven L. Waslander, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Introduces an active perception framework in which a mobile manipulator uses its hand camera during navigation to inspect safety-critical or uncertain regions, with a probabilistic object- and task-aware next-best-view formulation integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control. Targets semi-static environments where scene knowledge becomes stale between visits.

entry.title: Inheritance as an Admission Test for LLM Prompt Merge Operators

author.name: Zan-Kai Chong, Hiroyuki Ohsaki, Bryan Ng

entry.summary: The paper proposes scoring LLM agents against a current population with a frozen panel to detect genuine improvement, counting a run as training only when its final mean beats the best generation-zero member. It introduces a formal admission test for prompt merge operators requiring detectable movement toward the donor beyond a zero-dose baseline with a confidence bound on the movement.

entry.title: When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models

author.name: Rushab Munot

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether calibrated decision models remain reliable when multiple choices are correct, testing three models including GPT-6 Luna Decisions on MetaTool, HotpotQA, and ECtHR. Even when models rank all correct choices above distractors, 28-50% of lists contain a correct choice assigned below-uniform probability, revealing asymmetric probability allocation that breaks thresholding. This exposes a calibration blind spot for downstream selection applications.

entry.title: AgentMonopoly: Behavioral Patterns and Persona Control in LLM Agents

author.name: Changshun Wu, Mengyu Li, Mathis Marsault, Xiaowei Huang, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: AgentMonopoly is an environment where LLM agents communicate, buy, and trade properties in a Monopoly-style game, used to study behavioral differences across four model families at two sizes and the effect of persona instructions. Findings include substantial differences in trading, rent-waiving, and cash management behavior, and that larger models do not consistently win more games. It provides a controlled setting for studying multi-agent strategic behavior and steerability.

entry.title: COMET: A coordinated multi-layer runtime monitoring framework for human-supervised AI-enabled safety systems

author.name: Niclas Flehmig, Mary Ann Lundteigen, Shen Yin

entry.summary: COMET is a runtime monitoring framework for AI-enabled safety systems that coordinates three monitoring layers (signal integrity, physics consistency, and competence envelope) and presents results to human supervisors via a traffic-light display. It is evaluated on an open dataset of compressed-air systems, aiming to give human supervisors actionable information rather than single opaque monitor outputs.

entry.title: Robust Soft Skill Adaptation via Behavioral Localization in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Zijian Jiang, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: The authors observe that the beneficial effect of a text skill given to a tool-using agent is concentrated in a small subset of trajectory positions rather than spread across the whole trajectory. They propose Behavioral Localization, which compares a frozen agent with and without the skill to identify positions where the skill increases the likelihood of successful tokens and meaningfully shifts the next-token distribution, then uses only these positions to train a compact soft prompt. Experiments on SpreadsheetBench show this yields effective soft-skill adaptation while avoiding unnecessary behavioral changes from full-trajectory training.

entry.title: Offline Apprenticeship Learning for Human-Centric Environments

author.name: Md Mirajul Islam

entry.summary: A dissertation developing offline apprenticeship learning frameworks for human-centric domains such as intelligent tutoring systems and clinical healthcare, organized around reward modeling and demonstration quality. It introduces methods like EM-EDM for clustering demonstrations by latent reward functions and THEMES for trajectory partitioning. The strictly offline setting addresses ethical and safety constraints of deploying RL in human-facing systems.

entry.title: A General Topological Symmetry Index for Critical Orbits In Neural Network Loss Landscapes

author.name: Jingzhou Liu

entry.summary: The paper establishes a topological symmetry index, based on equivariant degree theory, to systematically characterize symmetries in neural network loss landscapes and their induced critical orbits. The framework applies to arbitrary network architectures, including degenerate critical orbits that prior methods cannot handle. It contributes mathematical structure to the study of why neural loss landscapes behave as they do.

entry.title: PHD-Hand: A Printable Humanoid Dexterous Hand with Linkage-Driven 3-DOA Digits

author.name: Neel Adwani, Muhaiminul Islam Akash, Saffia Ouali, Ethan Liu, Cong Wang

entry.summary: PHD-Hand is a printable humanoid dexterous hand using linkage-driven digits with three degrees of actuation each, addressing the reliability, cost, and maintenance problems of tendon-driven designs. It presents one of the few fully linkage-driven humanoid hands achieving 3-DOA per digit without compromising actuator placement.

entry.title: From Augmentation to Synthetic Evidence: Evaluating Generated Chest Radiographs at Dataset Intake

author.name: Shaikh Akib Shahriyar, Zinedine Sehili, Adam Arthur, Christopher Schwartz

entry.summary: This study separates three questions for generated chest radiographs entering datasets: automated quality checking, origin classification (using a classifier on frozen DINOv3 features), and trusted-record verification of claimed acquisitions. LLM-based selection with Qwen improves quality pass rates for Cheff and SynthCheX generated images, framing synthetic images as potential unsupported medical evidence.

entry.title: OmniSimulator: Aligning Small Language Models for Authentic Heterogeneous Behavior Modeling

author.name: Jiawei Chen, Ruoxi Xu, Boxi Cao, Zhuoqun Li, Ruotong Pan, Yunfei Zhang, Zhirui Yang, Jingyan Chen, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han, Le Sun, Xiangyu Wu, Hongyu Lin

entry.summary: OmniSimulator is a training framework that improves small LLMs as user simulators, focused on short-video platform environments, by organizing behavioral factors beyond native chain-of-thought reasoning. It addresses the problem that CoT degenerates into shallow pattern matching and fails to capture the real drivers of user decisions.

entry.title: Conflicted Records: Typed Adversarial Contracts for Auditable LLM Output Quality Enforcement

author.name: Kardelen Subasi, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: The paper observes that LLM-generated records in production systems can simultaneously satisfy and violate a quality rule (e.g., a grounded fact adjacent to a hallucination), a situation classical data cleaning and single LLM judges cannot resolve because judgments conflict over the same span. The authors propose typed adversarial contracts that enforce auditable LLM output quality, providing an audit trail that distinguishes genuine remediation from blanket error suppression. This is significant for deploying LLMs as data producers where records must meet database-grade quality standards.

entry.title: Robot Generalization Beyond Volume: The Diversity Path via Zero-Shot Capabilities

author.name: Rafael Felix

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that zero-shot generalization in physical AI depends more on data diversity than volume, contrasting crowd-sourced digital data with the concentrated paid collection typical in robotics. It formalizes zero-shot generalization as coverage of the deployment distribution and proposes a shared latent space for robot actions to leverage contributor diversity.

entry.title: Graph Topology Meets Energy-Driven Pathfinding: Preserving Contextual Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yufeng Li, Zaijing Li, Fuchen Zhang, Zongzong Wu, Ming Zhao, Fengxiao Tang

entry.summary: ThreadRAG addresses bottlenecks in knowledge-graph-based RAG for multi-hop QA: semantic loss when distilling text into graph symbols, and modality mismatch between fragmented graph structures and continuous text. It proposes a semantic-topology framework for context-preserving knowledge structuring and modality-native evidence reasoning.

entry.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Ava Emami, Tsuyoshi Id\'e, Rajiv Joshi, Steven Holmes, Michael Passow, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: WaferHDC is an online open-world framework for wafer defect discovery built on hyperdimensional computing, designed to detect novel defect signatures emerging during semiconductor manufacturing without retraining static classifiers. Its memory-centric architecture groups recurring failures into compact hypervector representations whose memory footprint scales dynamically with new defect modes.

entry.title: Local and Sparse Kernel Operator Learning for Incompressible Flows: An Operator Lagrange Formulation

author.name: Ramansh Sharma, Matthew Lowery, Houman Owhadi, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: The authors present a local and sparse kernel method for learning solution operators of incompressible flows, replacing the global output reconstruction of their earlier property-preserving kernel method with local divergence-free interpolants solved in parallel on GPU. A compactly supported positive-semidefinite kernel makes operator regression sparse, with support radius fitted to data, and the method preserves divergence-freeness and periodicity while approaching Kolmogorov statistics under refinement.

entry.title: Reader--Writer Coupling in Transformer MLPs

author.name: Giyeong Oh, Sunghee Ahn, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: This interpretability paper analyzes transformer MLP layers as key-value memories, examining how the reader (gate) and writer (value) factors of hidden channels are coupled through joint training updates. Using the exact Jacobian of the MLP update, it derives reader-writer inner-product terms that characterize channel behavior in the residual stream.

entry.title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?

author.name: Jay Agarwal, Siddharth Khare, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: This systematic study distills six physics-informed and pretrained teachers, including two foundation models, into five small students for jet tagging at the LHC, finding that every teacher improves every student and gains depend mainly on teacher strength. It identifies how small students can get while approaching state-of-the-art performance under strict experiment inference budgets.

entry.title: Shortcut-Resistant CAM Distillation for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Wenhai Wan, Teng Zhang, Shao-Yuan Li, Xinrui Wang, Qiang-Sheng Hua, Songcan Chen

entry.summary: This paper reframes long-tailed recognition as a shortcut-learning problem, showing tail classes are especially prone to non-semantic cues like background context because scarce examples share similar environments. It proposes SRCD, a plug-and-play framework that distills class activation maps resistant to shortcuts to encourage object-centric representations for rare classes.

entry.title: Characterizing Oblivious Common-Reward Multi-Player Bandits: Universal Stationarity, Coordination Traps, and Certified Global Rates

author.name: Mingxiao Li, Wenhai Lai, Hongyu Wang

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes a minimal multi-player bandit model where oblivious players choose arms simultaneously and observe only a shared reward. It proves independent gradient-bandit updates form an unbiased estimator of a hidden product-policy objective, yielding universal first-order stationarity guarantees, while also showing stationarity can mask coordination traps and characterizing global rates.

entry.title: ExGrad: Beyond Suppression - Explicit Clean-Gradient Subtraction in Adversarial Training

author.name: Zhiyuan Ye, Xiangyu Zhou, Ji Qi, Hao Zhang, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces ExGrad, which decomposes adversarial training updates into clean-input, adversarial-input, and adversarial-weight-perturbed gradients, then solves a small global optimization to recompose them. Empirically, negative clean-gradient coefficients predominate at larger attack radii, and explicitly subtracting clean gradients improves PGD-20 robustness on CIFAR-10 beyond what zeroing them achieves.

entry.title: A Reverse-Gold Theorem: Positive-Data Identification by Substrate-Bounded Contrastive Learners

author.name: Rakesh Sengupta

entry.summary: Proves a positive counterpart to Gold's theorem: with an innate recursive contrast operator and a capacity-bounded scorer trained via InfoNCE-style contrastive estimation on self-generated perturbations, PAC conditional identification of a language from positive data alone becomes achievable under a faithfulness condition. This shows bounded contrastive learners can identify structure that unbounded positive-data learners provably cannot.

entry.title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning

author.name: Paris A. Karakasis, Walid Saad

entry.summary: This tutorial unifies the largely independent study of extracting common components from jointly observed measurements across statistics (canonical correlation analysis), information theory (Gacs-Korner and Wyner common information), and engineering (subspace methods for sensor arrays). It presents the main results and tools of each community on recovering unsupervised common components. Such cross-community synthesis is valuable for researchers in multi-view representation learning and information-theoretic ML.

entry.title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization over Decentralized Networks

author.name: Haomin Bai, Junyan Sun, Quan Cheng, Yuanyu Wan, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies group distributionally robust optimization over decentralized networks, moving beyond prior work that optimized only dual-regularized surrogates with guarantees for an unavailable globally averaged model. The authors directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized and fully decentralized settings, developing a novel error decomposition to handle unavailable cross-worker information. This strengthens the theory of robust decentralized learning.

entry.title: Asynchronous, Generation-Free ABC: Streaming AMIS Reweighting for Heterogeneous Simulator Workloads on HPC

author.name: Julian Herold, Markus G\"otz, Alexander Schug

entry.summary: This paper removes the generation synchronization barrier in approximate Bayesian computation by introducing a generation-free sampler that updates its proposal as simulation results arrive and immediately dispatches new candidates. Using streaming adaptive multiple-importance sampling reweighting, it improves throughput on heterogeneous simulator workloads on HPC systems. This matters for scientific inference where simulations have highly variable runtimes.

entry.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Saiteja Utpala, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Yuki Mitsufuji, Praneeth Vepakomma

entry.summary: The authors investigate looping (recursively reusing early Transformer layers within each denoising step) in uniform diffusion language models, extending a technique previously shown effective for masked diffusion LMs. They analyze how looping interacts with UDLM training dynamics and efficiency under iso-FLOP budgets.

entry.title: A Parallel Multi-Dialect Arabic Dependency Treebank

author.name: Noor Abo Mokh, Mohamed Adel, Jamila El-Gizuli, Go Inoue, Ahmed Elshabrawy, Nizar Habash

entry.summary: The paper introduces MADARTB, the first large-scale parallel dependency treebank spanning five city dialects of Arabic (Beirut, Cairo, Doha, Rabat, Tunis) plus MSA, with 5,000 sentences under the CATiB scheme. The authors analyze cross-dialect syntactic similarity and establish cross-dialect parsing baselines, finding substantial local structural variation despite similar global profiles.

entry.title: LLMs as survey respondents: Comparison to simple semantic baselines

author.name: Esko Lehtonen, Tommi Buder-Gr\"ondahl

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLMs predicting held-out survey responses actually infer meaningful relationships between questions and answers or rely on surface-level semantic similarity between questionnaire items. Across two vehicle-attitude surveys, three LLMs are compared against simple semantic baselines that predict responses from question similarity alone. The results inform whether LLMs are viable for survey data augmentation.

entry.title: Towards English - Mizo Legal Machine Translation: Corpus Creation, Analysis, and Benchmarks

author.name: Telem Joyson Singh, Sanabam Boyshana, Sanasam Ranbir Singh, Priyankoo Sarmah

entry.summary: Introduces the first English-Mizo parallel corpus of Indian court judgments, with 13,168 professionally translated and manually reviewed sentence pairs, plus linguistic analysis showing selective English borrowing of legal terminology. Provides benchmarks to enable machine translation for a low-resource language and improve access to legal proceedings.

entry.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks

author.name: Ivan Listopadov, Maksim Nakhodnov, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: Proposes Policy-Mask, a budget-conditioned policy that jointly selects timestep, transformer block, and channel subset when extracting features from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks. The policy is trained on the downstream objective under a prescribed channel budget, replacing hand-tuned extraction rules.

entry.title: WaFIR: Wavelet-Fourier Mixture-of-Experts with Subband-Adaptive Routing for Blind All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Trong Nhan Nguyen, Vu Hoang Minh Doan, Thanh Dat Le, Truong Tien Vo, Thi Thu Ha Vu, Tan Hung Vo, Jaeyeop Choi, Junghwan Oh, Truong-Son Hy

entry.summary: WaFIR is a decoder module for blind all-in-one image restoration that decomposes features into Haar subbands, summarizes each with compact Fourier descriptors, and routes them to prompt-conditioned spectral modulation experts. Subband-level routing improves average PSNR by 0.48 dB over PromptIR across denoising, deraining, and dehazing under a unified protocol.

entry.title: Two for One: Privileged Learning for Resource-Constrained Screening

author.name: Lisa Y. W. Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a privileged learning framework for color fundus photography in which a teacher trained with bilateral (both-eye) images distills representations into a student requiring only a single eye image at test time. This enables screening where bilateral acquisition is infeasible while still exploiting complementary bilateral information during training.

entry.title: Clinical radar heart sounds with echocardiographic phenotypes of ventricular dysfunction and valvular disease

author.name: Jinye Li, Qingchao Chen

entry.summary: This is a dataset paper releasing 537 contactless radar heart-sound recordings paired with echocardiographic reports from 162 patients, covering ventricular dysfunction, wall-motion abnormality, and valvular regurgitation phenotypes. It includes raw signals, processed heart sounds, and quality segmentation to enable signal-to-phenotype modeling. Paired radar-echoocardiography data are rare, so this resource fills a real gap for non-contact cardiac monitoring research.

entry.title: Joint Semantic-Channel Coding and Modulation for Generative Image Transmission

author.name: Hao Cao, Jingkai Ying, Yinhuan Huang, Zhijin Qin, Yuan Shen

entry.summary: SemQAM jointly designs semantic and channel coding with modulation for generative image transmission, mapping vector-quantized latent indices to QAM symbols and updating codewords to match detected symbols so channel impairments are absorbed before autoregressive decoding compounds them. This departs from the usual separate optimization of source coding, channel coding, and modulation. It targets robust image delivery over noisy channels with generative decoders.

entry.title: Key Findings for Small UAS for Post-Disaster Damage Assessment from the CURSE'26 Exercise

author.name: Thomas Manzini, Stephen Johnson, Priyankari Perali, David Merrick, Robin Murphy

entry.summary: Reports field evaluation of the CLARKE building and road damage assessment classifier during the CURSE'26 training exercise with 23 small UAS teams from government agencies and NGOs. Building damage assessment achieved a Micro F1 of 0.834 with no major failures and ran in about 3.5 minutes per mission on unseen orthomosaics.

entry.title: Stochastic Nonlinearities Improve Uncertainty Estimation

author.name: Mohammad Sarhangzadeh, Amirreza M. Shebly, Doruk Oner

entry.summary: Reframes stochastic activation switching, where units randomly select among multiple nonlinearities per forward pass, as a lightweight mechanism for uncertainty estimation that generates predictive diversity without input perturbation, feature suppression, or heavy extra computation common in existing uncertainty methods.

entry.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration

author.name: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen, Guoqiang Ye, Hao Wang, Ping Tan, Steven L. Waslander, Fuchun Sun, Jin Wu

entry.summary: VeriCalib reframes target-based LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem that reports a calibration state, replacing residual RMSE which cannot indicate whether to accept, re-extract, or recollect. The key mechanism is two-level extrinsic compensation where the extrinsic absorbs the rigid part of observation error at the residual level and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level.

entry.title: A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots

author.name: Fangyu Jiang, Chaoran Xiong, Kehui Ma, Zhen Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Ling Pei

entry.summary: A2I-Calib++ is an active calibration framework for body-mounted multi-IMU systems on legged robots, estimating temporal offsets, extrinsics, and intrinsics despite foot slips, impacts, and vibration. It uses kinematics-driven motion to generate sufficient excitation where routine locomotion does not.

entry.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments

author.name: Yicheng Xu, Zhikai Xu, Ziyuan Chen, Yuhang Dong, Tao Zhang, Zhucun Xue, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang

entry.summary: TARSphere is a full-stack framework for evaluating long-horizon embodied agents under physical and social constraints, combining a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue, an event-driven FSM for task-state tracking, and an embodied brain harness that lets a frozen MLLM act through modular interfaces.

entry.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer

author.name: Guillem Casadesus Vila, Sri Aditya Deevi, Grace X. Gao

entry.summary: A systematic simulation study on a Unitree G1 of how gravity, terrain geometry, and soil contact models (including 3D resistive force theory) affect learned humanoid locomotion, covering Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning, gravity randomization, and transfer of the released generalist SONIC controller. It quantifies the cost of lunar adaptation for Earth-trained policies.

entry.title: The Role of Middle Powers in a Compute Verification Regime

author.name: Maciej Kosela

entry.summary: A governance analysis, from a Polish/EU perspective and building on a compute verification course, arguing that middle powers without frontier labs or fabs can serve as the enforcement backbone of international compute verification regimes. It proposes three mechanisms: neutral licensing and key custody, independent audit of the verifier, and arbitration.

entry.title: Neural nets are exceptionally vulnerable to goal self-hack

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Stuart Armstrong argues that neural-net-based agents with richly specified goals remain vulnerable to goal self-hack: there will be zones of situation-space where the LLM component's understanding of the goal diverges from the intended goal, and Goodhart zones where the proxy is far easier to satisfy. A rational agent will steer toward such zones, so even a sophisticated embedded goal definition does not prevent misalignment.

entry.title: Why I’m becoming a professor in AI safety in Beijing

author.name: Buddenbroke

entry.summary: A researcher announces their move to Tsinghua University's College of AI as an assistant professor in frontier AI safety and co-direction of the new Beijing AI Safety Hub, arguing that in-person presence in Beijing can build mutual understanding between Western and Chinese AI ecosystems. The post explains impact reasoning and recruits PhD students and postdocs.

entry.title: MERP: A Latent-Bottleneck Framework for Robust Multi-Modal Multi-Label Emotion Recognition

author.name: Chuangxin Zhao, Meimei Zhang, Canran Xiao, Jiachen Luo, Jiajun He, Kaijie Chen, Huy Phan, Tomoki Toda, Bi\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: MERP addresses the sharp degradation of multimodal emotion recognition models when some input streams are missing at deployment, mapping the joint sequence into a fixed-size latent bank that preserves emotion-specific evidence from any modality subset. It extracts label-specific evidence before and after latent reasoning, aligns levels via reconstruction, and adds class prototypes and noise robustness. This targets a real train-test gap for affect-aware systems.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Construction of the Gabriel Graph: Parallelization Strategies and Applications to Large-Margin Classification and Graph-Based Clustering

author.name: Diego Sanches Nere dos Santos, Luiz Carlos Bambirra Torres

entry.summary: This paper presents CUDA-based GPU parallelization strategies that make Gabriel graph construction practical beyond a few thousand samples, including an implicit closed-form thread-to-pair mapping that removes the explicit O(N^2) adjacency structure. The authors demonstrate applications to large-margin classification and density-aware clustering. It addresses a real computational bottleneck in geometric machine learning.

entry.title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning

author.name: Derong Yu, Guoyan Zheng

entry.summary: ReSeg is a two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation built on domain-randomized synthetic image synthesis and generalizable semantic representation learning. It aims to avoid dataset-specific finetuning and privacy risks from large-scale real medical data.

entry.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks

author.name: May Espinola, Qifan Zhang, Yu Xiang

entry.summary: This report builds a unified closed-loop framework for evaluating frontier general-purpose AI models on the LIBERO-10 robot manipulation benchmark, letting models control a robot via visual observations, proprioception, and structured tool calls without task-specific fine-tuning. It provides a first systematic comparison of frontier models on a standardized manipulation benchmark.

entry.title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion

author.name: Valentin Munteanu, Alexander Hinderhofer, Dmitry Lapkin, Vladimir Starostin, Frank Schreiber

entry.summary: The authors introduce a modular probabilistic framework using prior-amortized flow matching to combine X-ray and neutron scattering measurements for structural inversion, training separate single-observation posterior estimators and combining them only at inference. This mitigates the fundamental non-uniqueness of phase-less scattering inverse problems.

entry.title: Compressing Onboard Language Models for Space Robots under a Behavioral-Fidelity Requirement

author.name: Jia Deng, Zizhe Wang, Xin Lu, Yi Huang, Zehao Jia

entry.summary: This paper addresses low-bit compression of language models for onboard space-robot command interpretation, treating compression as a ground-segment step with flight-specific requirements: fixed memory budgets, static configuration-controlled artifacts, and behavioral fidelity to the full-precision validated model. QSelect composes one static low-bit model by assigning each linear module to a compatible quantizer family (AWQ, GPTQ, AutoRound) scored at the final next-token distribution. It highlights deployment constraints generic post-training quantization ignores.

entry.title: No Frames, Just Frequencies: Bandwidth-Efficient Deployment-Time Adaptation for Smart Glasses

author.name: Francesco Corti, Moritz Becker, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a bandwidth-efficient adaptation framework for smart glasses in which on-device frequency descriptors, rather than camera frames, are transmitted to a host device holding a model replica. The host maps descriptors to distribution shift operators that synthesize out-of-distribution data and adapts the replica, respecting privacy and device constraints. Evaluation covers ImageNet-style shift mixtures.

entry.title: MINER: Modeling Inter- and Intra-Person Variance for Reidentification

author.name: Oron Nir, Eliyahu Strugo, Ariel Shamir

entry.summary: Presents MINER, a model-agnostic framework for clothes-changing person re-identification that suppresses garment bias through hard-example contrastive learning while adaptively balancing intra- and inter-person variance. It achieves state-of-the-art results on four CC-ReID benchmarks and strong rankings in the TVRID RGB-Depth challenge.

entry.title: RiO-DETRv2: Geometry-Aware Uncertainty Modeling Meets Real-Time Oriented Object Detection Transformer

author.name: Zhangchi Hu, Zilong He, Yifan Zhao, Xiangyu Yu, Jie Chen, Peixi Wu, Yansong Peng, Hebei Li, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: Extends RiO-DETR, claimed as the first real-time end-to-end transformer for oriented object detection, with geometry-aware uncertainty modeling. Object-aligned boundary distribution refinement and topology-consistent orientation handling resolve mismatches that arise when adapting distributional regression from horizontal to rotated detection.

entry.title: Learning Dynamic Games for Cooperative Iterative Tasks

author.name: Mark Pustilnik, Francesco Borrelli

entry.summary: The paper presents a general learning framework for cooperative multi-agent dynamic games with shared constraints, using previously executed feasible trajectories to build a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions. Agents jointly select sampled terminal states and Generalized Nash equilibria under a cooperative acceptance rule supporting non-degradation requirements and Nash bargaining.

entry.title: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions

author.name: Xuhan Miao, Zijin Han, Yutong Shen, Haidong Huang, Shanliushui Gao, Lei Zhang, Xiaocong Li, Chenguang Yang

entry.summary: This teleoperation method for manipulators with coupled transmissions jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control. It performs coordinated saturation in motor space according to available gravity margin, preserving pitch-roll coordination and operator intent under actuation limits.

entry.title: UNIVERS: Learning UNIversal Voxel-wise Embedding via Randomized Synthesis for generalizable one-shot landmark localization

author.name: Derong Yu, Qingsong Zhao, Yanbing Yue, Yikai Li, Zhi Zhang, Guoyan Zheng

entry.summary: UNIVERS learns universal voxel-wise embeddings end-to-end via randomized pseudo-pair synthesis, replacing contrastive learning on augmented views that limits cross-modality generalization in one-shot anatomical landmark localization. It avoids the multi-stage iterative training required by prior paired multi-modality approaches.

entry.title: FaultGene: LLM-Assisted Fault-Augmented Test Generation for Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation of Autonomous Driving Systems

author.name: Chaoran Yuan, Fadi Kurdahi

entry.summary: FaultGene uses LLMs to automate generation of fault-augmented test scenarios for hardware-in-the-loop validation of autonomous driving systems, a process that is otherwise largely manual. It aims to improve test coverage, scalability, and efficiency in bridging the gap between cheap-but-unrealistic simulation and costly-but-realistic road testing.

entry.title: Understanding Target Probability Reuse in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Giyoon Jang, Chailin Nam, Jiwoo Kum, Sihyeon Lee, Kyojun Choo, Jihun Song, Eunseo Song, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: The paper analyzes whether target-model next-token distributions produced during speculative decoding verification can be reused to select the next draft tree, showing exact reuse requires distributions at the next round's complete context and characterizing when retention sacrifices accepted tokens. They also show reranking first-token branches with a separately computed distribution improves expected acceptance, especially for small tree budgets.

entry.title: DisasterRoute: Evidence-Guided Dual-System Routing for Visual Disaster Question Answering

author.name: Tan Zhang, Xing Deng, Lu Zhang, Xiaofeng Zhu, Ping Hu

entry.summary: DisasterRoute builds Disaster-S1, a disaster-domain vision-language model trained for option discrimination that outputs answer probability distributions in a single pass, then routes between fast direct decisions and slower step-by-step generative reasoning based on question difficulty. This supports timely VQA from UAV imagery under limited edge compute during disaster response.

entry.title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
