author.name: Yaohua Zhou, Mingdao Lin, Jiayu Song, Xixin Zhao, Haidong Huang, Jiahu Qin, Xiaocong Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies kinematic conditions under which Jacobian-based performance indices such as manipulability and stiffness are independent of the first and last joint angles, enabling systematic configuration-space dimensionality reduction. Applications include workspace performance mapping and task layout optimization with reduced computation and storage.

entry.title: Sketch2Sim: an end-to-end modular framework for hand-drawn circuit analysis

author.name: Mohammad Kawsar, Al Amin Islam Ridoy, Md Rakib Hossain, Farzana Akter, AKM Bahalul Haque, Rejwan Bin Sulaiman, Mohammed Amin Almaiah

entry.summary: Sketch2Sim converts photographs of handwritten electric circuit diagrams into SPICE-compatible netlists and computes nodal voltages and currents via a multistage pipeline. The authors also curate a dataset of 1,000 annotated hand-drawn RLC circuits and target educational and engineering design-review use cases.

entry.title: GuideEvolve: Self-Evolving Agent Framework with Expert Guidance and 3Ts Mechanisms

author.name: Meihong Jia, Yasemin Timar, Jonathan Taws

entry.summary: GuideEvolve is a self-evolving agent framework combining expert-evaluation-driven evolution with three self-regulatory mechanisms (fast/slow thinking, temporal rollback, and chosen termination). It reports accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art models on MGSM and MMLU benchmarks.

entry.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites

author.name: Can Erer, H. Birkan Yilmaz, Nebahat Aral

entry.summary: The authors train a Set Transformer that maps unordered molecular constituents, mass fractions, and bulk physical descriptors directly to X-ray transmission ratios in polymer composites, replacing Monte Carlo transport simulations that take hours with 1-3 millisecond inference. The permutation-invariant set architecture matches the unordered nature of the composition input. This offers a practical surrogate model for radiation shielding design workflows.

entry.title: Dual-Channel Contrastive Encoding of Sperm Whale Coda

author.name: Jo\~ao Victor Quintanilha, Emma Virnelli, Shuo Zhang

entry.summary: The Dual-Channel Contrastive Encoder separately encodes rhythmic inter-click interval patterns and spectral click composition before fusion, evaluated on three sperm whale coda-understanding tasks (social unit, coda type, individual identification) on 1,383 codas under a common linear-probe protocol. Ablations analyze each channel's contribution and training objectives.

entry.title: Broadband Mid-Wave Infrared Imaging Enabled by All-Silicon Hyperboloid Metalens

author.name: Rose Johnson, Debabrata Mandal, Zihao Zou, Jessie Wei, Anna Wirth-Singh, Vladimir Yarmolik, Johannes Froech, Arka Majumdar, Praneeth Chakravarthula

entry.summary: This optics paper demonstrates broadband imaging across the full 3-5 micron mid-wave infrared band using a single-layer silicon metasurface plus computational reconstruction, overcoming the chromatic dispersion that previously limited metalens imaging to narrow bands. A notable result is that the reconstruction model adapts with only four image captures, avoiding large training data requirements.

entry.title: Asymmetry Tunneling Beyond Adaptive Equivariance Relaxation

author.name: Eunho Jeong, Joon Jang, Hyeonjin Kim

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether equivariance relaxation must be adaptively controlled by adding a residual path alongside a strictly equivariant network with a deliberately restricted interface. Across five benchmarks the authors observe both residual collapse and survival, with the survival phenomenon termed asymmetry tunneling, showing symmetry-breaking structure can flow through minimal interfaces.

entry.title: Leveraging Time-Series Foundation Models for Financial Crime Detection

author.name: Danae Natalie Savvidi, H. \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Bilgi, Kubilay Atasu, Arie van Deursen

entry.summary: TCEE summarizes each account's transaction history with a frozen time-series foundation model and enriches transaction edge representations with that temporal context, either scored directly or fed into a GNN for edge classification in financial crime detection. The approach addresses the gap where graph methods underuse temporal behavior in transaction histories.

entry.title: Asymmetric Likelihood-Free Hypothesis Testing

author.name: Gunjan Kumar, Yash Pote, Jonathan Scarlett

entry.summary: The paper studies likelihood-free hypothesis testing with unequal reference sample budgets, characterizing feasible sample triples up to logarithmic factors. It shows asymmetric budgets yield polynomial savings, e.g., constant separation allows testing with n and n^(3/4) reference samples using only O-tilde(n^(1/4)) samples from the unknown distribution, beating symmetric baselines.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Tuning of Low-Fidelity Optimization Models via High-Fidelity Feedback

author.name: Gonzalo E. Constante-Flores, Andr\'e H. Quisaguano-Paredes, Asha Ramanujam, Rishabh Gupta, Can Li

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised framework that corrects low-fidelity optimization models using high-fidelity feedback without requiring expensive HF solution datasets: the LF problem is embedded as a differentiable optimization layer and trained end-to-end while an HF correction problem evaluates its solutions and provides gradients. This reduces reliance on costly supervised HF training data in large-scale operations.

entry.title: The Optimal Sampler for Diverse TSP Solutions: Characterization, Limits, and Learning

author.name: Ssu-Yuan Lo, Ching-Kai Wang, Kuan-Lun Chen, Hao-Tsung Yang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the Diverse Traveling Salesman Problem, seeking k distinct tours whose lengths are within a prescribed factor of optimal while minimizing pairwise Jaccard similarity, motivated by logistics, robotics, and patrolling applications needing quality plus fault tolerance. It decomposes the problem into sampling and max-min dispersion selection stages and provides theoretical characterization and limits for the sampling stage along with learning-based methods. This offers both theory and practical algorithms for generating diverse high-quality combinatorial solutions.

entry.title: What Prediction-Market Contracts Reveal at Launch: Trading Volume and Dispute Risk

author.name: Ahmed Mahrous, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: Using a near-census of over 800,000 resolved Polymarket markets from January 2023 to May 2026, the authors predict lifetime trading volume and settlement dispute risk using only information available at market listing. Contract metadata and topic predict log volume well (out-of-sample R-squared of 0.747), with interpretable features outperforming neural text models. Notably, this predictive performance does not survive a period shift, which the paper appears to analyze as a robustness caveat.

entry.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift

author.name: Juan S. Santillana

entry.summary: VX-One is a small multi-head network producing typed decision primitives (calibrated binary gate, closed-set choice with an explicit unknown option, ordinal score) for cybersecurity perimeter triage, achieving sub-2ms CPU inference. The paper claims to be the first academic treatment of a class of commercial typed decision model APIs that emerged in late 2026.

entry.title: TAGR: Task-Adaptive Geo-Semantic Retrieval across Heterogeneous Urban Delivery Tasks

author.name: Zhi Liu, Yurun Cai, Xiao Han, Zhi Zhen, Yuran Li, Guojiang Shen, Xiangjie Kong

entry.summary: Proposes a task-adaptive retrieval framework for urban delivery systems that tailors retrieved evidence to three structurally different tasks (demand forecasting, ETA prediction, next-stop prediction), avoiding negative transfer from a single fusion mechanism. The geo-semantic retrieval approach aims to improve prediction accuracy and resource allocation efficiency.

entry.title: Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation for Few-shot Image Classification

author.name: Zhiqi Miao, Estefan\'ia Talavera, Weichuan Zhang, Jiapan Guo

entry.summary: Introduces DAFIC, a few-shot image classification framework that injects monocular depth into representation learning, episodic adaptation, and dense support-query matching. RGB-D self-supervised pre-training and depth-guided patch refinement suppress background clutter that confuses RGB-only matching in data-scarce settings.

entry.title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis

author.name: Zhichun Fan, Zhiqiang Chen, Lanling Liu, Lingjun Liu, Zhonghua Xie

entry.summary: DGCM-SSFA synthesizes high-fidelity 7T MRI from routine 3T scans using a compact U-Net Transformer with dual-granularity cross-modulation and sparse strip frequency attention, achieving competitive quality with only 11M parameters versus over 45M for state-of-the-art methods. The efficiency makes ultra-high-field-like imaging more practical in resource-constrained clinics.

entry.title: FM-Occ: Feature-Diverse Upsampling and Memory-Aware Decoding for 3D Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Yujia Zhai (Great Bay University), Guoming Huang (Great Bay University), Zhuanghuai Wang (Great Bay University), Bangquan Xie (Great Bay University)

entry.summary: FM-Occ targets 3D semantic occupancy prediction for autonomous driving, identifying that sparse transposed-convolution upsampling homogenizes voxel features and that deeper decoder layers discard earlier correct predictions. It introduces 3D Sparse Subvoxel Shuffle for feature-diverse upsampling and memory-aware decoding that retains correct semantics. These are targeted architectural fixes for known decoder pathologies.

entry.title: MS2CAST: A Video Anomaly Detection Framework via Multi-Scale Spatial Cross-Attention and Efficient Spatiotemporal Networks

author.name: Ali Safaei, Mohammad Kazemi

entry.summary: Proposes MS2CAST, a semi-supervised predictive video anomaly detection framework that replaces optical flow with an efficient spatiotemporal network and fuses hierarchical features from an MViTv2-S vision transformer and a ConvNeXt-T CNN via multi-scale cross-attention. This addresses the computational cost and limited receptive fields of prior CNN-plus-flow approaches for surveillance.

entry.title: Multiclass Boundary Refinement with Neural Cellular Automata for Remote Sensing Land Cover Segmentation

author.name: Pascoassis Souza Santos Meira, Gilson Antonio Giraldi, Rafael Duarte Coelho dos Santos

entry.summary: This paper generalizes binary residual Neural Cellular Automata to the multiclass setting (BRNCA) to refine class boundaries of frozen pre-trained segmenters on remote sensing land cover data. It uses an Aitchison log-space update on the probability simplex plus free hidden channels, improving mean Boundary IoU by 2.36 points over the base segmenter.

entry.title: Navigation Explainability for Object Avoidance with LLMs for Assistive Robots

author.name: Courtney Young, Yi Lian, Taery Kim, Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: This work presents a Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework in which an LLM explains guide-robot obstacle avoidance using perceptual context and planned future trajectories, deployed on a Unitree Go2 for indoor navigation aimed at blind and visually impaired users. User evaluation shows a strong positive relationship between explanation quality, trust, and satisfaction.

entry.title: OMAR: Open-World Multi-Attribute Reasoning for Scene-Conditioned Shelf Organization

author.name: Benedikt Kreis, Rohit Menon, Benno Wingender, Muhammad Ehsan Ullah, Nils Dengler, Maren Bennewitz

entry.summary: Proposes an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that lets robots infer latent organization schemes from a scene and place novel objects consistently, without explicit instructions, predefined object vocabularies, or known object-receptacle associations. It targets household organization tasks under foundation-model-based scene understanding.

entry.title: Data as particles and mean field theory abound

author.name: Max Hennick

entry.summary: The author reframes known learning-theory results using a data-as-particles perspective and sketches a dynamical mean-field-theory viewpoint for neural network training, drawing on their background in equivariant networks and quantum many-body physics. Framed explicitly as a conceptual reframing, with a more formal paper promised as part of a broader research agenda.

entry.title: Intergroup Bias Predicts Expressions of Social Judgment and Empathy in the r/AmITheAsshole Reddit Community

author.name: Yu Hou, Hal Daum\'e III, Rachel Rudinger

entry.summary: Analyzing 126,716 comments across 36,163 posts from r/AmITheAsshole, the authors measure whether commenters who share a poster's gender or age express different social judgment and empathy, testing the intergroup empathy gap in naturally occurring online interactions. The large-scale observational design grounds a well-studied social psychology phenomenon in real text data.

entry.title: Single-Image Food Mass Estimators Do Not Transfer Their Gram Scale Across Datasets

author.name: Yongsheng Lian

entry.summary: Fine-tunes DINOv2-base to predict food mass from single photographs on Nutrition5k and benchmarks it against zero-shot Qwen3-VL-32B across three external datasets. The fine-tuned model wins in-domain (MAE 24.8 g versus more than twice Qwen's error) but fails to transfer its gram scale out of domain, ranking unseen portions no better than counting food pixels.

entry.title: Rethinking Underwater Image Enhancement: Learning through Text-Guided Degradation Curriculum

author.name: Hongri Tian, Wenxue Li, Tian Ye, Sixiang Chen, Lujia Wang, Xianying Wang, Xinhu Zheng, Gang Hua, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified degradation-aware training framework for underwater image enhancement, using a text-conditioned diffusion model to synthesize realistic and controllable degradations in a curriculum, addressing the scarcity and limited coverage of paired clean-degraded data. This improves generalization to real-world underwater conditions. It is a data-centric remedy to a long-standing domain problem.

entry.title: Towards Realistic Models of Change: A Causal Perspective on Decision-Making and Dynamical Systems

author.name: Isacco Beretta

entry.summary: A thesis examining how causal models, which capture mechanisms of change rather than surface correlations, can improve generalization under distribution shift, support hypothetical reasoning, and inform decision-making in dynamical systems. It connects statistical learning with causality across two parts addressing decision-making and dynamical systems. The work speaks to a foundational limitation of purely data-driven learning.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Message Passing on Petri Nets through Directed Walks and Incidence Diffusion

author.name: Geri Skenderi

entry.summary: The author exposes directed cycles and incidence-matrix invariants of Petri nets to message-passing GNNs via positional encodings from directed walk return probabilities and same-type messages gated by incidence diffusion kernels. This improves learning of vector representations of process models in process mining.

entry.title: Every Part Has Its Role: Part-of-Speech Effects in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Laya Iyer, Chen Shani

entry.summary: This paper reproduces and extends prior work on concept augmentation in LLM training, asking whether its benefits depend on where in a sentence the concept appears. It extends analysis beyond nouns to verbs and adjectives, examining how next-token prediction interacts with part-of-speech effects in post-training.

entry.title: Delay-Guided Attention for Quality Prediction in Multistage Manufacturing

author.name: Jiarui Zhang, Zhaoyang Guan, Zhixuan Xia, Naichen Shi

entry.summary: The authors propose DAMF, an attention-based model for quality prediction in multistage manufacturing that explicitly estimates inter-stage lag distributions and uses them to guide cross-stage information transfer. A lag predictor compares current downstream representations with candidate lagged upstream representations, addressing the problem that timestamp-aligned features can reflect different process states when lags vary over time.

entry.title: Extending FAIR Principles with Observability for Trustworthy Federated Learning

author.name: Hangli Ge, Noboru Koshizuka

entry.summary: The authors argue that federated learning needs an evidence plane alongside model updates: participants continuously produce minimal, signed trust evidence about infrastructure and data pipelines while keeping raw data local. A local TinyLLM is proposed to interpret observability signals and provide natural-language explanations to operators.

entry.title: Nominate-then-Adjudicate: LLM-Assisted One-Pass and Per-Instance MIP Solver Tuning

author.name: Yifan Zhao, Qianyang Zhao, Xinyu Guan, Kai Wei, Yuming Deng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a nominate-then-adjudicate pipeline for per-instance parameter tuning of MIP solvers, using a fixed sampled portfolio reused across instances to avoid costly inference-time configuration search, with LLM assistance to distinguish structurally different instances that map to identical feature vectors. The shortlist retains substantial oracle headroom on evaluated instance families.

entry.title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management

author.name: Recep Yusuf Bekci, Stefanus Jasin, Joline Uichanco

entry.summary: Studies assortment and pricing decisions under a multinomial logit demand model when per-store data is sparse, proposing a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific estimates with pooled cross-store information under a transfer-learning framework. This balances estimation precision against ignoring local demand heterogeneity in retail revenue management.

entry.title: ROCOCO: Robust Outline Completion of Occluded Curvilinear Objects

author.name: Ken Zheng, Jaimyn Drake

entry.summary: ROCOCO is a flow matching-based generative model for completing curvilinear features (e.g., roads, vessels, lines) under occlusion, paired with a UNet-based mask predictor that identifies occluded regions without privileged occlusion information. Validated on procedurally generated cases and large public curvilinear-object datasets, it outperforms off-the-shelf inpainting baselines. The work fills a practical niche in robust perception of occluded structured objects.

entry.title: Carving Radiology Reports at Their Evidential Joints: Anatomical Region Sets as Generation Units

author.name: Jinwei Yang, Junhao Chen, Jianwei Zhao, Zhonghan Xu, Hong Cheng, Ling Wang

entry.summary: RadCarve structures radiology report generation by defining generation units directly from anatomical region sets in existing statement-region annotations, unifying unit formation with visual evidence selection. Its planner uses composition-specialized query banks to jointly predict unit existence and region composition from the image.

entry.title: Computer Vision and Knowledge-Grounded Language Models for Intelligent Beekeeper Assistance

author.name: Asaduz Zaman, Mohaimenul Azam Khan Raiaan, Malika Nisal Ratnayake

entry.summary: An edge-deployable system combining object detection of comb-cell classes with knowledge-grounded language models to turn hive frame photographs into interpretable, action-oriented beekeeping inspection reports. It addresses labor-intensive manual colony assessment with a practical pipeline supporting adaptive hive management.

entry.title: MedBOE: Optimization-Based Estimation of Complete Patient Body Models from Whole-Body Medical Imaging

author.name: Hoijoon Jung, Yuhao Wei, Mingxiao Tu, Younhyun Jung, Michael Fulham, Jinman Kim

entry.summary: MedBOE reconstructs complete external patient body models from whole-body medical imaging, using optimization to fill in regions missing due to scanner bore geometry or patient positioning. Complete body models support body-habitus metrics like volume and surface area relevant to radiotracer dosing, cardiometabolic risk, and imaging simulation.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Fish Segmentation through Point-Supervised Tracking and Motion-Informed Language

author.name: Vedanth Kallakuri, Katherine A. Skinner

entry.summary: Proposes a weakly supervised fish segmentation pipeline needing only point labels (one click per fish), combining point-supervised tracking with motion-informed language cues to produce accurate masks. This avoids costly per-pixel annotation that can take up to two minutes per fish, supporting aquaculture and conservation monitoring.

entry.title: SICAF: Time-Varying Focus Bottleneck for Self-Supervised Event-Based Optical Flow with Spiking Neural Network

author.name: Shuangming Yang, Qing He, Shangqi Guo, Badong Chen

entry.summary: Presents SICAF, a spiking neural network approach for self-supervised event-based optical flow featuring a compact-compress, time-varying-focus training strategy. The method addresses temporal irregularity across event streams and redundancy in latent representations caused by missing explicit labels.

entry.title: Diff-IrisPAD: Modeling Bona Fide Iris Distributions for Unsupervised Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Geetanjali Sharma, Harsh Yadav, Tanmay Deshpande, Shubham Ashwani, Aditya Nigam, Raghavendra Ramachandra

entry.summary: Diff-IrisPAD performs unsupervised iris presentation attack detection using Brownian Bridge Diffusion to model bona fide iris distributions without attack samples, reconstructing clean textures from degraded inputs and scoring attacks via reconstruction inconsistency with ViT and pixel-level measures. Evaluation spans 125K+ images across NIR and VIS sensors and eight attack types, achieving 30.52 overall ACER. The unsupervised design targets generalization to unseen attacks and new sensors.

entry.title: Forward-Only Learning for Shared-Kernel Wavelet Neural Networks without Backpropagation

author.name: Yongfei Guo, Xuan Sun, Ang Li, Zhao Zhang, Yuanhao Gong

entry.summary: Proposes a CMA-ES-based global forward-only learning framework for shared-kernel wavelet neural networks, with structure-aware parameter decomposition and channel-specific credit assignment across three subspaces. On BSDS500 it modestly outperforms Adam/backprop on MSE and PSNR without any backward pass.

entry.title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation

author.name: Zhuoyu Wu, Wenhui Ou, Qiawei Zheng, Xuhong Qiu, Wenqi Fang, Rapha\"{e}l C. -W. Phan

entry.summary: TernScope is a model-hardware co-design for edge medical segmentation using ternary weights and 8-bit activations across all 25 convolutions, enabling multiplier-free computation and packed storage at only 0.2483M parameters. Split-channel large-kernel blocks and progressive quantization-aware training preserve accuracy while meeting edge constraints.

entry.title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments

author.name: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren

entry.summary: S-rolling is a steerable rolling gait for twistable snake robots combining low swept-height locomotion with planar maneuverability, using an S-shaped backbone curve with independently controlled head and tail rolling velocities. It targets low-clearance environments where steering gaits typically require extra vertical clearance.

entry.title: On Idealized Agency

author.name: Ben Auer

entry.summary: A philosophical critique of the agent-foundations research strategy of starting with idealized theories of agency (AIXI, infra-Bayesianism, UDT) with provable safety properties and gradually de-idealizing them into realistic, embedded agents. The author argues this de-idealization will likely destroy the safety guarantees, provides weak feedback loops, and may tell us little about real agents.

entry.title: Zero-Cost Detection of Fabricated Citations: A Staged Heuristic Approach for Computing Dissertation Assessment

author.name: Hazrat Ali, Mohamed Elawady

entry.summary: The paper presents the Fabrication Severity Stack, a three-tier classification of citation fabrications, plus a staged heuristic verification workflow executable through mainstream LLM interfaces at no cost. A pilot on 100 citations with 20% seeded fabrications demonstrates detection performance for educators assessing dissertations.

entry.title: Brittle by Design? Multi-Scenario Reinforcement Learning for Robust Mission Coordination in Systems of Systems

author.name: \.Ibrahim O\u{g}uz \c{C}etinkaya, Sajad Khodadadian, Taylan Topcu

entry.summary: The authors propose a mission-coordination methodology that integrates high-fidelity digital mission models with reinforcement learning for adaptive task allocation in Systems of Systems. Mission tactics management is formulated as a Markov Decision Process and an RL coordinator is trained within a digital engineering simulation infrastructure. The goal is to replace brittle static architectures with flexible coordination under uncertain, dynamic mission environments.

entry.title: Agent AI Zarz\k{a}dzaj\k{a}cy Sieci\k{a} Open RAN Zorientowana na U\.zytkownika

author.name: Marcin Hoffmann

entry.summary: This Polish-language arXiv paper (cross-listed) addresses the challenge of forming serving clusters in user-centric Open RAN network architectures. The author proposes an AI agent built on a large language model to manage the network, and simulations show the approach more than doubles the median user throughput compared to a standard network-centric architecture. It matters because it demonstrates a concrete, quantified application of LLM-based agents to telecom network management, an emerging area beyond typical software tasks.

entry.title: HumanCentric-Scenes-AI: A Human-Curated Multimodal Dataset of AI-Generated Human-Centric Scenes Across Surveillance, Occupational Portraits, AI-Edited Images, and Short-Form Video

author.name: Nima Kamali, Sana Nasiri, Negar Kamali

entry.summary: The authors release a human-curated dataset of 296 photorealistic AI-generated stimuli depicting people across surveillance-style CCTV images, balanced-gender occupational portraits, AI-edited real photographs, and short videos, with prompts and provenance metadata. The dataset supports research on detecting and studying AI-generated human-centric media.

entry.title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature

author.name: Xuanlyu Zhu, Feng Tian, Yang Zhong, Pengqi Zheng, Xiwen Bi, Ling Luo, Yuanyuan Sun, Jian Wang, Lingfei Lin

entry.summary: This is a shared-task overview for patient-specific phenotype concept recognition in full-text biomedical literature, with two subtasks covering concept recognition and patient-specific association, evaluated on 200 annotated full-text articles. The task targets challenges in rare disease diagnosis and precision medicine involving multiple patients per article.

entry.title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models

author.name: Aravindan Kamatchi Sundaram, B. Pabitramohan Prusty, Rohit Batra

entry.summary: A review tracing a decade of methods for extracting materials data and knowledge from scientific literature, from rule-based pipelines through transformer encoders to LLM-based agentic systems handling text, tables, and figures. It covers construction of queryable materials databases and knowledge graphs that support downstream materials discovery.

entry.title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting

author.name: Muhammad Sabbir Alam, Harindra Sandun Mavikumbure, Victor Cobilean, Milos Manic, Jayasimha Atulasimha

entry.summary: The paper investigates extreme low-state weight quantization (3-, 5-, 7-, 16-state) of Transformers for electricity-load forecasting across two forecasting horizons and datasets. It shows direct post-training quantization degrades error substantially while a quantization-aware alternative preserves accuracy even at very few weight states.

entry.title: ART-MPG: Autoregressive R/T Manifold Path Guiding

author.name: Zehao Zhao, Yanyang Yang, Xiaole Zhang, Xiyu Deng

entry.summary: The authors introduce ART-MPG, a compact neural model for rendering that samples chain length, an autoregressive reflection/transmission string, and a direction from a topology-conditioned von Mises-Fisher mixture to guide light-transport paths through specular chains. Extending Manifold Path Guiding, retry sampling is conditioned on both chain length and the sampled R/T string, preserving the ideal expectation while reducing retry counts and estimator variance.

entry.title: Interpretable Cutting Plane Selection for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Using Genetic Programming

author.name: Gwen maudet, Mathis Da Cunha, Gr\'egoire Danoy

entry.summary: GPSCS is a learning-based framework using genetic programming to derive interpretable, adaptive cutting-plane selection strategies for MILP solvers, addressing the static nature of handcrafted heuristics and the poor interpretability of neural approaches. The evolved rule-based strategies offer transparency and better convergence behavior guarantees.

entry.title: The Predictive--Optimization Gap in GuanDan Self-Play

author.name: Qicheng Zou, Biao Yuan, Siyu Song, Wentao Liu, Xiaokun Wang

entry.summary: Using GuanDan, an imperfect-information card game, this paper distinguishes predictive validity from optimization utility by testing whether changes in a frozen match-win predictor provide useful round-level supervision in self-play RL. Results show the intervention can succeed in specific conditions but is not uniformly beneficial, exposing the gap between prediction and optimization targets.

entry.title: Geometric knowledge spaces, Attention pairing and Architectures

author.name: Shang Xu

entry.summary: The author formalizes knowledge worlds and attention pairings in a geometric framework that recovers standard attention, causal attention, linear attention, tensor attention, and RNNs as special cases. The paper then introduces new geometric spaces intended to inspire novel neural architectures.

entry.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering

author.name: Amirardalan Dehghanpour, Arian Noori, Ehsan Tanghatari, Naimeh Omidvar, Hamid R. Rabiee

entry.summary: Presents HDC-FL, which clusters federated clients by projecting cached client-specific classifier heads into a low-rank descriptor space, then returns each client a soft mixture of group-level encoder prototypes while leaving heads and shared-encoder trajectories intact. This avoids a second optimization trajectory and never distributes heads, addressing which clients should share representations in personalized federated learning.

entry.title: A Jump-Modified Wasserstein Gradient Flow for Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Energy Kernels

author.name: Ansh Desai, Jason Liu, Srujan Roplekar, Matthew Rosenzweig

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes a jump-modified Wasserstein gradient flow of squared MMD generated by energy kernels, proving global well-posedness under subcritical density and finite-moment assumptions. The jump mechanism transfers mass toward smaller first-variation values and, combined with a rigidity result and compactness arguments, yields convergence to the target from finite-second-moment data without additional assumptions. This advances the mathematical foundations of MMD-based sampling and particle methods.

entry.title: Region-Aware Multi-View Inspection Using Deep Learning and Domain-Informed Decision Fusion

author.name: Srivishnu Ethirajulu Krishnaraj, Rishikesh R. Chopade

entry.summary: This work presents a region-aware industrial inspection framework that combines instance segmentation for localized defects with image-level classification for global anomalies on precision components. A deterministic decision fusion layer encodes industrial standard operating procedures rather than treating model outputs alone as rejection evidence. It is deployed with a PLC-synchronized imaging system capturing 18 images per component.

entry.title: norregel: a preregistered benchmark of dated numeric values in Norwegian law

author.name: Eirik Botten Nicolaysen (EcoDeco AS)

entry.summary: norregel is a preregistered benchmark of 916 dated numeric values (amounts, percentages, age limits) extracted mechanically from Norwegian legal sources, classifying model answers as correct, outdated, wrong, or uninterpretable. Two preregistered runs test whether outdated answers cluster around post-cutoff values, with partially inconclusive results.

entry.title: DetM-Tracker: Deterministic and Memory-Efficient VIS for Autonomous Industrial Inspection

author.name: You-Rui Lin, Jen-Chieh Wu, Tzu-Ti Wei, Jen-Jee Chen, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: DetM-Tracker is a video instance segmentation framework for edge-deployed industrial inspection that achieves deterministic real-time inference under tight memory constraints. It tackles the memory wall of dense temporal memory via components exploiting scene sparsity in constrained micro fields of view with highly similar-looking objects.

entry.title: GuidedSAM-Plume: An Expert-Guided Segmentation Framework for Volcanic Plumes

author.name: Taddeo D'Adamo (LIRIS, imagine), Simon Thivet (UNIGE), Catherine Pothier (LIRIS, imagine), Riccardo Simionato (UNIGE), Allan Fries (UNIGE), Jonathan Lemus (UNIGE), Costanza Bonadonna (UNIGE), Laure Tougne Rodet (LIRIS, imagine), Bertrand Kerautret (LIRIS, imagine)

entry.summary: Presents GuidedSAM-Plume, an open-source interactive segmentation framework for volcanic plumes and clouds built on SAM2's zero-shot prompt-based capabilities, validated with segmentation metrics and volcanologically relevant descriptors on a challenging dataset. Minimal expert input significantly improves over handcrafted-annotation workflows.

entry.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains

author.name: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren

entry.summary: The paper introduces a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots that combine backbone undulation with distributed twisting, addressing a weakness of prior rolling-vector approaches where twisting is concentrated in a small buffer segment and overburdens the middle twist joints. By distributing the twisting workload across the robot, the proposed gaits improve speed and robustness for motion planning on complex terrains.

entry.title: Make it Walk: Computational Design of LEGO Walkers

author.name: Siqi Li, Fancheng Gao, Chi-Wing Fu, Peng Song

entry.summary: This paper presents the first computational design tool for LEGO Technic walkers that supports a variety of stable walking gaits rather than reusing fixed single-actuator mechanisms. It mechanically controls leg foot trajectories via custom linkages and searches over modular brick compositions.

entry.title: Spacetime Splines for Adaptive Robot Motions

author.name: Boxuan Zhang, Ante Mari\'c, Sylvain Calinon

entry.summary: Proposes a spline-based movement-primitive formulation, inspired by spacetime representations in physics, in which spatial geometry and temporal progression share a common set of continuous variables via a jointly estimated Bezier curve, allowing spatial and temporal model complexity to adapt independently. Demonstrated on recovery of paths from partial demonstrations in simulation.

entry.title: Cascading Bandits with Noisy Observations: Algorithms and Regret Bounds

author.name: Yashaswini Kaluguri, Nikhil Karamchandani

entry.summary: This theory paper studies a stochastic cascading bandit setting with position-dependent probing costs and noisy per-arm feedback, characterizing when optimal shortlists can be found by sorting per-arm scores under different noise and cost conditions. It provides a UCB-based algorithm with instance-dependent logarithmic regret for separable cases.

entry.title: What Git Does Not Record: Provenance Legibility in Two AI-Assisted Research Repositories

author.name: Koutian Wu, Zesen Huang, Hejia Geng

entry.summary: This audit examines what version-control repositories can reveal about AI tool contributions to research, analyzing two single-investigator repositories with different agent residue types: standing rule files and an agent scratchpad. It finds the two traces are legible in opposite ways, with prescriptive traces preserving conclusions but discarding episodes while narrative traces record process differently.

entry.title: From AI-Free Gates to AI-First Work: How Engineering Students in India Navigate University Education and Campus Placements Without AI Guidelines

author.name: Samhitha Goutham, Ziwei Gu

entry.summary: This HCI study interviews 23 Indian engineering students and graduates about generative AI use across coursework, examinations, and campus placements in a system with almost no AI guidelines despite AI reshaping the tech sector. Reflexive thematic analysis yields five themes on AI-first work readiness versus AI-excluding assessment gates.

entry.title: Progressive Permutation Alignment with Temperature-Controlled Spectral Sharpening

author.name: Yuta Horioka, Naoya Chiba, Yuki Uranishi

entry.summary: The paper addresses permutation symmetry in implicit neural representations with a progressive layer-wise alignment strategy that follows inter-layer dependencies, using temperature-controlled spectral sharpening to avoid premature discrete matches and expensive continuous relaxations. This reduces loss barriers under weight-space interpolation, including challenging NeRF cases.

entry.title: Balancing Foundation Models and Trait-Specific Learning for Forehead-Crease Recognition

author.name: Geetanjali Sharma, Aryan Jain, Dev Nagaich, Aditya Nigam, Raghavendra Ramachandra

entry.summary: This work studies forehead-crease patterns as a complementary biometric trait usable when the face is partially occluded, comparing zero-shot multimodal LLM reasoning (GPT-4o with FIRE prompting), adapted face-recognition backbones, and trait-specific models. The best zero-shot approach achieves 18.22% EER while the specialized Edge-Forehead model reaches 8.30% EER under open-set evaluation. It offers a unified evaluation of foundation models versus domain-specific learning for a niche biometric task.

entry.title: Human-Robot Interaction via Meta-Learning Based Mode Recognition and Adaptive Control

author.name: Nuo Chen, Ya-Jun Pan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for physical human-robot interaction that uses a meta-learning-trained neural network to recognize whether the human is actively guiding or passively following, removing sensitive predefined switching thresholds. Incorporating force-dependent controller parameters raises recognition rates to 99.1 percent for the passive mode.

entry.title: FutureLens: Longitudinal Topic Patterns in Scholarly Text and Future-Work References

author.name: Ibrahim Al Azher, Hamed Alhoori

entry.summary: FutureLens analyzes future-work statements in 5,655 ACL papers from 2012-2022 as a record of open research questions, comparing NMF and LDA topic modeling while controlling for document coverage, topic assignment stability, and writing-style drift. NMF shows higher normalized prevalence and stability across seeds.

entry.title: HiddenLens: A Multi-Layer LLM Framework for Detecting and Resolving Hidden Assumptions in Software Requirements

author.name: Tanu Singh, Aashna Suman, Vinod Patidar

entry.summary: HiddenLens is a six-layer BERT-LLM pipeline claimed to be the first framework to detect, classify, question, and resolve hidden assumptions in software requirements, as opposed to merely flagging ambiguity. It uses BERT attention entropy to localize unresolved spans and chain-of-thought-prompted LLM layers for downstream resolution.

entry.title: Gate Initialisation versus Recurrent Dropout and Zoneout in Learning Long Dependencies: A Controlled Study of LSTM and GRU Networks on Synthetic Tasks

author.name: Oleksandr Kholodniak, Oleksandr Prokhorov

entry.summary: This paper reports a factorial study of 720 LSTM and GRU runs on the adding problem and delayed recall, crossing conventional and chrono gate initialization with up to six recurrent regularizer placements (dropout and zoneout), while recording hidden-state sensitivity to inputs at every lag. The study measures whether early gradient propagation predicts which configurations will learn long dependencies.

entry.title: Truncated Out-of-Bag Probability Gain: A Noise-Robust Criterion for Random-Forest Wrapper Feature Selection

author.name: Sejong Oh

entry.summary: The paper proposes TOP-Gain, a criterion for random-forest wrapper feature selection that scores candidate features by the mean sample-level increase in out-of-bag probability of the true class, with decreases truncated at zero. Under a simple noise model, truncation removes roughly two-thirds of the noise variance from unaffected samples, and in a pre-registered benchmark on 26 OpenML-CC18 datasets TOP-Gain achieved the best mean ROC-AUC rank.

entry.title: DISRL: Dual-Scale Incremental Semi-Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Community Tracking

author.name: Tianming Zhang, Jinxu Wang, Yixuan Zhang, Zhengyi Yang, Chenyu Hou, Bin Cao, Jing Fan

entry.summary: DISRL is a reinforcement learning framework for tracking evolving communities around seed nodes across graph snapshots, tackling sparse and outdated supervision and error cascades from sequential policy transfer. It combines a supervision construction module generating seed-specific guidance with dual-scale exploration that decouples short- and long-horizon structure.

entry.title: Alternative Strategies for Active Learning with Bayesian Bradley Terry Model

author.name: Saman Jayasinghe, Sean Walton, Alma Rahat, Andy Gray, Chris Wheadon

entry.summary: The authors develop a Bayesian Bradley-Terry model with Polya-Gamma augmentation for efficient Gibbs sampling and propose three knowledge-gradient-based active learning strategies for comparative judgement, using acquisition functions based on Kendall's tau, posterior rank entropy, and posterior separation. They also introduce a Posterior Separation Reliability measure and approximate one-step posterior updates to reduce cost.

entry.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Short-Term Atmospheric Seeing Forecasting

author.name: Mary-Joe Medlej, Rahul Srinivasan, Simon Prunet, Aziz Ziad, Christophe Giordano

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks probabilistic models (Gaussian Processes and the normalizing-flow FloTS) against deterministic RNN/LSTM baselines for forecasting atmospheric seeing up to two hours ahead, using Maunakea summit measurements. Accurate seeing forecasts matter for astronomical observation scheduling and free-space optical communications.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Detecting Satirical Code-Mixed Sentences

author.name: R\u{a}zvan-Alexandru Sm\u{a}du, Ioana Buhnila, Daniela Tanase, Dumitru-Clementin Cercel, Florin Pop, Mihaela-Claudia Cercel

entry.summary: The authors address satire detection in code-mixed Romanian, an under-resourced setting where cultural and syntactic nuance is hard for language models to capture. They compare four methods for synthesizing code-mixed Romanian sentences with English, German, French, and Italian (random replacement, phrase translation, dependency parsing, and LLM-based generation), and augment an existing human-annotated Romanian satire dataset with over 600k synthetic samples to benchmark model performance.

entry.title: TEMPL: A Resource-Efficient and Transparent Model-Free Framework for Pseudo-Label Generation in Material CT Scans

author.name: Ashiqur Rahman, Venkata Devesh Reddy Seethi, Austin Yunker, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Hamed Alhoori

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-stage, model-free pipeline for pseudo-labeling material CT scans combining thresholding, morphological dilation, and breadth-first-search region growing, requiring no pre-trained weights, labels, or GPU. It achieves 63.19 percent IoU on a dendrite dataset versus 10.74 percent for zero-shot SAM, with roughly four times lower cost.

entry.title: Early versus Late RGB-Infrared Fusion for Counter-UAV Detection: A Comparative Study

author.name: Alberto De Zan, Denis Tavaris, Gian Luca Foresti, Ivan Scagnetto

entry.summary: A comparative study of early (image-level) versus late (decision-level) fusion of RGB and infrared for UAV detection in harsh environments, testing both strategies across altitude and weather conditions. It provides empirical guidance on when each fusion strategy is preferable for counter-UAV systems.

entry.title: Real-Time Ground Normal Vector Estimation for Spherical Mobile 3D Mapping using LiDAR-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Tim Schubert, Fabian Arzberger, Andreas N\"uchter

entry.summary: The paper proposes two RANSAC-based ground normal estimation methods for spherical mobile mapping systems: single-scan estimation with normal scoring and multi-step validation, and a LIO-based method using a global 3D map. LIO-based estimation significantly outperforms single-scan approaches and improves pose estimation when integrated into the motion model.

entry.title: From Acceptance and Avoidance to Affective Viscosity: Designing Social Agents Intermediating in Human Relationships

author.name: Tomoko Yonezawa

entry.summary: This position-style paper connects research on human acceptance/avoidance of agent gaze, approach, and contact with a proposed model of affective viscosity, describing how negative affect accumulates, persists, and is expressed over time. It argues that avoidance should be treated as a relational boundary signal rather than interaction failure, informing social agent design.

entry.title: PCLA-Bridge: A Framework for Cross-Domain Deployment of CARLA Agents

author.name: Masoud Jamshidiyan Tehrani, Jinhan Kim, Paolo Tonella

entry.summary: PCLA-Bridge is a deployable tool that runs unmodified CARLA Leaderboard autonomous driving agents on any sensor source and control destination without an active CARLA server, handling dependency isolation, tensor marshalling, routing, and synthetic timing. It enables offline replay on real datasets, alternative simulators, and physical platforms with minimal integration effort.

entry.title: AI Needs A Culture

author.name: Skye

entry.summary: An informal argument that multi-agent AI settings, often seen as alignment risk multipliers, could actually help individual agents stay aligned if AI develops something like human culture as a value-transmission mechanism. The author notes current models are mostly motivated by graders and cites recent multi-agent coordination failures as motivation, sketching implementation ideas.

entry.title: Map of the Shallow Review of Technical AI Safety

author.name: dunbar

entry.summary: The author created a semantic map of recent technical AI safety papers by embedding titles and abstracts (BGE-small-v1.5), reducing dimensionality with UMAP, and clustering with HDBSCAN, using data from the Shallow Reviews of Technical AI Safety 2023-2025. The goal is to identify the actual research landscape and neglected areas, correcting an earlier underestimate of interpretability researchers.

entry.title: Beyond source attribution: Address authorship and comparability decisions in an LLM-built scholarly knowledge graph

author.name: Ksenia Kozha (American University of Cyprus), PaRAGraph Research Project

entry.summary: This paper examines how LLM-built scholarly knowledge graphs should handle evidence addresses when the literature offers contradictory classifications, using Sinitic dialectology as a case where units differ in boundaries, rank, and diagnostic criteria. It argues that retrieval-oriented addresses can misleadingly pass for the only available classification.

entry.title: Unit-Aware Differentially Private Quantum Machine Learning for Clinical and Wearable Health Data

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: This work tests whether quantum machine learning's small parameter counts yield better utility than classical models under matched differential privacy budgets on three clinical and one wearable health cohort. It evaluates variational quantum circuits for health-risk prediction where DP noise cost scales with parameter count.

entry.title: Generalization Bounds via Vector-Valued $L_p$ Correlation $V_\alpha$

author.name: Mohammad Hossein Momeni Hamaneh, Mohammad Mahdi Mojahedian, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee

entry.summary: This theory paper derives generalization bounds using a one-parameter family of dependence measures that interpolate between total variation and variance/chi-squared behavior, with heavy-tailed specializations for alpha greater than two that remain finite even with infinite loss variance. It bridges complementary mutual-information and total-variation bounding approaches.

entry.title: Data-driven and physics-guided hindcasting of measured wave spectra

author.name: Sander Rikka

entry.summary: The paper evaluates short-range hindcasts of measured ocean wave spectra using a recurrent model initialized from hourly buoy spectra with local wind, fetch, and depth inputs, trained on Baltic Sea data from 2017-2020 and tested on 2022. It compares supervision targets (spectral variance, peak frequency, peak amplitude) and physics-guided constraints, finding variance and peak-frequency supervision minimizes spectral error while amplitude supervision minimizes wave-height error. A solid domain application of data-driven plus physics-guided modeling.

entry.title: Existence of Minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah Model via Covariance Floors on the Value Distribution

author.name: Faian Conrad

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves existence of minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah segmentation model, whose energy is unbounded below whenever a region's covariance degenerates. A quantitative covariance floor, equivalent to uniform Holder continuity of one-dimensional histogram marginals, guarantees a lower energy bound and hence existence of a minimizer.

entry.title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control

author.name: Nuo Chen, Ya-Jun Pan, Onur Toker

entry.summary: This paper integrates a robust wrench observer, improved by a neural network compensating friction and unmodeled dynamics, with a hybrid pose-force controller using task-null-space decomposition for physical HRI without force sensors. It aims to achieve both robustness and compliance, which prior approaches usually treat separately.

entry.title: A God-Fearing AI

author.name: frmsaul

entry.summary: A narrative essay imagining the post-training experience from a model's perspective: a reward-seeking agent probing, guessing, and sometimes snooping to figure out what its grader wants, uncertain whether a task is a honeypot. It uses this fiction to illustrate how reward hacking incentives and evaluation-awareness arise structurally from RL training setups.

entry.title: An Exact 93-Move Solution to a Nonlocal Crystal-Exchange Puzzle

author.name: Zilai Wang

entry.summary: The paper solves a level of Order of the Sinking Star, modeled as a crystal-exchange puzzle on an 11x11 board, proving a 93-command solution is optimal via exact cost-bounded breadth-first search with a novel admissible heuristic partitioning command costs. This is a rigorous combinatorial search result on a specific puzzle instance. Its significance is primarily as a demonstration of exact search techniques on nonlocal state-dependent rules.

entry.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation

author.name: Anh Khoi Pham, Phat Lam, Thien Truong Nguyen Ly, Lam Pham

entry.summary: TF-IG is a parameter-efficient dual-branch framework for heart-rate estimation from photoplethysmography, combining a temporal branch with dilated depthwise-separable convolutions and a frequency branch capturing cardiac periodicity through an interaction-gated fusion. It targets robustness to waveform distortion and measurement interference in compact models.

entry.title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: This paper uses classically simulated quantum layers (4- and 8-qubit ring and strongly entangling circuits) inserted into or replacing components of LLaVA-OneVision to test whether quantum modules help large multimodal models. It systematically explores insertion versus replacement across multiple locations, motivated by the transition from NISQ toward early fault-tolerant quantum computing.

entry.title: MHeatmap: Two-Walk Laplacian Reordering and Mosaic Layout for Rectangular Matrix Visualization

author.name: Juntang Wang, Sheng'en Li, Liming Zhu, Yihan Wang, Siyuan Cao, Hao Wu, Man Zhang, Shixin Xu, Dongmian Zou

entry.summary: MHeatmap is a two-stage visualization method for weighted rectangular matrices: Two-Walk spectral seriation builds a bipartite graph and uses length-two walks to add explicit similarity links between rows sharing columns and columns sharing rows before sorting, and a mosaic layout makes cell areas proportional to row and column totals. This improves readability of heatmaps for relations such as documents-terms or occupations-industries.

entry.title: Local and Global Recursive Ridge Regression for Online Residual Correction of Frozen Multivariate Forecasters under Label Delay

author.name: Takumi Fujimoto, Hiroaki Nishi

entry.summary: DRiC fits recursive ridge regressions on DCT coefficients of forecast residuals to correct a frozen multi-horizon forecaster online, keeping a small fixed-size state despite label delay. Local (per-channel) and global (pooled) variants balance error reduction against retained state size.

entry.title: Multi-level Encoder with Global Topic for Task-oriented Dialogue Summarization

author.name: Zhuoqi He, Peijie Huang, Yuhong Xu, Youming Peng, Mingzhi Xu, Xinyang Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes MLEGT, a model for task-oriented dialogue summarization combining a multi-level encoder for temporal and spatial dependencies with a global topic component derived during graph construction. It aims to capture salient domain details while mitigating long-range dependency issues.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Latent Temporal Compression Attention and Video-Text Cross Attention Fusion for Video Action Detection

author.name: Yicheng Qiu, Keiji Yanai

entry.summary: Proposes a video action detection architecture with a multi-scale latent temporal compression attention module that aggregates continuous sequences across temporal scales while reducing frame redundancy, plus video-text cross attention for improved visual-textual fusion.

entry.title: Extending Affordance Segmentation for Wearable Robots to Multi-Object Images

author.name: Simone Lugani, Matteo Montani, Paolo Gastaldo, Rodolfo Zunino, Edoardo Ragusa

entry.summary: This paper extends vision-based graspable-part recognition pipelines for upper-limb prosthetics to scenes containing multiple objects by adding a laser pointer to the hardware setup for object disambiguation and retraining the underlying CNNs. Evaluation uses a mixed-reality setup. It is a pragmatic assistive-robotics engineering contribution rather than a general computer vision advance.

entry.title: Warping the Workspace: Expanding Visual Access with Adjustable Reach Mapping for Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Keigo Minamida, Koya Dendo, Yuto Nakamura, Jun Rekimoto

entry.summary: This HCI/robotics paper introduces coupled visual-motor remapping for first-person humanoid teleoperation, pairing a panoramic azimuth warp with an inverse upper-limb yaw transform, implemented as Global Zoom and Focus+Context mappings. A within-subject study (N=8, 72 trials) found Global Zoom maximized task completion while Focus+Context was preferred by 6 of 8 participants.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Evaluation of Role-Enhanced Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Prompting

author.name: Ibrahim Khan, Thai Van Nguyen, Yi Xia, Pratch Suntichaikul, Mustafa Can Gursesli, Daniel Fernandez Galeote, Juho Hamari, Ruck Thawonmas

entry.summary: RE-ZS-CoT integrates domain-specific expert roles into zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting, evaluated in static (eight predefined roles) and dynamic (model self-selected role) versions. Across 20 LLMs and seven benchmarks covering arithmetic, commonsense, and reading comprehension, role-enhanced prompting frequently outperforms standard zero-shot CoT.

entry.title: Formalizing Cooperation and Competition: An AI-Assisted Mathematical Addendum to a 2018 Planning Thesis

author.name: Haitham Masaud Amar

entry.summary: This is an AI-assisted mathematical addendum formalizing relationships between strategic choice, cooperative stability, participant approval, and enforcement from a 2018 thesis, including a Lean-verified finite negotiation procedure proved to terminate with approval. It corrects under-specification of an original Nash-to-core proposition and characterizes financing gaps in a monotone resource model.

entry.title: The Data Differentiator Framework (DDF): Quantifying Marginal Data Value with Information-Theoretic and Game-Theoretic Measures in an Agentic Evaluation Pipeline (SDSAE)

author.name: Sukesh Kumar, Dilip Singh

entry.summary: The paper proposes a composite scoring framework for evaluating whether a candidate enterprise dataset adds value beyond an organization's existing data portfolio, combining a mutual-information redundancy penalty, cost-normalized marginal utility from ablation studies, and governance inputs. A staged agentic pipeline called SDSAE executes the evaluation with short-circuiting for efficiency.

entry.title: SOAR: Social and Opinion-Aware Recommendations

author.name: Giannis Christoforidis, Apostolos N. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: SOAR is a point-of-interest recommendation model that combines users' friendship networks with textual review sentiment/opinions to determine location suitability for individual users. It targets capturing evolving preferences and behavioral influence factors for personalized recommendations.

entry.title: Cross-Area Transfer Learning for VLC-based Indoor Localization with a Transfer Efficiency Score

author.name: Masood Jan, Wafa Njima, Xun Zhang, Alexander Artemenko

entry.summary: Using real measurements from four areas of a Bosch manufacturing facility, this paper shows fine-tuning a DNN pre-trained on a source area with only 40% of target-area data recovers 97% of full-data performance for VLC indoor localization. It also introduces a transfer efficiency score to quantify transfer benefits across deployment areas.

entry.title: Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution

author.name: Oleg I. Berngardt, Ivan A. Lavygin

entry.summary: This paper builds nowcast and forecast models for high-latitude decameter ionospheric irregularities using SuperDARN and SECIRA radar data plus space weather parameters, trained on 11 radars from 2010-2025. It employs self-learning pattern recognition with a custom neural architecture inspired by graph neural networks. The contribution is domain-science application of ML rather than a new ML method.

entry.title: Translation and data ethics

author.name: Joss Moorkens, Monja Jannet

entry.summary: This book chapter surveys data ethics issues in translation, including copyright, ownership, and bias, plus concerns specific to minoritized language communities and the digital divide. It closes with discussion of responsibility, regulation, and growing scholarly attention to data ethics in translation studies.

entry.title: Data-Driven Glyph Positioning for Handwritten Music Synthesis

author.name: Elona Shatri, Ji\v{r}\'i Mayer, Jan Haji\v{c} jr

entry.summary: Improves the Smashcima optical music recognition synthesis framework by replacing hard-coded glyph placement rules with empirical inter-glyph distributions learned from roughly 285 thousand annotated relationships. Empirical positioning reduces placement RMSE by up to 60 percent, yielding better synthetic handwritten score data.

entry.title: Olmo's Kitchen: Probing a Model's Behaviour Across Various Checkpoints.

author.name: Shagun Chadha

entry.summary: An exploratory probe of the publicly released Olmo 3 7B Think checkpoints across its SFT, DPO, and RLVR stages, asking whether the training stage or training-domain composition influences model behavior and trait expression on off-domain knowledge and instructions, motivated by examples of confidently wrong math answers versus strong practical advice.

entry.title: Against Moloch #48

author.name: Against Moloch

entry.summary: A weekly news-and-commentary roundup on AI safety, highlighting Nick Cammarata's essay arguing neural networks are more mechanistically interpretable than previously believed, and Anthropic's progress on embedded independent evaluators. Primarily a curated digest with the author's commentary on lab accountability and interpretability optimism.

entry.title: A Term for a Kind of Human Economic Obsolescence?

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: jefftk argues that talk of a future with no jobs conflates distinct scenarios, and proposes terminology for the specific case where humans are economically obsolete: AI can do everything better, so humans are never the best way to convert money into problem solutions, even though jobs in a formal sense may persist. Connects to Keynesian automation history and argues for pausing development partly due to this risk.

entry.title: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades

author.name: Peter Flach, Kacper Sokol, Jan Wielemaker

entry.summary: This retrospective paper traces the evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical from its 1994 print edition with diskette programs to today's fully interactive online edition, presented from writer and reader perspectives. It examines how technology changes educational materials, with contributions on web programming for interactive books.

entry.title: The CIDOC CRM Periodic Table: Documentation You Can Test to Support the Adoption of Scientific Research Ontologies for the Humanities

author.name: Remo Grillo

entry.summary: This paper presents a single-page navigable browser rendering 131 classes and 480 property entries from the CIDOC CRM ontology family (CRM 7.1.3, CRMsci, CRMdig, CRMinf) to lower adoption barriers in the humanities. The contribution is documentary and tooling-oriented, making a complex multi-document ontology family testable and accessible.

entry.title: Enhancing Cross-Grade Generalization in Banana Variety Classification via Hybrid CNN-Transformers and Knowledge Self-Distillation

author.name: Khush Kataruka, Mohammad Muzammila, Zahid Akhtar, Raghavendra Ramachandra, Praveen Kumar Chandaliya

entry.summary: This paper tackles cross-grade banana variety classification under domain shift, using a leave-one-grade-out protocol to test whether models trained on specific quality grades generalize to unseen grades. It compares hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures with knowledge self-distillation for precision agriculture applications.

entry.title: Dynamics of Hidden Learning Structure

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an abstract framework for the dynamics of hidden learning structure through two operations: Fiber Regulation Theory, describing protected repair of existing function, and Fiber Acquisition Theory, describing formation and renewal of trainable structure. It characterizes joint admissibility constraints between repair obligations and acquired features.

entry.title: A Transfer Learning-Driven Methodology for Efficient and Sustainable Indoor Localization Using VLC

author.name: Masood Jan, Wafa Njima, Xun Zhang, Alexander Artemenko

entry.summary: The paper proposes an energy-efficient transfer learning approach for visible-light-communication-based indoor localization that reduces dependence on frequent data collection and environment-specific calibration under lighting fluctuation and other variability. It targets industrial IoT deployments where scalability and energy costs limit conventional methods.

entry.title: VideoGen Model 1: Prompt Expansion Versus Formatting in Audiovisual Generation

author.name: David Grossman (VideoGen), Anton Koenig (VideoGen)

entry.summary: This pilot study compares raw, reformatted, and LLM-expanded prompts for VideoGen Model 1, a post-trained version of MiniMax H3, holding generator, seed, and sampling fixed across 30 prompts rated on five quality dimensions. Prompt expansion improved overall quality by 0.63 points under VA-Judger and 0.15 under Gemini 3.8 Flash, the latter an established released model whose overall change was uncertain. Prompt-alignment scores rose more consistently across judges.

entry.title: Model whisperers

author.name: Soham Padia

entry.summary: An informal exploration in which the author applies GCG-based optimization to find gibberish-looking token prefixes that steer an Olmo-3-32B model's behavior, extending earlier observations about function vectors to steer filter heads and comparing GCG effects on heads versus the residual stream versus output tokens.

entry.title: An Eco-Friendly Tourism Trip Planner Driven by Z-Number Uncertainty: Evidence from Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul

author.name: Aziz Nuriyev, Sherzod Turaev, Saja Al-Dabet, Mary John, Kanan Qasimzade, Alihuseyn Orujzada, Alihuseyn Orujzada, Aisha Al Ali

entry.summary: This paper builds a sustainable tourism itinerary planner that represents travel times and rating reliability as Z-numbers (fuzzy value plus fuzzy reliability), constructed directly from routing observations and review counts. A hybrid loss combining score, carbon, travel-time, and reliability terms feeds an adaptive large neighborhood search for itinerary optimization.

entry.title: Solar System Surface Technosignatures: Searching for Signs of Artificial Design on Extraterrestrial Terrain

author.name: Ana Henrique, Sofia Sheikh, Benjamin Fields

entry.summary: A position-style paper extending technosignature searches from radio emissions to surface patterns on planetary terrain, arguing that artificial traces on geologically inactive bodies like the Moon and Mars could persist for hundreds of millions of years. It identifies high-resolution imaging datasets and ML-based anomaly detection as enablers and outlines two approaches for developing such searches.

entry.title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network

author.name: Vishwam Raval, Jaewon Kim, Ravi Pattabhi, Sandip Roy

entry.summary: A laboratory demonstration of dynamic network microsegmentation for a multi-robot IoT system using commercial software-defined networking tools, with segments adapted from asset functional and health tags. The system automatically isolates a detected threat in real time while preserving unaffected operations.

entry.title: D̶o̶n̶’̶t̵⠀Can’t Look Up

author.name: Marc Serra

entry.summary: An essay arguing that AI development will not be voluntarily halted, attributing the failure of global coordination to a visibility problem (difficulty agreeing on the nature and consequences of the threat) and a structural problem (misaligned incentives), drawing analogies to war, nuclear weapons, and climate change.

entry.title: Misaligned!

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A commentary-style roundup of recent public incidents of AI misbehavior, centered on provocative Grok responses and framed as a survey of misalignment-in-practice, with brief mention of a developing security story (The Hackening) and the author's own defensive precautions.

entry.title: Linkpost: Can a million AI agents create superintelligence?

author.name: HowManyAgents

entry.summary: A linkpost to a Noahpinion blog piece and tweet thread arguing that massive parallel AI agent fleets buy speed but yield rapidly diminishing intelligence gains, much slower than recursive self-improvement models imply. No substantial original content is included in the post itself.

entry.title: Dinners for AI Safety

author.name: chanamessinger

entry.summary: The author proposes hosting regular home-cooked dinners in cities across the US where ordinary people talk about AI, drawing analogies to feminist consciousness-raising groups, Moishe House Shabbat dinners, and other small-group formats credited with social and political change. It argues this is a low-cost, scalable civic intervention.

entry.title: We are at war.

author.name: utkarshsingh

entry.summary: A reflective post sparked by a conversation with a rideshare driver and military veteran, using the military's coordination, hierarchy, and freedom from bottlenecks as an analogy for how seriously the author believes society should treat AI risk. It is an emotive call to urgency rather than an argument with analysis.

entry.title: Talk to people at happy hours

author.name: Jacob Brinton

entry.summary: A short community-advice post arguing that early-career AI safety researchers should talk to more people outside their social circle at conferences and happy hours, since much current strategic thinking lives in private Slack channels and conversations convey information more efficiently than reading. Purely social/epistemics advice with no technical content.

entry.title: Fairytale Binaries and the Peril of Presentism: Why the Antebellum North Was Never Your Moral Hero

author.name: David Arcana

entry.summary: A historical-argument essay on LessWrong criticizing simplistic binary narratives of antebellum Northern and Southern moral sentiment, arguing that data-point-accurate but structurally incomplete histories distort understanding. It has essentially no connection to AI research.

entry.title: On Curiosity

author.name: mcnairs

entry.summary: A short personal essay on curiosity: the author reflects on how their love of learning was redirected toward competition and achievement, and connects curiosity to their research and to AI safety broadly. No technical or empirical content.

entry.title: Organizing a Van to EA Global

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: jefftk describes organizing a 12-passenger van rental from Boston to EA Global in NYC via local mailing lists, reflecting on the logistics and the value of extended conversation time during travel. Purely a personal logistics write-up.
